definition_zh: 渔业；渔场；渔业资源；捕捞与养殖产业；内陆渔业；渔业管理
definition_en: the industries and systems that catch, manage and sometimes farm fish and other aquatic organisms
core_image: 港口里渔船并排靠岸，冰面上摊着不同大小的鱼，拍卖牌不停翻动
scene: 天还没亮，港口已经挤满渔船，拍卖员举着牌子喊出第一筐鱼的价格。 Fisheries across the region agreed to a shared catch limit.
sceneCN: 这里指「捕捞与管理水产品的产业体系」（第 1 个义项：以捕获、养殖与经营鱼类及其他水生物为业的行业整体）；句意为本区域各渔业同意接受一个共享的捕捞上限。场景物件：渔船、鱼筐、冰面、拍卖牌。

pos.zh: 渔业；渔场（fishery 的复数，常作集合名词）

derivatives.zh: 渔业；渔场
鱼；捕鱼
渔民；渔船
捕鱼；渔业
渔民

senses.title: The industry as a whole
senses.definition: the industries and systems that catch, manage and sometimes farm fish and other aquatic organisms
senses.definitionCN: 以捕获、管理并有时养殖鱼类及其他水生物为业的产业与体系
senses.example: Fisheries across the region agreed to a shared catch limit.
senses.exampleCN: 本区域各渔业同意接受一个共享的捕捞上限。
senses.why: The plural of fishery can name the whole sector, not just several fishing grounds, because the industry is made of many units.
senses.whyCN: fishery 的复数可指整个行业，而不只是几处渔场，因为产业由许多单元组成。

senses.title: Fishing grounds
senses.definition: the places where commercial fishing takes place
senses.definitionCN: 商业捕捞实际进行的海域或水域
senses.example: The northern fisheries closed after the stock fell.
senses.exampleCN: 资源下降后，北方各渔场关闭了。
senses.why: A fishery is first a place on the water, so the plural can simply mean several grounds.
senses.whyCN: fishery 首先是水面上的一个地点，因此复数可以只指几处渔场。

senses.title: Fleets and operations
senses.definition: the boats, gear and crews that work a stock
senses.definitionCN: 作业于某一资源的船只、渔具与船员
senses.example: Artisanal fisheries use smaller boats than industrial ones.
senses.exampleCN: 手工渔业使用的船比工业渔业小。
senses.why: Management counts capacity, so the word can mean the operating units rather than the fish or the place.
senses.whyCN: 管理要统计产能，因此这个词也可指作业单元，而不是鱼或地点。

senses.title: Fish stocks
senses.definition: the populations of fish that a fishery harvests
senses.definitionCN: 渔业所收获的鱼类种群
senses.example: Shared fisheries require joint stock assessments.
senses.exampleCN: 共享渔业需要联合的资源评估。
senses.why: A fishery is also shorthand for the stock it depends on, because management is written about the two together.
senses.whyCN: fishery 也常简称它所依赖的资源，因为管理文本把两者写在一起。

senses.title: The sector including aquaculture
senses.definition: the wider food sector that includes capture fisheries and fish farming
senses.definitionCN: 包含捕捞渔业与鱼类养殖的更宽食品行业
senses.example: Global fisheries now produce more farmed than wild fish.
senses.exampleCN: 全球渔业如今生产的养殖鱼多于野生鱼。
senses.why: Statistical agencies group capture and culture under one heading, so the plural widened to cover both.
senses.whyCN: 统计机构把捕捞与养殖归在同一标题下，因此复数扩展到两者。

senses.title: Inland fisheries
senses.definition: fisheries in rivers, lakes and reservoirs rather than the sea
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊与水库而非海中的渔业
senses.example: Inland fisheries feed millions of people.
senses.exampleCN: 内陆渔业养活了数百万人。
senses.why: The same activity happens in fresh water, so the plural needed a modifier rather than a new word.
senses.whyCN: 同一活动也发生在淡水中，因此复数只需加修饰语，而不必另造新词。

senses.title: Management and science
senses.definition: the agencies, rules and assessments that regulate fishing
senses.definitionCN: 规范捕捞的机构、规则与评估
senses.example: Fisheries science sets the limit, and fisheries policy enforces it.
senses.exampleCN: 渔业科学设定上限，渔业政策负责执行。
senses.why: Because the word appears constantly in regulation, it can stand for the management system itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词不断出现在法规中，它可以指管理体系本身。

senses.title: Access rights and jurisdiction
senses.definition: the legal rights to fish a stock or in a zone
senses.definitionCN: 在某资源或某区域捕鱼的法定权利
senses.example: The two states share fisheries in the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 两国共享海峡内的渔业权。
senses.why: Law treats the right to fish as a kind of property, so the plural can name those rights.
senses.whyCN: 法律把捕鱼权当作一种财产，因此复数可以指这些权利。

intro.en: Fisheries is the plural of fishery, formed from native fish plus the place-and-practice suffix -ery, which came through French from Latin -aria. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fisheries 是 fishery 的复数，由本族词 fish 加表示地点与行业的后缀 -ery 构成，后者经法语来自拉丁 -aria。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fisc 'fish' descends from Germanic *fiskaz, a reconstructed form related to Latin piscis.
items.cn: fisc「鱼」出自日耳曼语 *fiskaz，此为重构形式，与拉丁 piscis 同源。

items.en: The suffix -ery came through Old French -erie from Latin -aria, naming a place where something is done or a collective practice.
items.cn: 后缀 -ery 经古法语 -erie 来自拉丁 -aria，命名做事的地点或集合性的行业。

items.en: Fishery first named a place for catching fish, then the business carried on there.
items.cn: fishery 最初指捕鱼的地点，随后指在那里进行的生意。

items.en: The plural fisheries widened from several grounds to the whole industry and its management systems.
items.cn: 复数 fisheries 从几处渔场扩展到整个产业及其管理体系。

items.en: Twentieth-century statistics extended fisheries to include aquaculture and inland capture, making it a sector term.
items.cn: 二十世纪统计把水产养殖与内陆捕捞纳入 fisheries，使其成为行业术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic source of *fiskaz is not settled, and the first use of fisheries as a sector term is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*fiskaz 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论，fisheries 作为行业术语的最早使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds singular, plural and personal forms of the same fish family; group two holds neighbouring food-sector and management terms.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 fish 词族的单数、复数与人物形式；第二组是邻近的食品行业与管理术语。

entries.definition: One ground, stock or business; fisheries can mean several of them or the whole sector.
entries.definitionCN: 一处渔场、一份资源或一家企业；fisheries 可指数个，也可指整个行业。

entries.definition: A person who fishes or a fishing vessel; it is an agent, not the industry.
entries.definitionCN: 捕鱼的人或渔船；它是施事者，不是行业。

entries.definition: The act or sport of catching fish; fisheries is the organized industry and its management.
entries.definitionCN: 捕鱼的行为或运动；fisheries 是有组织的产业及其管理。

entries.definition: The animal itself; the plural fisheries names the human system built around catching it.
entries.definitionCN: 动物本身；fisheries 指围绕捕捉它建立的人类体系。

entries.definition: The farming of aquatic organisms; it is included in the broad sector but is not capture fishing.
entries.definitionCN: 水生物的养殖；它被纳入宽口径行业，但不是捕捞。

entries.definition: A population of fish treated as a harvestable unit; fisheries depend on stocks but are not the stocks.
entries.definitionCN: 被当作可收获取单元的鱼类种群；渔业依赖资源，但不等同于资源。

entries.definition: The fish actually taken; it is the output of a fishery, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 实际捕到的鱼；它是渔业的产出，不是体系本身。

entries.definition: The rules and assessments that regulate fishing; it is one part of fisheries, not the whole sector.
entries.definitionCN: 规范捕捞的规则与评估；它是渔业的一部分，不是整个行业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffix history, real sector categories and real management collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀历史、真实行业类别与真实管理搭配。

normal.en: Fish plus -ery makes fishery, a place and practice of catching fish.
normal.cn: fish 加 -ery 构成 fishery，即捕鱼的地点与行业。

normal.en: Fisheries is simply the plural, but it often names the whole sector.
normal.cn: fisheries 只是复数，却常指整个行业。

normal.en: Marine and inland are the two great divisions.
normal.cn: 海洋与内陆是两大分区。

normal.en: Fisheries science sets limits; fisheries policy enforces them.
normal.cn: 渔业科学设上限，渔业政策执行上限。

normal.en: The broad sector now includes aquaculture as well as capture.
normal.cn: 宽口径行业如今既含捕捞也含养殖。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour before dawn, every boat carrying a share of one shared stock.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明前的港口，每条船都载着同一份共享资源的一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where catches, limits and licenses are written on the same page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，渔获、上限与许可证写在同一页。

abstract.en: Picture a single fish counted by a scientist, a boat and a treaty at once.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条鱼同时被科学家、渔船与条约计算。

examples.en: Small-scale fisheries employ most of the region's coastal workers.
examples.cn: 小规模渔业雇用了该区域大部分沿海劳动者。

examples.en: Fisheries and conservation groups negotiated the closed season.
examples.cn: 渔业与保护团体谈判确定了禁渔期。

examples.en: Inland fisheries collapsed after the dam blocked the migration.
examples.cn: 水坝阻断洄游后，内陆渔业崩溃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fish（鱼）+ -ery（行业/场所）+ 复数」——捕鱼的行业与渔场 → 渔业

root: fish 出自古英语 fisc，属日耳曼语 *fiskaz（重构形式），与拉丁 piscis 同源；后缀 -ery 经古法语 -erie 来自拉丁 -aria，表示地点或行业；fishery 加复数 -ies 成 fisheries，现代常指整个渔业部门。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one industry: the sector, the grounds, the fleets, the stocks, the wider scope, inland fisheries, management and access rights.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一行业展开：产业、渔场、船队、资源、宽口径、内陆渔业、管理与渔业权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a harbour at dawn, boats side by side, iced fish on the quay and an auction board turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时的港口，渔船并排，码头冰面上摊着鱼，拍卖牌不停翻动。

branches.en: SECTOR TO PLACE: an industry is also a set of named grounds on the water.
branches.cn: 从行业到地点：一个产业同时也是一片片具名水域。

branches.en: GEAR TO RESOURCE: boats and gear exist only because there is a stock to harvest.
branches.cn: 从渔具到资源：船与网存在，只因为有可收获取的资源。

branches.en: THE INLAND WATERS: the same harvest logic applies in rivers and lakes.
branches.cn: 内陆水域：同一套收获逻辑也适用于河流与湖泊。

branches.en: THE WIDER SECTOR: once aquaculture is counted, one word covers both.
branches.cn: 行业口径：一旦算入养殖，一个词就覆盖两者。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT TO RIGHTS: rules decide who may fish, and those permissions become property.
branches.cn: 从管理到权利：规则决定谁能捕鱼，这些许可随后成为财产。

intro.en: Fisheries is a plural noun whose base fishery is a transparent native root plus a borrowed suffix; the plural adds no new meaning beyond number.
intro.cn: fisheries 是复数名词，其基础 fishery 由本族词根加借入后缀透明构成；复数除数量外不添加新义。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -ery reaches Latin -aria through French, while fish itself is Germanic; only piscis is a distant Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -ery 经法语上溯拉丁 -aria，而 fish 本身属日耳曼语；只有 piscis 是拉丁远亲。

items.example: The fish return to the river each year.
items.exampleCN: 鱼每年回到这条河。

items.example: The suffix builds words like bakery and fishery.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 bakery 与 fishery 一类词。

items.example: The fishery reopened after recovery.
items.exampleCN: 资源恢复后渔场重新开放。

items.example: Fisheries depend on healthy stocks.
items.exampleCN: 渔业依赖健康的资源。

items.example: The fisher mended the net at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔民在黎明修补渔网。

items.example: The fisherman knew the tide by memory.
items.exampleCN: 这位渔民凭记忆就知道潮汐。

items.example: Fishing is restricted in spring.
items.exampleCN: 春季捕鱼受限。

items.example: Fisheries management uses stock assessments.
items.exampleCN: 渔业管理使用资源评估。

items.example: Aquaculture now exceeds capture in some markets.
items.exampleCN: 在某些市场，养殖已超过捕捞。

items.meaning: the scientific estimate of a fish population
items.example: The stock assessment set the catch limit.
items.exampleCN: 资源评估设定了捕捞上限。

definition_zh: 污染物；沾染物；使某物变得不纯或不宜使用的物质
definition_en: a substance that makes something impure, unsafe or unfit for its intended use by being present in it
core_image: 取样瓶里浮着一层薄薄的油膜，原本清澈的水面被这一点外来物搅得不再可信
scene: 检测员在水厂的取样瓶里发现一层薄薄的油膜，仪器读数随即报警。 A single contaminant in the sample pushed the reading past the safety limit.
sceneCN: 这里 contaminant 指「混入某物、使其不纯或不宜使用的物质」（第 1 个义项：外来的沾染物使整体失去纯净）；句意为样本中一种污染物就把读数推过了安全限值。图中可辨识物件：取样瓶、油膜、检测仪、报警灯。

pos.zh: 污染物；沾染物（可数，指一种具体的污染物质）

derivatives.zh: 污染；使沾染
污染；沾染
受污染的；沾染的
去污；消除污染
造成污染的

senses.title: A substance that makes something impure
senses.titleCN: 使某物变得不纯的外来物质
senses.definition: any substance whose presence spoils the purity or quality of a material, medium or product
senses.definitionCN: 任何因其存在而破坏材料、介质或产品纯度与品质的物质
senses.example: A single contaminant in the sample pushed the reading past the safety limit.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中一种污染物就把读数推过了安全限值。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'to touch together', so a contaminant is literally something that has touched a clean body and left itself behind in it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「接触在一起」，因此 contaminant 字面上就是「碰过洁净之物并在其中留下自己的东西」。

senses.title: A pollutant in air, water or soil
senses.titleCN: 空气、水体或土壤中的污染物质
senses.definition: a substance present in an environmental medium at a level that harms organisms or uses
senses.definitionCN: 存在于环境介质中、其含量足以危害生物或用途的物质
senses.example: The aquifer held a solvent contaminant from the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 含水层里存着老工厂留下的一种溶剂污染物。
senses.why: Environmental science adopted the word because it names the thing rather than the harm, which is measured separately.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学采用这个词，因为它命名的是物质本身，而危害另有指标衡量。

senses.title: A biological contaminant such as a microbe
senses.titleCN: 微生物等生物性沾染物
senses.definition: a bacterium, virus, fungus or other organism that makes a product or surface unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 使产品或表面变得不安全的细菌、病毒、真菌或其他生物
senses.example: A bacterial contaminant closed the production line for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一种细菌污染物让生产线停了一周。
senses.why: Living things contaminate as effectively as chemicals, and laboratories needed one word that covers both.
senses.whyCN: 活物与化学品一样能造成沾染，实验室需要一个词同时涵盖两者。

senses.title: A trace residue of chemicals
senses.definition: a pesticide, drug, heavy metal or solvent left at very low concentration in food, water or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 以极低浓度残留在食品、水或组织中的农药、药物、重金属或溶剂
senses.example: Regulators set a limit for each pesticide contaminant.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构为每种农药残留设定了限值。
senses.why: Modern instruments can find a few parts per billion, so the word now covers amounts far too small to see.
senses.whyCN: 现代仪器能检出十亿分之几，这个词于是涵盖了肉眼完全看不见的量。

senses.title: Foreign matter in food or medicine
senses.titleCN: 食品与药品中的外来异物
senses.definition: glass, metal, plastic or other matter that enters a product during handling and makes it unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 在加工过程中进入产品、使其不安全的玻璃、金属、塑料或其他物质
senses.example: A metal contaminant triggered the recall of the batch.
senses.exampleCN: 一种金属污染物触发了这批产品的召回。
senses.why: For manufacturers the word covers anything that should not be in the package, living or not.
senses.whyCN: 对制造商而言，这个词涵盖一切不该出现在包装里的东西，无论是否有生命。

senses.title: A radioactive contaminant
senses.definition: a radionuclide deposited on a surface, in soil or in a body where it does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 沉积在不该出现的表面、土壤或人体内的放射性核素
senses.example: Workers mapped the radioactive contaminant around the old reactor.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员标出了旧反应堆周围的放射性污染物。
senses.why: Radiation is invisible and persistent, so the word stresses location and unwanted presence rather than visible dirt.
senses.whyCN: 辐射看不见又持久，这个词于是强调位置与「不该在此」，而非看得见的脏污。

senses.title: A particle in a cleanroom or vacuum
senses.titleCN: 洁净室或真空中的微粒沾染物
senses.definition: a dust particle, fibre or molecular film that ruins a wafer, lens or vacuum process
senses.definitionCN: 使晶圆、镜片或真空工艺失效的尘粒、纤维或分子膜
senses.example: A sub-micron contaminant ruined the coating on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒亚微米级污染物毁掉了镜片镀膜。
senses.why: In manufacturing the threshold is not health but function: a particle too small to see can still break a circuit.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，门槛不是健康而是功能：小到看不见的颗粒仍能毁掉电路。

senses.title: Abstract: anything that corrupts a clean system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何使洁净系统失真的东西
senses.definition: a transferred use for an element that corrupts the purity of data, language or a process
senses.definitionCN: 转指使数据、语言或流程丧失纯净性的因素
senses.example: A stale record is a contaminant in the training set.
senses.exampleCN: 过时记录是训练集里的一种污染。
senses.why: The metaphor works because the physical image is general: a small foreign thing enters a clean body and changes what the body can be used for.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为物理意象很通用：一小点外来物进入洁净的整体，改变了这个整体还能做什么。

intro.en: Contaminant is the noun use of the present participle of contaminate, which came to English from Latin by way of French. The root image is touching. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: contaminant 是 contaminate 现在分词的名词化用法，而 contaminate 经法语来自拉丁语。其词根意象是「接触」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tangere meant 'to touch'. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European root often proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触摸」。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧词根是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus the touch root produced contamen 'contact, pollution', the idea of one thing being defiled by touching another.
items.cn: com-「共同」加「触摸」词根构成 contamen「接触、污染」，即一物因碰到另一物而被弄脏。

items.en: Contaminare meant 'to defile by contact, to corrupt'. It carried both the physical and the moral sense of making something unclean.
items.cn: contaminare 意为「因接触而弄脏、败坏」。它同时带有「使不洁」的物理义与道德义。

items.en: English contaminate appears in the sixteenth century, first of moral or ritual defilement and later of physical mixture.
items.cn: 英语 contaminate 出现于十六世纪，先指道德或仪式上的玷污，后指物理上的混入。

items.en: Contaminant became a separate noun in modern technical English, once laboratories needed a word for the offending substance itself rather than the act.
items.cn: 当实验室需要一个词来指「肇事的物质本身」而非动作时，contaminant 在现代技术英语中成为独立名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the noun, deeper origin of tangere): the noun's first technical citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; the pre-Latin origin of tangere is unsettled and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词的首见年代、tangere 的更深词源）：这个名词最早的 technical 书证没有定论，年代只能约计；tangere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same touch-root family that are easily mistaken for the noun; group two holds other words for unwanted material, each with a different reason for being unwanted.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「触摸」词根、容易被误当作本名词的各种形式；第二组是其他表示「不该有的物质」的词，各自「不该有」的理由不同。

entries.definition: The act or result of contaminating; it names the event or condition, while contaminant names the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 污染的动作或结果；它指事件或状态，而 contaminant 指物质。

entries.definition: To make impure by contact; it is the action that puts a contaminant into something.
entries.definitionCN: 因接触而使不纯；它是把污染物放进某物的动作。

entries.definition: Touching or communication, from the same tangere root but with no sense of defilement.
entries.definitionCN: 接触或联系，同出 tangere 词根，但不含「玷污」之义。

entries.definition: Spread of disease by contact, from contingere 'to touch upon'; it shares the touch root but follows a medical path.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经接触传播，出自 contingere「触及」；它与 contaminant 同享触摸词根，却走的是医学路线。

entries.definition: A substance that harms the environment; a contaminant may be harmless in small amounts and still unfit a product.
entries.definitionCN: 危害环境的物质；污染物质量小时可能无害，却仍能使产品不合格。

entries.definition: Any foreign matter in a material, often harmless; it is a purity term rather than a safety term.
entries.definitionCN: 材料中混入的任何外来物，常为无害；它是纯度术语，而非安全术语。

entries.definition: A substance that is poisonous to living things; toxicity is its defining property, which a contaminant need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物有毒的物质；毒性是它的定义属性，而污染物不一定有毒。

entries.definition: Something added to a product to cheapen or fake it; the motive is deception, not accidental mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 为降低成本或造假而加入产品的东西；其动机是欺骗，而非意外混入。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is tangere 'to touch': something touched the clean body and stayed in it.
normal.cn: 词根是 tangere「触摸」：某物碰过洁净之物并留在了里面。

normal.en: Contaminant is the thing, contamination is the process, contaminate is the act.
normal.cn: contaminant 是物，contamination 是过程，contaminate 是动作。

normal.en: The family runs contaminate, contamination, contaminated, decontaminate and contaminative.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 contaminate、contamination、contaminated、decontaminate 与 contaminative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: chemical contaminant, biological contaminant, trace contaminant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：化学污染物、生物污染物、痕量污染物。

normal.en: Contact and contagion share the touch root but carry no idea of impurity in the same way.
normal.cn: contact 与 contagion 共享触摸词根，但并不以同样的方式带有「不纯」之意。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of ink falling into a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨落进一杯清水。

abstract.en: Picture a single wrong figure entering an otherwise clean ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个错数进入一本本来干净的账。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour passing through a room and changing what everyone repeats.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言穿过一间屋子，改变了每个人复述的内容。

examples.en: The filter removes the contaminant before the water reaches the tap.
examples.cn: 过滤器在水到达龙头之前去除污染物。

examples.en: Each contaminant has its own detection limit and removal method.
examples.cn: 每种污染物都有自己的检出限与去除方法。

examples.en: A biological contaminant can multiply after it enters the product.
examples.cn: 生物污染物进入产品之后还可能增殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ tamin（接触）+ ant」——碰到干净东西、把它弄脏的那一位 → 污染物

root: 拉丁 contaminare「弄脏、败坏」< contamen「接触、污染」= com-（共同）+ tangere「触摸」；tangere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one intrusion: a foreign thing touches a clean body, purity is lost, fitness is lost, the intruder is measured, and finally the same shape is used for corrupted data.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次侵入展开：外来物碰触洁净体，纯净性失去，可用性失去，侵入者被计量，最后同一形态被用于被污染的数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop of oil floating in a bottle of clear water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一瓶清水里浮着一滴油。

branches.en: PURITY AND ENVIRONMENT: the general definition and the environmental case both name the intruder, not the harm.
branches.cn: 纯净与环境：总定义与环境情形命名的都是侵入者，而非危害。

branches.en: LIVING AND TRACE: a microbe and a residue are both small enough to escape the eye.
branches.cn: 活物与痕量：微生物与残留都小到肉眼难辨。

branches.en: PRODUCT SAFETY: what should never be in the package defines this sense.
branches.cn: 产品安全：本不该出现在包装里的东西，界定了这个义项。

branches.en: LOCATION AND FUNCTION: radiation in the wrong place and a particle in a cleanroom both ruin by being where they are.
branches.cn: 位置与功能：错处的辐射与洁净室里的颗粒，都因「待在那里」而毁事。

branches.en: TRANSFER: a bad record contaminates a dataset as oil contaminates water.
branches.cn: 转移：坏记录污染数据集，正如油污染水。

intro.en: Contaminant is a Latin-derived noun with a prefix, a touch root and a participial suffix, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: contaminant 是拉丁来源名词，含前缀、触摸词根与分词后缀，可以逐语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere 'to touch' gives contact, contagion, contiguous and tangible; con- adds 'together' and -ant marks the thing that does the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tangere「触摸」衍生 contact、contagion、contiguous 与 tangible；con- 添「共同」，-ant 标出执行动作之物。

items.example: The prefix marks contact between two things.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出两物之间的接触。

items.example: The root carries the idea of contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「接触」的意思。

items.example: Contamen named the defilement left by touch.
items.exampleCN: contamen 指接触留下的污损。

items.example: The verb entered English as contaminate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词以 contaminate 进入英语。

items.meaning: the thing or person that does
items.example: The suffix makes the verb into the offending thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成「肇事的物」。

items.example: One contaminant spoiled the whole tank.
items.exampleCN: 一种污染物毁掉了整罐。

items.meaning: the act or state of being defiled
items.example: Contamination closed the well.
items.exampleCN: 污染使这口井关闭。

items.example: Teams decontaminated the site.
items.exampleCN: 队伍对场地进行了去污。

items.example: The two surfaces were in contact.
items.exampleCN: 两个表面相互接触。

items.example: Contagion spread through the barracks.
items.exampleCN: 传染病在营房里蔓延。

definition_zh: 顺序；次序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；秩序；修会；勋章；议事规则
definition_en: the arrangement of things in a sequence, a command, or a rank in biological classification
core_image: 一队人按身高排成一行，队首的人手里拿着写有编号的名单
scene: 火车站的值班员按出发时间把列车排成一条队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。 At the station the dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure, and passengers followed that sequence to find their own service.
sceneCN: 这里 order 是「顺序、次序」（第 1 个义项：事物按先后排列的方式）；句意：值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；秩序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；修会；勋章
命令；订购；整理；点（菜）

derivatives.zh: 有序的；被命令的
整齐的；勤务兵
排序；次序安排
序数的；序数词
普通的（同出拉丁 ordo 词根）
法令；条例

senses.title: A sequence of things
senses.definition: the way things are arranged one after another, especially according to time, size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 事物按时间、大小或重要性一个接一个排列的方式
senses.example: The dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure.
senses.exampleCN: 值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列。
senses.why: Latin ordo first meant a row of threads in a loom, then a row of any kind; a sequence is literally a row read from one end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ordo 最初指织机上一排经线，后指任何一排；所谓顺序，字面上就是从一端读过去的一排。

senses.title: A command given to someone
senses.definition: an instruction that must be obeyed, especially one given by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须服从的指示，尤指由权威给出的指示
senses.example: The captain gave the order to close the gates.
senses.exampleCN: 队长下令关闭大门。
senses.why: A command is what puts others into an order: the word names both the arrangement and the act of imposing it, which is why a military order and a neat row share one term.
senses.whyCN: 命令就是让别人进入某种次序：这个词既指排列，也指强加排列的动作，因此军令与整齐的一行共用一个词。

senses.title: A purchase request
senses.definition: a request for goods or food to be supplied, or the goods so requested
senses.definitionCN: 要求供应商品或食物的请求，或如此要求的货物
senses.example: She placed an order for two hundred copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她订购了两百册。
senses.why: Commerce extended the word from arrangement to instruction: an order tells a supplier what to arrange and in what quantity.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个词从排列延伸到指示：订单告诉供货者要安排什么、数量多少。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank order
senses.definition: the rank below class and above family in biological classification
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于纲之下、科之上的阶元
senses.example: The order contains twelve families of beetles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个目包含十二个甲虫科。
senses.why: Taxonomy used the Latin word for a row: an order is a row of families, read in one direction down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 分类学用了这个意为「一排」的拉丁词：一个目就是一排科，沿层级往一个方向读下去。

senses.title: Social or public order
senses.definition: the condition in which rules are obeyed and normal activity can continue
senses.definitionCN: 规则得到遵守、正常活动得以继续的状态
senses.example: The police restored order after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 游行之后警方恢复了秩序。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the row: when everyone is in their place, the whole is in order, and the word names that condition rather than any particular row.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「一排」一般化：当人人各在其位，整体就有秩序，这个词命名的正是那种状态，而非某一特定行列。

senses.title: A religious order
senses.definition: a body of monks, nuns or friars living under one rule, such as the Franciscans
senses.definitionCN: 遵同一会规生活的修士、修女或托钵僧团体，如方济各会
senses.example: The order ran the hospital for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会经营了那所医院三百年。
senses.why: A religious order is a body ordered by a rule; the word names both the community and the discipline that holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 修会是一个按会规排序的团体；这个词既指群体，也指维系群体的那套纪律。

senses.title: An honorary order or decoration
senses.definition: a society of people honoured for service, or the decoration that marks membership
senses.definitionCN: 因功绩受表彰者组成的团体，或标记成员身份的勋章
senses.example: He was admitted to the order for public service.
senses.exampleCN: 他因公共服务被授予该勋位。
senses.why: The sense grew from rank: an order is a graded body of members, and the medal is the visible mark of one's place in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义由「等级」生长出来：勋位是一个分级的成员团体，勋章则是个人在其中的位置可见的标记。

senses.title: A procedural point in a meeting
senses.definition: a question raised about whether the rules of procedure are being followed, as in a point of order
senses.definitionCN: 关于议事规则是否得到遵守而提出的问题，如程序问题
senses.example: A member raised a point of order before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 表决之前有成员提出了程序问题。
senses.why: Meetings run by rules, and the rules are themselves an order; raising a point of order is asking whether the meeting is still following its own arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 会议依规则进行，而规则本身即是一种秩序；提出程序问题就是问会议是否仍遵守自己的安排。

senses.title: Order of magnitude
senses.definition: a class of scale in which one value is about ten times another, used for rough comparison
senses.definitionCN: 一个值约为另一个值的十倍的尺度等级，用于粗略比较
senses.example: The cost rose by an order of magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上升了一个数量级。
senses.why: Here order is a step in a graded series: each step multiplies by ten, so the word names a rung rather than a sequence of items.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 order 是分级系列中的一级：每一级乘以十，因此这个词命名的是一级台阶，而不是一串物件。

senses.title: The classical orders of architecture
senses.definition: one of the recognized styles of column and entablature, such as Doric or Corinthian
senses.definitionCN: 多立克、科林斯等被承认的柱与檐部样式之一
senses.example: The facade mixes two architectural orders on one level.
senses.exampleCN: 这面外墙在同一层混用了两种柱式。
senses.why: Vitruvius used ordo for the due arrangement of parts, and the word became the name of each fixed arrangement of column and capital.
senses.whyCN: 维特鲁威用 ordo 指各部分的合宜安排，这个词后来成为柱与柱头每一种固定搭配的名称。

intro.en: Order comes from Latin ordo 'row, rank, arrangement', a third-declension noun whose deeper origin is disputed. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: order 来自拉丁 ordo「一排、等级、安排」，是第三变格法名词，其更深来源有争议。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, especially a row of threads in a loom, then a rank or an arrangement. The physical row is the oldest image.
items.cn: ordo 指一排，尤其织机上的一排经线，后指等级或安排。物理的一排是最古老的意象。

items.en: The noun is linked to ordiri 'to begin, to lay out a warp'; the connection is accepted, though the verb's own origin is debated.
items.cn: 该名词与 ordiri「开始、铺开经线」相关；这一联系一般认为是成立的，但动词本身的来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French ordre brought the word into English, where it covered both a row and a command by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 ordre 把该词带入英语，到 13 世纪已兼指一排与命令。

items.en: The medieval church used order for the ranks of clergy, and the phrase religious order fixed the sense of a community under one rule.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 order 指神职等级，religious order 一语则固定了「同一会规下的团体」这一义。

items.en: Linnaeus gave order a place in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, between class and family.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪给 order 在层级中安排了位置，位于纲与科之间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between ordo and ordiri is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of both is unsettled, so Indo-European forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ordo 与 ordiri 的联系一般认为是成立的，但二者在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the many English words that descend from ordo; group two compares words of neighbouring meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分源自 ordo 的众多英语词；第二组比较意思相邻的词。

entries.definition: A number that marks position in a series, such as first or tenth, from ordinalis. It names a place, not a command.
entries.definitionCN: 标记序列位置的数词，如第一、第十，出自 ordinalis。它指位置，不指命令。

entries.definition: Common or usual, from ordinarius 'according to order'. The sense drifted from 'regular' to 'unremarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 普通、通常的，出自 ordinarius「按次序的」。词义从「合规矩」漂移到「不出奇」。

entries.definition: A decree or regulation, from ordinare 'to arrange'. It is a law that arranges conduct, not a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或条例，出自 ordinare「安排」。它是安排行为的法规，不是顺序。

entries.definition: To confer holy orders or to decree, from ordinare. It names an authoritative act, not an arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 授予圣职或颁布，出自 ordinare。它指权威性的行为，而非排列。

entries.definition: A series in which one thing follows another, from sequi 'to follow'. It stresses succession, while order can also mean a command or a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一物接一物形成的系列，出自 sequi「跟随」。它强调接续，而 order 还可指命令或阶元。

entries.definition: The way items are placed relative to one another. It is the result, while order can be the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 各物彼此的摆放方式。它是结果，order 则可以是背后的原则。

entries.definition: A directive from an authority. It matches one branch of order but not the sequence branch.
entries.definitionCN: 权威发出的指示。它对应 order 的一支，而不对应顺序那一支。

entries.definition: A position in a graded scale, as in taxonomic rank. It names the level, while order can name the whole arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 分级尺度中的位置，如分类阶元。它指层级，order 则可指整套安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ordo was a row of threads: order is first a row, then a rule that keeps things in rows.
normal.cn: ordo 原是一排经线：order 先是一排，后指使事物各在其排的规则。

normal.en: The same word gives ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain, all built on ordinare 'to arrange'.
normal.cn: 同一个词给出 ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain，皆基于 ordinare「安排」。

normal.en: In biology the order sits between class and family, one rung of the ladder.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，目位于纲与科之间，是梯子上的一级。

normal.en: A point of order asks whether the meeting is following its own rules.
normal.cn: 程序问题问的是会议是否遵守自己的规则。

normal.en: An order of magnitude is one step of ten, a rung rather than a row.
normal.cn: 数量级是以十为一步的一级，是一级台阶而非一排。

abstract.en: Picture a loom where one wrong thread makes the whole pattern shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机，一根线错了，整个花样就移位。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that stays calm because everyone knows their number.
abstract.cn: 想象一支队伍因为人人知道自己的号而保持平静。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet whose drawers are labelled by size, each ten times the one before.
abstract.cn: 想象一柜按大小标注的抽屉，每一格是前一格的十倍。

examples.en: The names were read out in the order in which they had been received.
examples.cn: 姓名按收到的先后顺序被念出。

examples.en: The general's order reached the front line before dawn.
examples.cn: 将军的命令在黎明前传到了前线。

examples.en: The two families belong to the same order but different superfamilies.
examples.cn: 这两个科属于同一个目，但属于不同的总科。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「or 或者 + der 得」——或者这样排、或者那样排，总得有个次序 → order 顺序；命令

root: 拉丁 ordo, ordinis「一排、等级、安排」，与 ordiri「铺开经线、开始」相关；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of order follow the row outward: a sequence, a command that imposes sequence, a purchase, a taxonomic rung, social calm, a ruled community, an honour, a procedural question, a factor of ten and a style of columns.
sensesIntro.cn: order 的十个义项沿着「一排」向外走：顺序、强加顺序的命令、订单、生物阶元、社会安定、守会规的团体、勋位、程序问题、十倍一级、柱式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row read from one end, and the rule that keeps it a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一端读过去的一排，以及使它保持成一排的那条规则。

branches.en: THE ROW ITSELF: a sequence of items, a factor of ten, or a fixed arrangement of columns.
branches.cn: 一排本身：一串物件、十倍的级差，或柱子的固定搭配。

branches.en: THE INSTRUCTION: a command and a purchase both tell someone what to arrange.
branches.cn: 指示：命令与订单都在告诉别人该安排什么。

branches.en: THE RANK: an order in taxonomy and an honour both place a member on a graded ladder.
branches.cn: 等级：生物学的目与勋位都把成员放在分级的梯子上。

branches.en: THE RULE: social order and a point of order both concern whether rules are being kept.
branches.cn: 规则：社会秩序与程序问题都关心规则是否被遵守。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: a religious order is a body held together by one rule.
branches.cn: 团体：修会是由一条会规维系的群体。

intro.en: Order is a Latin noun that English uses for rows, commands and ranks alike; the common thread is arranged position.
intro.cn: order 是拉丁名词，英语用它同时指行列、命令与等级；共同的线索是「被安排的位置」。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo yields order, ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain; ordinare 'to arrange' is the verb behind the derived forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ordo 衍生 order、ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain；ordinare「安排」是这些派生形式背后的动词。

items.example: Ordo began as a row of threads.
items.exampleCN: ordo 最初指一排线。

items.example: The verb supplies ordering and ordinance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 ordering 与 ordinance。

items.example: One word covers the row and the rule.
items.exampleCN: 一个词同时覆盖一排与规则。

items.example: Ordinal numbers answer 'which place'.
items.exampleCN: 序数回答「第几位」。

items.example: The ordinary sense drifted to 'unremarkable'.
items.exampleCN: ordinary 的词义漂移到「不出奇」。

items.example: An ordinance arranges conduct by rule.
items.exampleCN: 法令按规则安排行为。

items.example: Ordain names the act of putting someone in place.
items.exampleCN: ordain 指把某人放到位置上的行为。

items.example: An orderly ward keeps everything in its row.
items.exampleCN: 整齐的病房让一切各在其位。

items.example: A suborder narrows the row of families.
items.exampleCN: 亚目收窄了那一排科。

definition_zh: 受益人；受惠者；（遗嘱、保险、信托等的）受益方
definition_en: a person or organization that receives money or an advantage under a will, policy, trust, or other arrangement
core_image: 一份文件的受益人栏上写着一个名字，箭头从文件指向这个人
scene: 她把人寿保单的受益人一栏填上妹妹的名字。 She named her sister as the sole beneficiary of her life insurance policy.
sceneCN: 这里 beneficiary 是「受益人」（第 2 个义项：保险金受益人）；句意：她指定妹妹作为她人寿保险的唯一受益人。场景要点：保单、受益人栏、签名、保险公司印章、信封。

pos.zh: 受益人；受惠者；（保险、遗嘱、信托的）受益方

derivatives.zh: 有益的；有利的
好处；受益；有益于
捐助者；施惠者
善行；仁慈

senses.title: One named in a will
senses.titleCN: 遗嘱受益人：按遗嘱取得财产的人
senses.definition: a person named in a will to receive property or money from an estate
senses.definitionCN: 在遗嘱中被指定从遗产中获得财产或钱财的人
senses.example: Her three grandchildren were the beneficiaries of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 她的三个孙辈是这笔遗产的受益人。
senses.why: beneficium is a favor or benefit, and -arius names the person connected with it; English -ary carries that personal sense. The first English use (1610s) was simply 'one who receives profits or advantages', and a will is the oldest concrete setting for that idea.
senses.whyCN: beneficium 是恩惠或好处，-arius 指与之相关的人，英语 -ary 承接了这个指人的含义。该词 1610 年代最早只是“获得利润或好处的人”，而遗嘱是这一观念最古老的落地场景。

senses.title: Insurance beneficiary
senses.titleCN: 保险金受益人：保单指定领钱的人
senses.definition: the person or party named in an insurance policy to receive its payout
senses.definitionCN: 在保险单中被指定领取保险金的人或方
senses.example: The policy pays the beneficiary directly, outside the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 保单直接向受益人赔付，不进入遗产程序。
senses.why: Insurance law lets a nomination do the work: the named person steps into the benefit at death. The general 'receiver of advantage' is narrowed to a named payee, which is why a beneficiary need not be an heir.
senses.whyCN: 保险法让“指定”本身发挥作用：被指定者在被保险人死亡时直接承接这笔利益。泛指的“好处接受者”在这里收窄为具名收款人，所以受益人未必是继承人。

senses.title: Trust beneficiary
senses.titleCN: 信托受益人：享有信托利益的人
senses.definition: a person entitled to income or capital from a trust, while a trustee holds the legal title
senses.definitionCN: 有权从信托中获得收益或本金、而由受托人持有法定所有权的人
senses.example: The trust's beneficiaries receive the income but do not control the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 信托受益人领取收益，但不控制本金。
senses.why: In a trust, legal title and enjoyment split: the trustee holds, the beneficiary enjoys. The word names the equitable side of that split, which is the same 'one who enjoys the benefit' idea in technical form.
senses.whyCN: 在信托中，法定所有权与享受权被拆开：受托人持有，受益人享有。这个词命名的正是这条裂缝中“享有”的那一侧，也就是“享有利益者”这一观念的技术形态。

senses.title: Charity or aid recipient
senses.definition: a person or household that receives help from a charity, welfare scheme, or aid programme
senses.definitionCN: 从慈善机构、福利计划或援助项目获得帮助的个人或家庭
senses.example: The programme asks each beneficiary to attend a training session.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目要求每位受助者参加一次培训。
senses.why: Aid language prefers beneficiary to 'poor person' because it frames the person as the rightful receiver of a benefit, not as an object of pity. The legal word supplies dignity as well as precision.
senses.whyCN: 援助话语更愿意用 beneficiary 而不是“穷人”，因为它把人框定为“有资格获得好处的人”，而不是被怜悯的对象。这个法律词同时提供了精确与尊严。

senses.title: Payment beneficiary in banking
senses.titleCN: 银行付款的收款人；信用证受益人
senses.definition: the party to whom a payment is to be made, especially under a transfer or letter of credit
senses.definitionCN: 应收款的一方，尤指汇款或信用证项下的收款人
senses.example: The bank released the funds once the beneficiary presented the shipping documents.
senses.exampleCN: 受益人一提交装运单据，银行就放款了。
senses.why: In banking the benefit is a payment, so the beneficiary is the party to whom money is owed or addressed. The word becomes a technical label printed on forms, and the 'benefit' is reduced to a sum of money.
senses.whyCN: 在银行业务中，好处就是一笔付款，所以 beneficiary 是应收款或被指定收款的一方。这个词成了印在单据上的技术标签，“好处”被压缩为一笔金额。

senses.title: Third-party beneficiary of a contract
senses.definition: a person outside a contract who is intended to receive its benefit and may enforce it
senses.definitionCN: 合同之外、被意图给予合同利益并可据此主张权利的人
senses.example: The subcontractor was a third-party beneficiary of the main contract.
senses.exampleCN: 分包商是主合同的第三方受益人。
senses.why: Contract law extends the will model: a person who never signed the agreement may still be its intended receiver. Beneficiary then means 'the one the promise was meant to benefit', not 'the one who made the promise'.
senses.whyCN: 合同法延伸了遗嘱模型：从未签过协议的人也可能是约定的受益对象。此时 beneficiary 指“承诺本想使之受益的人”，而不是“作出承诺的人”。

senses.title: Development beneficiary or country
senses.titleCN: 发展项目的受益群体；受援国
senses.definition: a community, household group, or country that receives development assistance
senses.definitionCN: 接受发展援助的社区、家庭群体或国家
senses.example: The report compared outcomes across five beneficiary countries.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了五个受援国的结果。
senses.why: When the receiver is a whole community or state, the noun becomes a policy category. The benefit is now development assistance rather than a private gift, so the word works at the scale of projects and governments.
senses.whyCN: 当接受方是整个社区或国家时，这个名词变成政策类别。此时的好处是发展援助而非私人赠与，于是这个词在项目与政府的尺度上运作。

senses.title: Anyone who gains from an event
senses.titleCN: 泛指受益者：从某事中得到好处的人
senses.definition: a person or group that profits from a change, event, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 从某种变化、事件或局势中获利的人或群体
senses.example: Small exporters were the main beneficiaries of the weaker currency.
senses.exampleCN: 小出口商是货币走弱的主要受益者。
senses.why: Once the legal senses are established, the word can be used loosely of anyone who profits from an event. The benefit need not come from a document at all; it can come from a policy, a storm, or a market move.
senses.whyCN: 法律义项确立之后，这个词可以宽松地指任何从事件中获利的人。好处完全不必来自文件，也可以来自政策、风暴或市场波动。

senses.title: Attributive: the receiving side
senses.titleCN: 受益方的：作定语指接受的一方
senses.definition: used before another noun to label the receiving side of a scheme or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 置于另一名词前，标记某项计划或安排中接受的一方的
senses.example: Beneficiary families received the cash transfer at the start of each term.
senses.exampleCN: 受益家庭在每学期开始时收到现金补助。
senses.why: English often puts a noun before another noun instead of using an adjective, and beneficiary does this job in phrases such as beneficiary country and beneficiary family. It still names a person or party, but it now modifies rather than stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用名词而非形容词来修饰另一个名词，beneficiary 就在 beneficiary country、beneficiary family 这类短语里承担这个功能。它仍然指人或一方，但此时是修饰而非独立充当名词。

intro.en: Beneficiary and beneficial come from the same Latin noun beneficium, but they are not the same derivative. Beneficial goes through the adjective suffix -alis and names a quality; beneficiary goes through -arius and names a person. The noun reached English in the 1610s, probably through French.
intro.cn: beneficiary 和 beneficial 出自同一个拉丁名词 beneficium，但它们不是同一条派生。beneficial 走 -alis 这一形容词后缀，命名性质；beneficiary 走 -arius，命名人。这个名词在 17 世纪 10 年代进入英语，可能经由法语。

items.en: bene 'well' plus facere 'to do, make' produce beneficus 'generous, kind, obliging', literally 'doing well'. The pair is the common base of benefit, benefactor, beneficial and beneficiary.
items.cn: bene“好”加上 facere“做、造”产生 beneficus“慷慨的、善良的、乐于助人的”，字面即“做好事”。这一对成分是 benefit、benefactor、beneficial、beneficiary 的共同基础。

items.en: The noun beneficium 'a favor, service, kindness' adds -ium to the stem. It can mean a concrete benefit, a kindness done, and later a church office granted as a 'benefit' with its income.
items.cn: 名词 beneficium“恩惠、服务、善意”在词干上加 -ium。它可以指具体的好处、一次善举，后来也指作为“好处”授予的、带收入的教会圣职。

items.en: beneficiarius means 'enjoying a favor, privileged', built with -arius 'connected with, belonging to'. In Latin it describes a person attached to a benefit; the suffix is personal, not abstract.
items.cn: beneficiarius 意为“享有恩惠的、有特权的”，由 -arius“与……有关的、属于……的”构成。在拉丁语中它描述与好处相连的人；这个后缀是指人的，不是抽象性质的。

items.en: English beneficiary (1610s) probably came via French bénéficiaire, first as a noun 'one who receives profits or advantages', then in the 1620s as an adjective. The noun is now far more common than the adjective.
items.cn: 英语 beneficiary（17 世纪 10 年代）很可能经由法语 bénéficiaire 而来，先作名词“获得利润或好处的人”，17 世纪 20 年代再作形容词。如今名词用法远比形容词用法常见。

items.en: This is the key contrast with beneficial. beneficialis uses -alis to make 'pertaining to a benefit', a quality adjective. beneficiarius uses -arius to make 'the person who enjoys a benefit', a personal noun. Same base, different suffix, different word class.
items.cn: 这是它与 beneficial 的关键差别。beneficialis 用 -alis 构成“与好处有关的”性质形容词；beneficiarius 用 -arius 构成“享有好处的人”这一指人名词。同一词基，不同后缀，不同词性。

items.en: Modern English pushed the noun into law and finance: wills, life insurance, trusts, letters of credit, third-party contract rights. The old adjective use faded, and the attributive use in beneficiary country is a noun adjunct, not a revival of the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词推入法律与金融：遗嘱、人寿保险、信托、信用证、合同第三方权利。旧的形容词用法衰落了；beneficiary country 里的定语用法是名词作定语，并不是旧形容词的复活。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin base but differs in suffix and direction (giver or receiver); the second group contains words for receivers that differ in legal status and setting.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基，但后缀和方向不同（给予者还是接受者）；第二组都是“接受者”，但法律身份与场景不同。

entries.definition: Producing a good effect. It is an adjective, so it can never stand for the person who receives; -ial marks quality, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 产生良好效果的。它是形容词，绝不能代替接受者本人；-ial 标记性质，不指人。

entries.definition: Kind and generous in character. It points at the person who does good, the opposite direction from beneficiary.
entries.definitionCN: 生性仁慈慷慨的。它指向行善的人，方向与 beneficiary 相反。

entries.definition: A church office with its income. It looks like beneficiary shortened, but it comes from the 'office granted' branch of beneficium.
entries.definitionCN: 带收入的教会圣职。它看起来像 beneficiary 的缩短形式，但来自 beneficium“授予的职位”这一分支。

entries.definition: A person who gives help or money. Benefactor gives; beneficiary receives; the -fact- of benefactor is the 'do' of facere.
entries.definitionCN: 提供帮助或金钱的人。benefactor 给，beneficiary 收；benefactor 里的 -fact- 就是 facere 的“做”。

entries.definition: Anyone who receives something. It is neutral and carries no legal entitlement, whereas beneficiary implies a recognized right to the benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接受某物的人。它是中性的，不含法律权利；而 beneficiary 暗示对该利益有被承认的权利。

entries.definition: A person who inherits property by law or blood relationship, whether or not a will names them.
entries.definitionCN: 依法定或血缘继承财产的人，无论遗嘱是否点名。

entries.definition: A person who receives a legacy, usually money or movable property, under a will. Narrower than beneficiary, which also covers insurance and trusts.
entries.definitionCN: 依遗嘱接受遗赠（通常是钱或动产）的人。比 beneficiary 窄，后者还涵盖保险与信托。

entries.definition: The party to whom a payment is made, especially on a cheque or bill. It names only the receiving end of a payment.
entries.definitionCN: 收款的一方，尤指支票或票据上的收款人。它只命名付款的接收端。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real documents and real contrasts with the giver's word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的文书，以及和“给予者”一词的真实对比。

normal.en: -ary marks a person attached to something; in beneficiary that person is attached to a benefit, while -ial in beneficial marks a quality instead.
normal.cn: -ary 标记附着于某物的人；在 beneficiary 里此人与“好处”相连，而 beneficial 的 -ial 标记的是性质。

normal.en: Three documents always have a beneficiary line: a will, an insurance policy, and a trust deed.
normal.cn: 三种文书总有受益人栏：遗嘱、保单、信托契约。

normal.en: Direction test: benefactor gives, beneficiary receives. If the sentence is about giving, it is the wrong word.
normal.cn: 方向测试：benefactor 给，beneficiary 收。如果句子讲的是“给”，那就用错了词。

normal.en: Same stem as beneficial, different suffix: -ary makes a person, -ial makes a quality.
normal.cn: 与 beneficial 同词干、不同后缀：-ary 造人，-ial 造性质。

normal.en: In a letter of credit the form itself names the beneficiary, so banking gives the word a concrete place.
normal.cn: 在信用证里，表格本身就要填 beneficiary，银行业务给了这个词一个具体的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a document with an arrow leaving the page and landing on a person: the person at the arrow's end is the beneficiary.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件，一支箭头离开纸面落在一个人身上：箭头末端的那个人就是 beneficiary。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs facing each other: the giver's chair is benefactor, the receiver's chair is beneficiary.
abstract.cn: 想象两把面对面的椅子：给予者的椅子是 benefactor，接受者的椅子是 beneficiary。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a line: the line is the channel through which the benefit flows, and the name is the person at its end.
abstract.cn: 想象一条横线上写着一个名字：这条线是利益流动的通道，名字就是通道末端的人。

examples.en: She left the house to her nephew as the sole beneficiary of her will.
examples.cn: 她把房子留给侄子，作为她遗嘱的唯一受益人。

examples.en: The insurance company paid the beneficiary within thirty days.
examples.cn: 保险公司在三十天内向受益人支付了赔款。

examples.en: Rural households were the main beneficiaries of the electrification programme.
examples.cn: 农村家庭是电气化项目的主要受益者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 本（ben）来的好处（benefit）舍（she）给谁，谁就是 beneficiary 受益人

root: 拉丁 bene“好”+ facere“做” → beneficium“恩惠” → beneficiarius“受恩惠者、享有特权者”；-ary 表“与……有关的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one position: the person at the receiving end of a benefit. What changes is the document that assigns it — a will, a policy, a trust, a contract, a payment order — or, in the loosest sense, no document at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个位置：处在利益接受端的那个人。变化的是分配利益的那份文书——遗嘱、保单、信托、合同、付款指令——或者在最宽松的义项里，根本没有文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named person at the receiving end of a benefit written into a document.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在文书里的利益，末端是一个具名的接受者。

branches.en: PRIVATE AND CHARITABLE RECEIVERS: a will names an heir; a charity names the person it helps.
branches.cn: 私人与慈善接受者：遗嘱点名继承人；慈善机构点名它帮助的人。

branches.en: POLICY AND TRUST: the nomination or the trust deed assigns the benefit to a named party.
branches.cn: 保单与信托：指定或信托契据把利益分配给具名的一方。

branches.en: PAYMENT AND CONTRACT: banking and contract law make the beneficiary a technical party with a right to enforce.
branches.cn: 付款与合同：银行和合同法使 beneficiary 成为有主张权的技术性当事方。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND ATTRIBUTIVE: whole countries and households become the receiving side of a programme.
branches.cn: 集体与定语用法：整个国家与家庭成为项目的接受方。

branches.en: LOOSE EXTENSION: anyone who profits from an event, with no document at all.
branches.cn: 宽松延伸：任何从事件中获利的人，完全不需要文书。

intro.en: Beneficiary is bene- + -fic- + -ary, and each piece is still readable: 'well' + 'doing' + 'person connected with'. The -ary ending is the decisive one, because it turns a benefit into a person.
intro.cn: beneficiary 是 bene- + -fic- + -ary，每一块至今仍可读：“好”+“做”+“与之相连的人”。决定性的是 -ary，因为它把“好处”变成了“人”。

latinIntro.en: Latin bene and facere also produced beneficium, beneficus and beneficiarius. English keeps the -ary branch for people (beneficiary) and the -ial branch for qualities (beneficial), a split inherited from Latin suffix choice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bene 和 facere 还产生了 beneficium、beneficus、beneficiarius。英语把 -ary 那一支留给指人（beneficiary），把 -ial 那一支留给性质（beneficial），这一分裂承自拉丁语的后缀选择。

items.meaning: an advantage; to help or gain
items.example: The scholarship brought a real benefit to her family.
items.exampleCN: 这笔奖学金给她家带来了实实在在的好处。

items.example: The change was beneficial to the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 这一变化对整个团队都有益。

items.meaning: a person who receives a benefit
items.example: The beneficiary must show proof of identity.
items.exampleCN: 受益人必须出示身份证明。

items.meaning: one who gives help or money
items.example: A benefactor funded the new laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 一位捐助者出资修建了新实验室。

items.example: The clinic depends on the beneficence of donors.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所依靠捐助者的善心维持。

items.example: A beneficent stranger paid for the medicine.
items.exampleCN: 一位好心的陌生人付了药费。

items.meaning: a church office with its income
items.example: The bishop granted him a benefice.
items.exampleCN: 主教授予他一处圣职俸禄。

items.meaning: the formal act of naming a beneficiary
items.meaningCN: 受益人指定（正式指定受益人的行为）
items.example: A beneficiary designation must be signed and dated.
items.exampleCN: 受益人指定必须签名并注明日期。

items.example: The maleficent spell brought illness to the village.
items.exampleCN: 恶毒的咒语给村庄带来了疾病。

items.example: They manufacture medical devices in this plant.
items.exampleCN: 他们在这座工厂生产医疗器械。

latinEntries.meaning: a favor, service, kindness; a granted office
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恩惠；服务；善意；授予的职位

definition_zh: 优化；最优化；最佳化；调优
definition_en: the process of making something as good or as effective as possible, often within stated limits
core_image: 一条曲线上有一个最低点，一支笔沿着线移动，最后停在那一点上。
scene: 工程团队反复调整参数，让同一台发动机在油耗与动力之间找到折中。 Years of optimization brought fuel use and power into balance.
sceneCN: 这里 optimization 是“在约束下把效果调到最好”（第 2 个义项）；句意：多年的优化让油耗与动力达到平衡。

pos.zh: 优化；最优化；最佳化；调优

最优的；最佳的
最适条件；最佳的
乐观主义者

senses.title: Making it as good as it can be
senses.definition: the process of improving something toward its best possible state
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物朝其最佳可能状态改进的过程
senses.example: The optimization of the design took months of small changes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项设计的优化花了数月时间做小改动。
senses.why: The word is comparative in secret: it assumes a scale of better and worse, then moves an object along that scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个词暗含比较：它预设了一条“更好—更差”的尺度，然后把对象沿这条尺度推动。

senses.title: Best under constraints
senses.titleCN: 最优化：在限制里找最好的那点
senses.definition: the mathematical process of finding the best solution to a problem within given limits
senses.definitionCN: 在给定限制内为问题寻找最佳解的数学过程
senses.example: The optimization problem asked for the shortest route under a fixed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这个最优化问题要求在固定预算下找出最短路线。
senses.why: Mathematics adds constraints: without limits almost anything could be improved, and with them a best point may exist.
senses.whyCN: 数学加上了约束：没有限制，几乎任何东西都能再改进；有了限制，才可能存在一个最优点。

senses.title: A procedure that searches
senses.titleCN: 优化算法：一步步试出更好的解
senses.definition: an algorithm or method that searches for a better solution by repeated adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复调整搜索更优解的算法或方法
senses.example: The optimization converged after forty iterations.
senses.exampleCN: 该优化过程在四十次迭代后收敛。
senses.why: When the best point cannot be calculated directly, the work becomes a search: adjust, measure, keep what improves, repeat.
senses.whyCN: 当最优点无法直接算出时，工作就变成搜索：调整、测量、保留改进、重复。

senses.title: Spending less for the same result
senses.titleCN: 成本优化：同样的效果，更少的钱
senses.definition: the reduction of costs while maintaining an acceptable level of output or quality
senses.definitionCN: 在维持可接受产出或质量水平的同时降低成本
senses.example: Cost optimization cut the packaging budget without changing the product.
senses.exampleCN: 成本优化削减了包装预算，产品本身没有变化。
senses.why: In business the scale is money: the same output is held fixed while the input is pushed down, which is optimization in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 在商业中，尺度是钱：产出保持不变，投入被压低，这是单向的优化。

senses.title: Being found by search engines
senses.titleCN: 搜索引擎优化：让页面更容易被找到
senses.definition: the practice of improving a web page so that search engines rank it more highly
senses.definitionCN: 改进网页以使其在搜索引擎中获得更高排名的做法
senses.example: Search engine optimization raised the shop's traffic without any advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 搜索引擎优化在没有投放广告的情况下提高了店铺流量。
senses.why: Here the 'best state' is defined by an external ranking system, so optimization means fitting the page to someone else's scoring rule.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“最佳状态”由外部排名系统定义，因此优化意味着让页面迎合别人的评分规则。

senses.title: Getting more from what you have
senses.titleCN: 资源优化：同一批人、同一批料，做出更多
senses.definition: the arrangement of people, materials, or time so that available resources produce the most value
senses.definitionCN: 安排人力、物料或时间，使现有资源产出最大价值
senses.example: Resource optimization moved two nurses to the night shift and cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 资源优化把两名护士调去夜班，缩短了等待时间。
senses.why: When resources are fixed, improvement can only come from arrangement: the same pieces are ordered differently.
senses.whyCN: 当资源固定时，改进只能来自安排：同样的零件被重新排序。

senses.title: Making software run faster
senses.titleCN: 性能优化：让程序少等、少算
senses.definition: the process of making software use less time, memory, or power for the same task
senses.definitionCN: 使软件完成同一任务时消耗更少时间、内存或电力的过程
senses.example: Performance optimization reduced the page load from four seconds to one.
senses.exampleCN: 性能优化把页面加载时间从四秒降到一秒。
senses.why: Computing gives optimization a measurable target: the same output must be produced with fewer machine cycles.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域给优化一个可测量的目标：同样的输出必须用更少的机器周期完成。

senses.title: Rewriting code before it runs
senses.titleCN: 编译器优化：运行前先替代码省力
senses.definition: the rewriting of code by a compiler to make the resulting program faster or smaller
senses.definitionCN: 由编译器改写代码，使生成的程序更快或更小
senses.example: Compiler optimization removed a loop that always ran zero times.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器优化删掉了一个永远执行零次的循环。
senses.why: The compiler optimizes on the programmer's behalf, using facts proved at compile time to drop work the program would otherwise do.
senses.whyCN: 编译器替程序员做优化，利用编译期已证明的事实删去程序本会执行的工作。

intro.en: Optimization comes from optimize, formed from Latin optimum, 'the best', plus -ize and -ation. Optimum is the neuter of optimus, the superlative of bonus, good.
intro.cn: optimization 来自 optimize，由拉丁语 optimum“最好的”加 -ize 与 -ation 构成。optimum 是 optimus 的中性形式，而 optimus 是 bonus“好”的最高级。

items.en: Bonus meant good. Its comparative melior and superlative optimus supplied the whole scale of better and best.
items.cn: bonus 意为好。其比较级 melior 与最高级 optimus 提供了“更好—最好”的整条尺度。

items.en: Optimus meant best. The neuter optimum named the best thing or the best condition, and entered English as a noun and adjective.
items.cn: optimus 意为最好的。其中性形式 optimum 指最好的事物或最佳条件，作为名词与形容词进入英语。

items.en: English optimum first appeared in scientific writing for the best condition, such as the temperature at which an enzyme works best.
items.cn: 英语 optimum 最初出现在科学写作中，指最佳条件，例如酶活性最高的温度。

items.en: Optimize was formed in the 19th century on optimum plus -ize, meaning to make the best of a situation.
items.cn: optimize 于 19 世纪由 optimum 加 -ize 构成，意为“充分利用条件、使达到最好”。

items.en: The suffix -ation, from -atio, turns the verb into the name of the process. Optimization is therefore the process of making optimal.
items.cn: 后缀 -ation（源自 -atio）把动词变成过程之名。因此 optimization 就是“使之最优”的过程。

items.en: Mathematics and computing gave the word its technical sense: a search for a best point under constraints, and the rewriting of code for speed.
items.cn: 数学与计算赋予该词技术含义：在约束下搜索最优点，以及为提速而改写代码。

note.en: The first group is the optimum family; the second compares words for improvement, each with a different standard of 'better'.
note.cn: 第一组是 optimum 词族；第二组比较表示“改进”的词，各自对“更好”的标准不同。

entries.definition: to make something as effective as possible. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能有效；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: best or most favourable among the options available.
entries.definitionCN: 在可选方案中最好的或最有利的。

entries.definition: the best possible condition or level.
entries.definitionCN: 最佳的可能条件或水平。

entries.definition: a change that makes something better. It does not imply that a best point has been reached.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变好的改变；不暗示已到达最优点。

entries.definition: a small change that makes something more precise or elegant. It is improvement by polishing.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物更精确或更精致的小改动；靠打磨实现的改进。

entries.definition: output divided by input. Optimization often raises it, but the two are not the same.
entries.definitionCN: 产出与投入之比；优化常提高效率，但二者并不相同。

entries.definition: making something as large as possible. Optimization can target a maximum or a minimum.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能大；优化既可以求最大，也可以求最小。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: optimum, the best, plus -ize and -ation. Optimization is the process of moving something toward the best available point.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：optimum“最好的”，加 -ize 与 -ation。optimization 就是把事物推向最佳可用点的过程。

normal.en: Optimum is the best point on the curve; optimization is the walk toward it.
normal.cn: optimum 是曲线上的最优点；optimization 是走向它的那段路。

normal.en: No constraints, no optimum: the limits are what make a best point exist.
normal.cn: 没有约束就没有最优：正是限制让“最优点”得以存在。

normal.en: Cost optimization keeps the output and squeezes the input.
normal.cn: 成本优化固定产出，挤压投入。

normal.en: Search engine optimization is fitting a page to someone else's scoring rule.
normal.cn: 搜索引擎优化就是让页面迎合别人的评分规则。

normal.en: Compiler optimization does the tidying before the program ever runs.
normal.cn: 编译器优化在程序运行之前就替它收拾干净。

abstract.en: Every optimization chooses a measure, and the measure quietly decides what counts as good.
abstract.cn: 每次优化都要选一个度量，而度量悄悄决定了什么算“好”。

abstract.en: What is optimal for one part of a system is often costly for another; the whole is rarely optimized at once.
abstract.cn: 对系统某部分最优的事，往往对另一部分代价高昂；整体很少能一次同时达到最优。

abstract.en: The word sounds final, but an optimum is only the best among the options someone thought to consider.
abstract.cn: 这个词听起来像终点，但最优点只是“在某人想到要考虑的选项里”最好的那个。

examples.en: The optimization of the timetable saved eight buses without lengthening any trip.
examples.cn: 时刻表的优化省下了八辆车，却没有延长任何一趟行程。

examples.en: The algorithm's optimization step is where most of the computing time goes.
examples.cn: 算法中耗去大部分计算时间的正是优化那一步。

examples.en: She studied cost optimization in hospitals and found that supplies, not staff, drove the waste.
examples.cn: 她研究医院成本优化，发现造成浪费的是耗材，而不是人力。

dict_mnemonic.text: optim（最好）+ ization（化）——朝“最好”去的过程，就是优化、最优化。

root: 源自拉丁语 optimum（最好的，为 optimus 的中性形式，optimus 又是 bonus“好”的最高级），加 -ize 与 -ation 构成，本义为“使之达到最佳状态的过程”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of optimization, all built on one shape: a curve with a best point and a search toward it. The curve may be mathematical, financial, operational, computational, or a search engine's ranking rule.
sensesIntro.cn: optimization 的八个义项都建立在同一个形状上：一条带有最优点的曲线，以及朝它进行的搜索。这条曲线可以是数学的、财务的、运营的、计算的，或搜索引擎的排名规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve with a lowest point, and a pen moving along it until it stops there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条带最低点的曲线，一支笔沿线移动，最后停在那一点。

chain: ENGLISH OPTIMIZE TO MAKE THE BEST OF
OPTIMIZATION THE SEARCH FOR THE BEST AVAILABLE POINT

branches.en: THE GENERAL MOVE AND THE MATHEMATICAL ONE: improving toward a best state, and finding a best point under constraints.
branches.cn: 一般推进与数学求解：朝最佳状态改进，以及在约束下找最优点。

branches.en: SEARCH BY ITERATION: adjust, measure, keep what improves, repeat.
branches.cn: 迭代搜索：调整、测量、保留改进、重复。

branches.en: SAME OUTPUT, LESS INPUT: cost squeezed with quality held, and fixed resources rearranged.
branches.cn: 同产出、少投入：质量不变而压缩成本，以及重排固定资源。

branches.en: FITTING AN EXTERNAL RULE: a page tuned to a ranking system it does not control.
branches.cn: 迎合外部规则：页面被调向一个它无法控制的排名系统。

branches.en: MACHINE SPEED: fewer cycles at run time, and code rewritten before run time.
branches.cn: 机器速度：运行时减少周期，以及运行前改写代码。

intro.en: Optimization is optimize plus -ation. Optimize is optimum plus -ize, and optimum is the Latin superlative 'best'. The family also gives optimal, optimally, and optimist.
intro.cn: optimization 是 optimize 加 -ation。optimize 是 optimum 加 -ize，而 optimum 是拉丁语最高级“最好的”。词族还有 optimal、optimally、optimist。

latinIntro.en: The base is optimus, best, the superlative of bonus, good. Optimum is its neuter form, used as a noun for the best condition.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 optimus“最好的”，为 bonus“好”的最高级。optimum 是其中性形式，作名词指最佳条件。

items.meaning: the most favourable condition or level
items.example: The crop grows best near the optimum temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这种作物在最佳温度附近长得最好。

items.example: The optimal route avoids the morning traffic.
items.exampleCN: 最优路线避开了早高峰。

items.meaning: to make as effective as possible
items.example: They optimized the layout to cut walking distance.
items.exampleCN: 他们优化布局以缩短走动距离。

items.meaning: the process of reaching the best available state
items.meaningCN: 达到最佳可用状态的过程
items.example: The optimization reduced fuel use by a fifth.
items.exampleCN: 这项优化把燃料消耗降低了五分之一。

items.example: The engine runs optimally at this speed.
items.exampleCN: 发动机在这个转速下运转最佳。

items.meaning: the view that things are or will be good; hopefulness
items.meaningCN: 认为事物是或将是好的观点；乐观
items.example: Her optimism carried the team through the delay.
items.exampleCN: 她的乐观让团队熬过了延误。

items.meaning: the opposite of optimism, built on the Latin superlative for worst
items.meaningCN: 乐观的反面，由拉丁语“最坏”的最高级构成
items.example: The two words are structured alike: best and worst plus -ism.
items.exampleCN: 这两个词结构相同：最好与最坏各加 -ism。

items.meaning: the condition of being the best available
items.meaningCN: 处于最佳可用状态的性质
items.example: The proof establishes the optimality of the schedule.
items.exampleCN: 该证明确立了这份排程的最优性。

items.meaningCN: 低于最佳标准的；次优的
items.example: The plant runs at suboptimal pressure in summer.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂夏季在次优压力下运行。

definition_zh: 膜；薄膜；细胞膜；隔膜
definition_en: a thin layer of tissue or material that separates two regions or covers a surface
core_image: 一层薄而柔韧的皮，把两边隔开又允许某些东西通过
scene: 这里指「膜」。 The membrane around the cell controls what enters and leaves.
sceneCN: 这里 membrane 指「细胞膜」（第 2 个义项：包围细胞的薄膜）；句意：细胞周围的膜控制物质的进出。

pos.zh: 膜；薄膜；细胞膜；隔膜；（鼓、扬声器的）振动膜

derivatives.zh: 膜的；膜状的
膜的（少用）
小膜
膜结合的
双分子层

senses.title: Thin separating layer
senses.definition: a thin sheet of material that separates two spaces or covers a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把两个空间隔开或覆盖表面的薄片
senses.example: A membrane kept the salt water from mixing with the fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 一层膜阻止盐水与淡水混合。
senses.why: The Latin word named a thin skin, and the core sense remains any thin layer that divides one region from another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指一层薄皮，核心义仍是把两个区域隔开的任何薄层。

senses.title: Cell membrane
senses.definition: the thin layer that surrounds a cell and controls what passes through
senses.definitionCN: 包围细胞并控制物质通过的薄膜
senses.example: The cell membrane is a double layer of lipids.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜是脂质的双层结构。
senses.why: Every cell is separated from its surroundings by a skin, so biology uses the word for the boundary of life itself.
senses.whyCN: 每个细胞都靠一层皮与外界隔开，因此生物学用这个词指生命本身的边界。

senses.title: Mucous membrane
senses.definition: the moist lining of body cavities such as the mouth and nose
senses.definitionCN: 口腔、鼻腔等体腔的湿润内衬
senses.example: The virus enters through the mucous membrane of the nose.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒经由鼻腔的黏膜进入。
senses.why: Anatomy names the lining of a cavity by its thin membranous character, and the fixed phrase mucous membrane marks the wet ones.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按薄而似膜的特征命名体腔内衬，固定说法 mucous membrane 标出其中湿润的那类。

senses.title: Synthetic membrane
senses.definition: a manufactured film used to filter or separate substances
senses.definitionCN: 用于过滤或分离物质的人造薄膜
senses.example: The plant uses a membrane to remove salt from seawater.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂用一层膜从海水中除盐。
senses.why: Engineers copy the biological boundary with synthetic films, and the same word follows the function rather than the material.
senses.whyCN: 工程师用人工薄膜复制生物边界，同一个词跟随的是功能而不是材料。

senses.title: Eardrum
senses.definition: the thin membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound
senses.definitionCN: 耳中随声音振动的薄膜
senses.example: A loud noise can rupture the tympanic membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 巨大的噪声可能震破鼓膜。
senses.why: The eardrum is literally a small stretched membrane, so anatomy borrows the general word without metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 鼓膜字面上就是一张绷紧的小膜，因此解剖学直接借用这个通用词，并不构成比喻。

senses.title: Membrane proteins
senses.definition: the proteins and lipids that make up a biological membrane
senses.definitionCN: 构成生物膜的蛋白质与脂质
senses.example: Membrane proteins pump ions across the bilayer.
senses.exampleCN: 膜蛋白把离子泵过双分子层。
senses.why: Once the membrane is an object, its components need names, and compounds such as membrane protein locate them in that layer.
senses.whyCN: 一旦膜成为对象，它的组成部分就需要名字，membrane protein 这类复合词就把它们定位在这层结构中。

senses.title: Membrane potential
senses.definition: the voltage difference across a biological membrane
senses.definitionCN: 生物膜两侧的电压差
senses.example: The membrane potential changes when an ion channel opens.
senses.exampleCN: 离子通道打开时膜电位会改变。
senses.why: Because a membrane separates two compartments, a difference in charge can build across it, giving the word a physical role.
senses.whyCN: 由于膜把两个隔间分开，电荷差会在它两侧积累，于是这个词有了物理学角色。

senses.title: Tensile structure
senses.definition: a thin fabric or sheet stretched to carry loads in architecture
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中绷紧以承载的薄织物或薄片
senses.example: The stadium roof is a membrane supported by cables.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场的屋顶是由钢索支撑的张拉膜。
senses.why: Architecture uses the word for a surface that works by tension, the same idea of a thin skin doing a structural job.
senses.whyCN: 建筑用这个词指靠张力工作的表面，仍是「一层薄皮承担结构任务」的同一想法。

senses.title: Vibrating diaphragm
senses.definition: the stretched sheet in a drum, speaker or microphone that produces or senses sound
senses.definitionCN: 鼓、扬声器或麦克风中产生或感知声音的绷紧薄片
senses.example: The microphone's membrane moves with the slightest sound.
senses.exampleCN: 麦克风的振动膜会随极轻微的声音移动。
senses.why: A thin sheet stretched over a frame is the physical shape of every drumhead, so the word covers that everyday object too.
senses.whyCN: 绷在框架上的薄片正是每个鼓面的物理形态，因此这个词也涵盖这种日常物件。

intro.en: Membrane is Latin for a thin skin; its link to the word for a limb is plausible but not certain.
intro.cn: membrane 在拉丁语里指一层薄皮；它与表示「肢体」的词的联系看似合理，但并不确定。

items.en: Latin membrana meant a thin skin, parchment or the surface of a body part. English borrowed it in the 15th century for anatomical coverings.
items.cn: 拉丁语 membrana 指薄皮、羊皮纸或身体某部分的表面。英语在 15 世纪借入，用于解剖上的覆盖层。

items.en: Many dictionaries connect membrana with membrum, 'limb, member of the body'. The connection is plausible but not proven, so it is uncertain.
items.cn: 许多词典把 membrana 与 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」联系起来。这一联系看似合理但未被证实，属于来源不确定。

items.en: As microscopy revealed thin boundaries in plants and animals, membrane became the general word for any such layer. Hooke and his contemporaries described membranes in cork and in tissue.
items.cn: 显微镜揭示动植物中的薄边界之后，membrane 成为指这类薄层的通用词。Hooke 及其同代描述了软木与组织中的膜。

items.en: Cell theory gave the cell membrane its modern role as the boundary of the cell. The phrase cell membrane is 19th century or later.
items.cn: 细胞学说赋予细胞膜「细胞边界」的现代角色。cell membrane 这一说法出现于 19 世纪或更晚。

items.en: In the 20th century the lipid bilayer, membrane proteins and membrane potential became standard terms in biophysics.
items.cn: 20 世纪，脂质双分子层、膜蛋白与膜电位成为生物物理学的标准术语。

note.en: The first group separates membrane from words for its material and from the specific cell boundary; the second separates it from other thin layers and coverings.
note.cn: 第一组把 membrane 与指其材料的词以及专指细胞边界的词分开；第二组把它与其它薄层和覆盖物分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of membrane' or 'membrane-like'; membrane is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「膜的」或「膜状的」；membrane 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A person in a group or a limb; it may share a Latin source with membrane, but its meaning is unrelated to thin layers.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体中的成员或肢体；它可能与 membrane 共享拉丁来源，但词义与薄层无关。

entries.definition: A small membrane-like structure in a cell, used in specialist biology; it is not a general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞中膜状的小结构，属于专业生物学术语，不是通用同义词。

entries.definition: A thin layer of any material, often on a surface; a membrane usually separates two spaces and has a function.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何材料的薄层，常附在表面；membrane 通常分隔两个空间并具有功能。

entries.definition: A layer covering the inside of something; a mucous membrane is a lining, but not every lining is a membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖在内部的一层；黏膜是一种内衬，但不是所有内衬都是膜。

entries.definition: Anything that blocks movement; a membrane can act as a barrier but may also let selected substances through.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻挡运动的东西；膜可以起屏障作用，但也可能让特定物质通过。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin membrana 'thin skin': a sheet that separates two spaces.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 membrana「薄皮」：把两个空间隔开的一层薄片。

normal.en: The family runs membranous, membranal, membranelle, membrane-bound and bilayer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 membranous、membranal、membranelle、membrane-bound、bilayer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cell membrane, mucous membrane, tympanic membrane, semipermeable membrane.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细胞膜、黏膜、鼓膜、半透膜。

normal.en: The same word covers a soap bubble film, an eardrum and a stadium roof.
normal.cn: 同一个词涵盖肥皂泡的薄膜、鼓膜与体育场屋顶。

normal.en: A membrane is defined by being thin and by separating something.
normal.cn: 膜的定义特征就是薄，并且把某物隔开。

abstract.en: A membrane is a border checkpoint: it does not just block, it chooses.
abstract.cn: 膜像一个边境检查站：它不只是阻挡，还会选择。

abstract.en: Think of a drum: a stretched skin turns a hit into a sound, and a cell membrane turns a signal into a response.
abstract.cn: 想象一面鼓：绷紧的皮把敲击变成声音，细胞膜则把信号变成反应。

abstract.en: A stadium roof is a membrane holding up the sky, the same thin sheet doing a structural job.
abstract.cn: 体育场屋顶像一层托住天空的膜，同样是薄片承担结构任务。

examples.en: The cell membrane controls which ions enter the cell.
examples.cn: 细胞膜控制哪些离子进入细胞。

examples.en: A semipermeable membrane lets water through but holds salt back.
examples.cn: 半透膜让水通过，却把盐挡住。

examples.en: The mucous membrane of the nose traps dust and viruses.
examples.cn: 鼻腔黏膜会截留灰尘与病毒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「membrane 像一层薄皮」→ 把两边隔开的薄膜 → 细胞膜、黏膜、隔膜

root: 拉丁语 membrana「薄皮、羊皮纸」→ 英语 membrane；与 membrum「肢体」的联系看似合理但未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all describe a thin layer with a job: separating, covering, filtering, vibrating, or carrying a voltage. The cell membrane, mucous lining, filter, eardrum, roof and drumhead are all the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都描述一层有任务的薄层：分隔、覆盖、过滤、振动或承载电压。细胞膜、黏膜、滤膜、鼓膜、屋顶与鼓面都是同一种形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin flexible skin that separates two sides and lets some things through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄而有弹性的皮，把两边隔开，允许某些东西通过。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LAYER: any thin sheet that divides two regions.
branches.cn: 一般薄层：任何把两个区域分开的薄片。

branches.en: THE CELL BOUNDARY: the membrane itself, its proteins, and the voltage across it.
branches.cn: 细胞边界：膜本身、它的蛋白，以及跨膜的电压。

branches.en: ANATOMICAL LINING: the wet membrane covering a body cavity.
branches.cn: 解剖内衬：覆盖体腔的湿润薄膜。

branches.en: FUNCTIONAL SHEETS: synthetic filters and the eardrum.
branches.cn: 功能性薄片：人工滤膜与鼓膜。

branches.en: ENGINEERED AND VIBRATING: tensile roofs and the stretched diaphragm of instruments.
branches.cn: 工程与振动：张拉屋顶与乐器、麦克风的绷紧膜片。

intro.en: Membrane is a Latin noun with no prefix; its family is built with -ous, -al and the diminutive -elle.
intro.cn: membrane 是不带前缀的拉丁名词；其词族由 -ous、-al 与指小后缀 -elle 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrana supplies the root; the adjective ending -ous comes from Latin -osus, and -elle is a French/Latin diminutive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 membrana 提供词根；形容词词尾 -ous 来自拉丁语 -osus，-elle 是法语与拉丁语的指小成分。

items.example: The membrane is only a few molecules thick.
items.exampleCN: 这层膜只有几个分子厚。

items.example: The tissue has a membranous cover.
items.exampleCN: 该组织有一层膜状覆盖。

items.example: Membranal proteins differ from soluble ones.
items.exampleCN: 膜蛋白与可溶性蛋白不同。

items.example: The membranelle beats water toward the mouth.
items.exampleCN: 小膜把水扇向口部。

items.meaning: attached to or enclosed by a membrane
items.meaningCN: 附着于膜或被膜包围的
items.example: Membrane-bound receptors sit at the surface.
items.exampleCN: 膜结合受体位于表面。

items.example: The lipid bilayer forms the cell membrane.
items.exampleCN: 脂质双分子层构成细胞膜。

items.example: The membrane is permeable to water.
items.exampleCN: 该膜对水是可透的。

items.example: The cuticle is impermeable to water.
items.exampleCN: 表皮对水不可透。

items.example: The mucous membrane secretes mucus.
items.exampleCN: 黏膜分泌黏液。

definition_zh: 触发；引发；激起；扳机；触发器；诱因
definition_en: to cause something to start suddenly, and the small lever or device that sets a mechanism going
core_image: 靶场上，一根手指搭在扳机上，只要一个很小的动作，整支枪的力量就会释放
scene: 靶场上，一根手指搭在扳机上，只要一个很小的动作，整支枪的力量就会释放。 A single spark was enough to trigger the alarm.
sceneCN: 这里指引发、触发（第 1 个义项：使某事突然开始）；句意为一个火花就足以触发警报。

pos.zh: 触发；引发；激起
扳机；触发器；诱因

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「触发；引发性的」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「被触发的；受激的」
由该名词与表示「热衷」的形容词合成为复合形容词，义为「动辄开枪的；莽撞行事的」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被触发的」

senses.title: Cause an event to begin suddenly
senses.definition: to set off an event or a chain of events that would not have started by itself
senses.definitionCN: 使一个本不会自行开始的事件或连锁事件开始
senses.example: A small error can trigger a chain of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小错误就可能引发一连串故障。
senses.why: The word began as the small lever that releases a gun, and the idea of a little act releasing a large force is the heart of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指释放枪械力量的小杠杆，而「一个小动作释放巨大力量」正是每个义项的核心。

senses.title: Provoke a strong feeling
senses.definition: to cause anger, fear or excitement in a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 引起个人或群体的愤怒、恐惧或激动
senses.example: The news triggered an angry response from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那条消息激起人群的愤怒回应。
senses.why: A feeling that was quiet suddenly fires, and the word pictures it as a mechanism released by a small event.
senses.whyCN: 原本安静的情绪突然开火，这个词把它画成被小事释放的机械。

senses.title: Set a device into operation
senses.definition: to make a sensor, circuit or machine begin working, often automatically
senses.definitionCN: 使传感器、电路或机器开始工作，常为自动进行
senses.example: The sensor triggers the lamp when someone walks past.
senses.exampleCN: 有人走过时，传感器就会触发那盏灯。
senses.why: This is the most literal modern sense: a small signal releases a larger action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的现代义：一个小信号释放一个更大的动作。

senses.title: Induce an illness or symptom
senses.definition: in medicine, to cause a disease, attack or symptom to begin
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指引起疾病、发作或症状开始
senses.example: The virus can trigger a high fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒能引发高烧。
senses.why: A body already carrying a condition may need only one small provocation, and the word names that provocation.
senses.whyCN: 身体本就带着病因，也许只差一个很小的刺激，而这个词命名的正是那个刺激。

senses.title: The lever on a firearm
senses.definition: the small lever a finger pulls to fire a gun
senses.definitionCN: 手指扣动以使枪械击发的小杠杆
senses.example: He kept his finger off the trigger until the order came.
senses.exampleCN: 在命令下达之前，他的手指一直没有放在扳机上。
senses.why: This is the sense from which every other sense borrows its shape: the smallest part controls the largest release.
senses.whyCN: 这是其他所有义项借取形状的源头义：最小的部件控制最大的释放。

senses.title: An electronic pulse that starts an action
senses.titleCN: 电子触发器或触发脉冲
senses.definition: a signal in a circuit that tells another part to begin its cycle
senses.definitionCN: 电路中通知另一部件开始运行周期的信号
senses.example: The circuit sends a trigger to the camera every two seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 电路每隔两秒向相机发送一个触发信号。
senses.why: Electronics kept the gun image and made the lever invisible: a pulse instead of a finger.
senses.whyCN: 电子学保留了枪的意象，却把杠杆变得看不见：用脉冲代替手指。

senses.title: The cause or occasion of an event
senses.definition: the event or remark that was the immediate occasion for something larger
senses.definitionCN: 成为更大事件的直接起因的事件或言论
senses.example: The report was the trigger for a wider debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告成了更广泛争论的诱因。
senses.why: In this noun sense the lever becomes the occasion itself, the point at which the mechanism was released.
senses.whyCN: 在这个名词义项里，杠杆变成了事件本身，即机械被释放的那一刻。

senses.title: Bring a memory back
senses.definition: to cause a scene, smell or sound to bring an old memory into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 使景象、气味或声音把旧日记忆带回心中
senses.example: The smell of bread triggered a memory of his grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的气味唤起了他对祖母厨房的记忆。
senses.why: A memory sits loaded like a spring, and one small sensory cue can release it whole.
senses.whyCN: 记忆像上了弦的弹簧，一个小小的感官线索就能把它整个释放。

senses.title: Set off a biological response
senses.definition: to start an allergic, immune or inflammatory reaction in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 在生物体内引起过敏、免疫或炎症反应
senses.example: The pollen may trigger an allergic reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉可能引发过敏反应。
senses.why: The body is the machine here, and the allergen is the finger on the lever.
senses.whyCN: 这里的机器是身体，而过敏原就是搭在杠杆上的那根手指。

intro.en: Trigger is a Dutch loan. It comes from trekker, a puller, from trekken, to pull, and it entered English first as a name for the lever of a firearm.
intro.cn: 这个词借自荷兰语，来自 trekker「拉者」，而 trekker 出自 trekken「拉」；它进入英语时最先指枪械上的杠杆。

items.en: Trekken meant to pull or draw, and it is also the source of the English word trek, a long journey drawn out by oxen.
items.cn: trekken 意为拉、拖，它也是英语 trek「长途跋涉」的来源，那正是牛车拉出来的路。

items.en: The noun meant one that pulls, and it could name a person, a rope or a part of a machine.
items.cn: 这个名词意为「拉的东西」，可以指人、指绳，也可以指机器部件。
