items.en: The earliest English form was tricker, recorded in the sixteenth century for the lever of a gun; the spelling was not yet fixed.
items.cn: 最早的英语形式是 tricker，十六世纪时用来指枪的杠杆；当时拼写尚未固定。

items.en: The modern spelling settled in the seventeenth century, still tied to firearms before it moved to any small releasing part.
items.cn: 现代拼写在十七世纪固定下来，仍先与枪械绑定，之后才转向任何小的释放部件。

items.en: Machines and then circuits borrowed the word for any small part that starts a larger motion.
items.cn: 机器、随后是电路，都借这个词来指任何启动更大运动的细小部件。

items.en: Psychology and medicine extended it to memories, emotions and symptoms, where a small cue releases a large response.
items.cn: 心理学与医学把它扩展到记忆、情绪与症状，那里一个小小的线索就释放出很大的反应。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like trigger; the second group names neighbouring ways of starting something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 trigger 相近；第二组是与「引发、启动」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of setting something off, or the quality of doing so.
entries.definitionCN: 指触发的行为，或指具有引发作用的性质。

entries.definition: Set off or activated by something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指被某物触发或激活的。

entries.definition: Too ready to shoot or to act rashly.
entries.definitionCN: 指动辄开枪或鲁莽行事的。

entries.definition: A large striped cat; it looks close in spelling but has no shared history.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种大型条纹猫科动物；拼写相近，但没有共同来源。

entries.definition: To flow in a thin stream; it sounds close but comes from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指细细地流；读音相近，但来自另一个动词。

entries.definition: To make something happen; neutral about size and speed, and the broadest word here.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事发生；不涉及大小与速度，是这里最宽泛的词。

entries.definition: To stir a feeling or a reaction, often deliberately; it stresses the irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 指激起情绪或反应，常含故意；强调被激起的恼怒。

entries.definition: To start something large from a very small beginning, with the image of a spark and dry grass.
entries.definitionCN: 指由极小的开端引发大事，意象是火星与干草。

entries.definition: To start a device, alarm or chain of events; plainer and more physical than trigger.
entries.definitionCN: 指启动装置、警报或一连串事件；比本词更朴素、更物理。

entries.definition: To begin something formally or deliberately, without the idea of a small lever.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式或有意地开始某事，不含「小杠杆」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pulling root, the gun lever and the small-cause-large-effect pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「拉」的词根、枪的杠杆，以及「小原因、大效果」的模式。

normal.en: The Dutch root means pull, so the trigger is the part you pull to release everything else.
normal.cn: 荷兰语词根意为拉，所以扳机就是你拉一下、其余一切随之释放的那个部件。

normal.en: A finger moves a few millimetres and the whole gun answers; that is the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 手指移动几毫米，整支枪都作出回应；这就是这个词的形状。

normal.en: A smoke detector is a trigger made electronic: a little smoke, a loud alarm.
normal.cn: 烟雾报警器就是电子化的扳机：一点烟，一阵大响。

normal.en: A smell that brings back a kitchen is the same mechanism working on memory.
normal.cn: 让厨房重现的气味，是同一套机械在记忆上工作。

normal.en: The stock phrase pull the trigger keeps the original object visible inside the modern verb.
normal.cn: 固定说法「扣动扳机」让原本的物件在现代动词里仍然可见。

abstract.en: A trigger is defined by the ratio between the small input and the large release.
abstract.cn: 扳机的本质，在于小输入与大释放之间的比例。

abstract.en: The same event can be a trigger for one person and a trifle for another, because the mechanism is inside.
abstract.cn: 同一件事对一个人是扳机，对另一个人却无关紧要，因为机械装在内部。

abstract.en: Naming a trigger is already a way of taking some power back from it.
abstract.cn: 说出一个触发点，本身已经是从它手里收回一部分权力。

examples.en: The ruling triggered protests across the country.
examples.cn: 那项裁决引发了全国范围的抗议。

examples.en: A loud noise can trigger a panic attack.
examples.cn: 巨大的声响可能引发惊恐发作。

examples.en: The alarm was triggered by a broken wire.
examples.cn: 警报是被一根断线触发的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「吹格」——手指一「吹」，扳机一「格」响，整支枪就响了：扳机、触发

root: 荷兰语 trekken「拉」→ trekker「拉者、拉动的部件」→ 英语早期形式 tricker（十六世纪指枪的杠杆）→ trigger「扳机」→ 动词「触发、引发」；核心是「一个很小的拉动释放很大的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all follow one pattern, a small act releasing a large response: events, feelings, devices, illness, the gun lever itself, circuits, occasions, memories and allergic reactions.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都遵循同一个模式——小动作释放大反应：事件、情绪、装置、疾病、枪的杠杆本身、电路、诱因、记忆与过敏反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger on a small lever, and the whole weapon answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指搭在小杠杆上，整件武器随之响应。

branches.en: THE RELEASE BRANCH: one error starts a chain, and one allergen starts a reaction.
branches.cn: 释放分支：一个错误引发连锁，一个过敏原引发反应。

branches.en: THE INNER BRANCH: a piece of news fires anger, and a smell fires a memory.
branches.cn: 内部分支：一条消息点燃愤怒，一种气味点燃记忆。

branches.en: THE MACHINE BRANCH: a sensor starts a lamp, and a pulse starts a camera.
branches.cn: 机械分支：传感器启动灯，脉冲启动相机。

branches.en: THE ILLNESS BRANCH: a virus provokes a fever in a body already carrying it.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：病毒在本已带病的身体里诱发高烧。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN BRANCH: the gun lever itself, and the occasion that releases a debate.
branches.cn: 源头分支：枪的杠杆本身，以及释放一场争论的诱因。

intro.en: Trigger is not a Latin word at all: it is a Dutch loan whose parts are a verb of pulling and an agent ending.
intro.cn: 这个词根本不是拉丁词，而是一个荷兰语借词，其部件是一个表示「拉」的动词和一个施动词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon behind this word. Its family is Germanic, and the Latin entries are therefore left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁语词源，它属于日耳曼语族，因此拉丁语条目留空。

items.example: The pulling action is the physical core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 「拉」这个动作是这个词的物理核心。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun for the thing that pulls.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指「拉动之物」的名词。

items.example: The Dutch noun named the part that sets a mechanism going.
items.exampleCN: 这个荷兰语名词命名启动机械的那个部件。

items.example: English took the Dutch noun and narrowed it to the gun part.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入这个荷兰语名词，并把意义收窄到枪的部件。

items.structure: English conversion from noun to verb
items.example: English turned the part into an action without adding an ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个部件直接变成动作，没有加任何词尾。

items.example: The compound keeps the gun sense alive in ordinary speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词让枪的义项在日常说法里继续存活。

items.example: It forms triggered, the past and participle of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triggered，即该动词的过去式与过去分词。

items.meaning: ongoing action, or the act itself
items.meaningCN: 正在进行的动作，或行为本身
items.example: It forms triggering, both participle and verbal noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triggering，既是分词也是动名词。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「触发；引发性的」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「被触发的；受激的」
由该名词与表示「热衷」的形容词合成为复合形容词，义为「动辄开枪的；莽撞行事的」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被触发的」

definition_zh: 恒星的；星体的；极好的；明星级的；星形的
definition_en: relating to stars, or (informally) outstanding and excellent
core_image: 一台望远镜对准一小片天区，屏幕上的光点被拆成温度、质量与年龄三条曲线
scene: 评价一场几乎无懈可击的演出，你说 Her performance was stellar.
sceneCN: 这里 stellar 是引申义「极好的、出色的」（第 3 个义项：由「恒星般明亮」转为对质量的评价）；句意为她的演出极为出色。图中可辨识物件：舞台、聚光灯、评分表、满格星标。

pos.zh: 恒星的；星体的；（口语）极好的；星形的

derivatives.zh: inter- + stellar：星际的；前缀表「在……之间」
non- + stellar：非恒星的；前缀表否定
stella + -ate：星形的；后缀表「具有……形状」
-tor 表装置：仿星器，一种受控核聚变装置；词干取 stellar 的「恒星」义

senses.title: Of or relating to stars
senses.definition: relating to stars in general
senses.definitionCN: 泛指与恒星有关的
senses.example: Stellar astronomy studies how stars are born and die.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星天文学研究恒星如何诞生与死亡。
senses.why: stellar is simply the Latin adjective of stella, so its first duty is to stand beside any noun about stars.
senses.whyCN: stellar 就是 stella 的拉丁形容词，因此它的首要职责是为任何与恒星有关的名词作定语。

senses.title: Of a star's physical nature
senses.titleCN: 恒星自身的物理性质与演化
senses.definition: describing the measurable properties of a star, such as its mass, temperature or evolutionary stage
senses.definitionCN: 描述恒星可测的性质，如质量、温度或演化阶段
senses.example: Stellar mass decides how a star will end.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星质量决定一颗恒星将如何终结。
senses.why: once astronomers could measure stars, the adjective attached itself to the quantities that define them.
senses.whyCN: 当天文学家能测量恒星之后，这个形容词就附着在定义恒星的那些量上。

senses.title: Outstanding, excellent
senses.definition: extremely good; excellent, especially in performance or quality
senses.definitionCN: 极好的；尤指表现或质量出色
senses.example: Her performance was stellar.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演出极为出色。
senses.why: the praise sense is figurative: something stellar shines like a star compared with everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 这层赞美义是比喻：某物与周围相比，亮得像一颗星。

senses.title: Of a star-studded cast
senses.titleCN: 明星云集的；由明星组成的
senses.definition: featuring famous performers; used of a cast or lineup
senses.definitionCN: 由著名表演者组成的；用于阵容
senses.example: The film drew a stellar cast of stage actors.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片召集了一批明星级的舞台演员。
senses.why: the sky image slides from real stars to stage stars, and the adjective follows the same path as the noun star.
senses.whyCN: 天空的意象从真星滑向舞台明星，形容词与名词 star 走的是同一条路。

senses.title: Star-shaped
senses.definition: shaped like a star, with radiating points, as some hairs or crystals
senses.definitionCN: 形状像星、带放射状尖角的，如某些毛发或晶体
senses.example: The leaf surface is covered with stellar hairs.
senses.exampleCN: 叶面覆盖着星状毛。
senses.why: this sense keeps the oldest visual meaning of stella, the drawn or natural shape with rays.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了 stella 最古老的视觉含义：带放射线的画成或天然形状。

senses.title: Of a star's emitted material
senses.titleCN: 恒星喷出的物质与辐射
senses.definition: describing matter or radiation flowing out from a star, as in stellar wind
senses.definitionCN: 描述从恒星流出的物质或辐射，如星风
senses.example: The stellar wind strips the planet of its atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 星风把行星的大气剥走。
senses.why: wind and radiation are properties of the star in action, so the adjective marks them as coming from the star rather than from elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 风与辐射是恒星在活动时的表现，因此这个形容词标明它们来自恒星而非别处。

senses.title: Of a star-forming region
senses.definition: describing the clouds and regions where new stars are forming
senses.definitionCN: 描述正在形成新恒星的云气与区域
senses.example: Dust hides the young stars inside the stellar nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 尘埃遮住了恒星育婴室里年轻的恒星。
senses.why: a nursery is where new lives begin, so astronomers borrowed the domestic word and kept the adjective to mark what is being born.
senses.whyCN: 育婴室是新生命开始之处，天文学家借来这个日常词，并保留形容词以标明诞生的是恒星。

senses.title: Radiant, shining (literary)
senses.definition: shining or radiant in a literary description, often of light or a smile
senses.definitionCN: 文学描写中光辉四射的，常用于光或笑容
senses.example: A stellar glow filled the hall as the lamps were lit.
senses.exampleCN: 灯点亮时，一片星光般的光辉充满大厅。
senses.why: the literal shine and the figurative praise meet here: what shines is praised for shining.
senses.whyCN: 字面的「发光」与比喻的「赞美」在此会合：发光者因发光而被称赞。

intro.en: Stellar is Latin stellaris 'of stars', built on stella 'star' with the adjective suffix -aris. It entered English as an astronomical adjective and later acquired a colloquial sense of excellence. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stellar 是拉丁 stellaris「恒星的」，由 stella「星」加形容词后缀 -aris 构成。它作为天文学形容词进入英语，后来又获得「出色」的口语义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stella 'star' is the Latin noun, a cognate of English star and Greek aster rather than their source; all go back to a reconstructed Indo-European root.
items.cn: stella 是拉丁语「星」，与英语 star、希腊 aster 属同源，而非它们的来源；三者都出自一个印欧重构词根。

items.en: Stella plus -aris produced stellaris 'of stars', the ordinary adjective used with such nouns as stellarum motus 'motion of the stars'.
items.cn: stella 加 -aris 构成 stellaris「恒星的」，是与「星的运动」等短语搭配的普通形容词。

items.en: The adjective is generally believed to have entered English astronomical writing in the seventeenth century, alongside other Latin scientific adjectives.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个形容词在 17 世纪随其他拉丁科学形容词一起进入英语天文写作。

items.en: The informal sense 'outstanding' is nineteenth-century and later; it extends the literal shine of a star to any performance that seems to outshine its surroundings.
items.cn: 「出色」的口语义出现于 19 世纪及以后；它把恒星字面的光亮扩展到任何看似盖过周围的表现。

items.en: The star-shaped sense is also nineteenth-century, when descriptive botany borrowed stellar for radiating hairs and crystals.
items.cn: 星形义同样出现于 19 世纪，当时描述性植物学借 stellar 指放射状的毛与晶体。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European form behind stella is a reconstruction. First-date uncertainty only: the earliest use of the praise sense is not exactly dated and is usually placed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 词根存疑：stella 背后的印欧形式属重构。仅首见年代存疑：赞美义的最早用例没有确切年代，通常定在 19 世纪。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns of the same star stock that are easily confused; group two holds the ordinary words that compete with the praise sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「星」词干、容易混淆的形容词与名词；第二组是与「出色」义竞争的普通词。

entries.definition: From Latin stellatus 'set with stars', it means shaped like a star and is used in botany; it does not mean 'of stars'.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 stellatus「布满星」，意为星形的，用于植物学；它不表示「恒星的」。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus stellar: it names the space or matter between stars, not a quality of a single star.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「在……之间」加 stellar：指恒星之间的空间或物质，而非单颗恒星的性质。

entries.definition: The noun names the body itself; stellar is only the adjective, so a sentence needs star where a thing is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指天体本身；stellar 只是形容词，指「东西」时须用 star。

entries.definition: The neutral, everyday word for very good; stellar is informal and adds the image of shining.
entries.definitionCN: 中性、日常的「很好」；stellar 属口语并多了「发光」的意象。

entries.definition: Praise for being clearly above others; it stresses comparison, while stellar stresses brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 赞扬明显高于其余；它强调比较，而 stellar 强调光亮。

entries.definition: From Greek astron 'star'; it belongs to astrology and esoteric writing, where stellar belongs to physics and praise.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 astron「星」；多用于占星与秘学文本，而 stellar 用于物理与赞美。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: stella 'star' + -ar 'of': of a star.
normal.cn: stella「星」+ -ar「……的」：星的。

normal.en: Physics collocations: stellar mass, stellar wind, stellar evolution.
normal.cn: 物理搭配：恒星质量、星风、恒星演化。

normal.en: Praise collocations: a stellar performance, a stellar cast.
normal.cn: 赞美搭配：出色的演出、明星阵容。

normal.en: The same stock gives constellation and interstellar.
normal.cn: 同一词干还给出 constellation 与 interstellar。

normal.en: Stellate means star-shaped, not of stars.
normal.cn: stellate 意为星形，不是「恒星的」。

abstract.en: Picture a single lamp so bright that everything else in the room looks grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯亮到房间里其他东西都显得灰暗。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard where one name is printed larger than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌，其中一个名字印得比别的大。

abstract.en: Picture a crystal cut into rays around a centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一块晶体围绕中心被切成放射状。

examples.en: Stellar evolution depends on how much gas the cloud contains.
examples.cn: 恒星演化取决于云气含有多少物质。

examples.en: The orchestra gave a stellar performance on opening night.
examples.cn: 乐团在首演夜献上极为出色的演出。

examples.en: Stellar parallax is the tiny shift seen as the earth moves.
examples.cn: 恒星视差是地球移动时看到的微小位移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stellar」听着像「是他了」——全场最亮的那颗星「是他了」 → 恒星的；出色的

root: 拉丁 stella「星」+ -aris「……的」→ stellaris「恒星的」；stella 与英语 star、希腊 aster 同源，印欧词根属重构形式；「出色」义一般认为始于 19 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: the literal 'of a star' is applied to a star's physics, its wind, its nursery and its shape, and then the same brightness is borrowed for a great performance, a famous cast and even a literary glow.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词展开：字面的「恒星的」依次用于恒星的物理、星风、育婴区与形状；随后同样的「亮」被借去形容出色的演出、明星阵容，乃至文学描写中的光辉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp so bright that the rest of the room falls into grey.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯亮到房间里其余一切都落进灰色。

branches.en: THE PLAIN ADJECTIVE: it belongs to any noun about stars.
branches.cn: 普通定语：可与任何关于恒星的名词搭配。

branches.en: THE STAR AT WORK: what it is made of, what it blows out, where it is born.
branches.cn: 工作中的恒星：由什么构成、吹出什么、在哪里诞生。

branches.en: THE DRAWN SHAPE: rays around a centre, not a body in space.
branches.cn: 画出的形状：围绕中心的射线，而非天上的天体。

branches.en: PRAISE: a performance that outshines its surroundings.
branches.cn: 赞美：盖过周围的表现。

branches.en: BORROWED BRIGHTNESS: famous faces and literary glow.
branches.cn: 借来的光：明星面孔与文学中的光辉。

intro.en: Stellar is a Latin root plus adjective suffix; the root also builds several nouns and verbs through the same stella.
intro.cn: stellar 是拉丁词根加形容词后缀；这个词根还经同一个 stella 构成若干名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stella gives stellar, stellate, constellation and stellify; Greek aster gives astral and asteroid, a parallel family rather than the same one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stella 给出 stellar、stellate、constellation、stellify；希腊 aster 给出 astral 与 asteroid，是并行词族而非同一族。

items.example: Stella is a cognate, not the source, of English star.
items.exampleCN: stella 是英语 star 的同源词，不是来源。

items.example: Stellaris is stella plus this suffix.
items.exampleCN: stellaris 就是 stella 加这个后缀。

items.example: The adjective entered English through scientific Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经科学拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: Botany uses it for radiating hairs.
items.exampleCN: 植物学用它指放射状毛。

items.example: The noun names a group, not a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指一群，而非一种性质。

items.example: It names the space between stars.
items.exampleCN: 它指恒星之间的空间。

items.example: The prefix reverses the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀反转了形容词。

items.example: Rare, but built on the same root.
items.exampleCN: 罕见，但同出这一词根。

items.example: The device is named for the stellar plasma it mimics.
items.exampleCN: 这种装置因模仿恒星等离子体而得名。

definition_zh: 依赖；依靠；取决于；信赖；指望
definition_en: to rely on something for support or survival, to be decided by a condition, or to trust a person
core_image: 一只吊篮用一根绳子挂在梁上，篮里的重量一增，绳子就绷紧，梁也跟着微微下沉
scene: 果园主人蹲在干裂的土上，抬头看天，又翻看手机里的降雨预报。 The size of the crop may depend on rain in the next three weeks.
sceneCN: 这里指收成多少由某个条件决定（第 2 个义项：结果取决于某一因素）；句意为收成的大小可能取决于未来三周的降雨。图中可辨识物件：干裂的土、果树、降雨预报、水桶。

pos.zh: 依赖；依靠（不及物动词短语加介词，后接所依靠的人或物）
取决于；视……而定（后接条件、变量或情况）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「依赖；依靠」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「依赖的；受扶养者」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可靠的」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「独立的」
由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「依附关系；属地」

senses.title: Rely on for survival
senses.definition: to need something in order to live or to keep operating
senses.definitionCN: 为了生存或继续运转而需要某物
senses.example: The village must depend on the spring for drinking water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄必须依靠那眼泉水取饮用水。
senses.why: The core verb meant to hang from something; what hangs from a support cannot stand without it.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「从某物上悬垂」；挂在支撑物上的东西，离开它便立不住。

senses.title: Be decided by a condition
senses.definition: to have one's outcome fixed by a stated factor
senses.definitionCN: 结果由某一明确因素决定
senses.example: The harvest can depend on two weeks of dry weather in June.
senses.exampleCN: 收成可能取决于六月里连续两周的干燥天气。
senses.why: What hangs from a support has its place fixed by that support, so a harvest hangs from rain.
senses.whyCN: 挂在支撑上的东西，位置由支撑决定，因此收成挂在雨上。

senses.title: Trust a person
senses.definition: to place one's confidence in someone's reliability
senses.definitionCN: 把信心放在某人的可靠之上
senses.example: Readers should depend on the handbook only after checking its sources.
senses.exampleCN: 读者只有在核对手册的来源之后，才应信赖它。
senses.why: Trust is hanging one's confidence on another person's reliability.
senses.whyCN: 信赖，是把信心挂在另一个人的可靠上。

senses.title: Rely economically
senses.definition: to have one's income or livelihood tied to one source
senses.definitionCN: 收入或生计系于单一来源
senses.example: The island may depend on a single crop for most of its income.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛可能依赖单一作物获取大部分收入。
senses.why: A single crop is a single rope holding an island's income.
senses.whyCN: 单一作物就是吊住整岛收入的一根绳子。

senses.title: Rely on a habitat
senses.definition: to survive only in a particular environment
senses.definitionCN: 只能在特定环境中存活
senses.example: The beetle can depend on one kind of rotting log.
senses.exampleCN: 这种甲虫可能只依赖一种腐木生存。
senses.why: A beetle hangs from one kind of log, and nowhere else holds it up.
senses.whyCN: 甲虫挂在一种腐木上，别处托不住它。

senses.title: Vary with a variable
senses.definition: to change in value as another measured quantity changes
senses.definitionCN: 数值随另一测量量的变化而变化
senses.example: The measured rate should depend on temperature and pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 测得的速率应随温度与压力而变化。
senses.why: A measured rate hangs from the conditions that set it.
senses.whyCN: 测得的速率挂在决定它的那些条件上。

senses.title: Be conditional in planning
senses.definition: to remain undecided until a future condition is known
senses.definitionCN: 在未来的条件明确之前不作定论
senses.example: The launch may depend on the wind at the pad.
senses.exampleCN: 发射可能要看发射台上的风况而定。
senses.why: A launch hangs from the wind at the pad, a condition not yet known.
senses.whyCN: 发射挂在发射台的风况上，而那条件尚未可知。

senses.title: Rely on a substance
senses.definition: to be unable to function without a drug or a habit
senses.definitionCN: 离开某种药物或习惯便无法正常运转
senses.example: Patients should not depend on sleeping pills for more than a month.
senses.exampleCN: 患者不应连续一个多月依赖安眠药。
senses.why: A sleeper hangs from a pill when the body can no longer hold the night alone.
senses.whyCN: 当身体无法独自撑过夜晚，睡眠就挂在药片上。

senses.title: Count on someone to act
senses.definition: to expect a person to perform a task one needs done
senses.definitionCN: 期待某人去完成自己需要完成的事
senses.example: The committee must depend on volunteers to staff the doors.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会必须依靠志愿者来守门。
senses.why: A committee hangs from volunteers when no one is paid to stand at the door.
senses.whyCN: 没有人领薪守门时，委员会就挂在志愿者身上。

intro.en: The phrase centres on a Latin verb meaning to hang down from something. Every sense keeps the picture of a weight suspended: what hangs needs the thing it hangs from, and its position is fixed by that support.
intro.cn: 这个短语的核心是拉丁语中表示「从某物下垂」的动词。每个义项都保留「重物悬垂」的画面：挂着的东西需要所挂之处，它的位置也由那个支撑决定。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang, to weigh, and it stands behind pendant, suspend and pendulum.
items.cn: 这个词意为「悬挂、称重」，吊坠、悬停与摆锤诸词都由它而来。

items.en: De- 'down from' plus pendere produced dependere, to hang from something, to be attached to it.
items.cn: 表示「自下」的前缀加「悬挂」，构成「挂在某物上、附着于它」的动词。

items.en: Old French carried the verb with the sense of being subject to another's will.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入「受他人意志支配」的意思。

items.en: English took it first for being sustained by something, then for being decided by a condition.
items.cn: 英语最初用它表示「由某物支撑」，随后表示「由某条件决定」。

items.en: The frame with on fixed in the following centuries for support, condition and trust alike. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 与介词搭配的框架在此后几个世纪固定下来，兼指支撑、条件与信任。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin hanging verb; the second group holds other verbs of relying or being decided.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「悬挂」动词；第二组是其他表示「依靠」或「由……决定」的动词。

entries.definition: It describes a person or thing that relies on another; the phrase states the reliance as an action.
entries.definitionCN: 它形容依赖他人的人或物；短语则把这种依赖说成一个动作。

entries.definition: The noun names the state of relying; it cannot take the specific condition as its object.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「依赖的状态」，不能像短语那样带出具体的条件。

entries.definition: It says that nothing hangs from another support, the exact reverse of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不挂在别的支撑上，正是本短语的反面。

entries.definition: From the same hanging verb, it means awaiting a decision; it shares the image but not the reliance.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「悬挂」动词，意为「待决的」；共享意象，却不含「依靠」。

entries.definition: It stresses confidence in the support, and is common for people and services rather than for equations.
entries.definitionCN: 强调对支撑的信心，多用于人与服务，少用于方程式。

entries.definition: It adds the note of expecting a person to act; the phrase can mean this but does not stress expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 多一层「期待某人行动」的意思；本短语可含此义，但不强调期待。

entries.definition: A vivid phrase for an outcome that turns on a single factor, as a door turns on a hinge.
entries.definitionCN: 形象地表示结果系于单一因素，如门绕铰链转动。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for a result that follows only if a condition holds; it is limited to the conditional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式表示「只有在某条件成立时结果才成立」，只覆盖条件义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the hanging basket, the dry field, the sleeping pill and the volunteer at the door.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用吊篮、干裂的田、安眠药与守门的志愿者四个场景。

normal.en: A basket hung from a beam: add weight and the rope tightens and the beam dips.
normal.cn: 篮子挂在梁上：加重一点，绳就绷紧，梁也下沉。

normal.en: A cracked field, a rain forecast, and a farmer doing arithmetic in his head.
normal.cn: 干裂的田、一份降雨预报，农夫在心里算账。

normal.en: One beetle, one kind of rotting log, nowhere else to go.
normal.cn: 一种甲虫，一种腐木，别处无处可去。

normal.en: A pill that must be taken or the night does not end.
normal.cn: 一片必须吃的药，不吃夜就到不了头。

normal.en: A volunteer standing at the door because no one is paid to.
normal.cn: 志愿者守在门口，因为没有人是领薪的。

abstract.en: To depend is to have one's position fixed by something outside oneself.
abstract.cn: 依赖，就是自己的位置由身外之物决定。

abstract.en: Every support is also a limit: what holds you up decides how far you can move.
abstract.cn: 每个支撑同时是限制：托住你的东西，也决定你能走多远。

abstract.en: The same hanging image covers water, weather, trust and truth, because all of them hold something up.
abstract.cn: 同一个「悬挂」意象覆盖水、天气、信任与真值，因为它们都托着某物。

examples.en: Coastal cities may depend on desalination if the rivers keep shrinking.
examples.cn: 若河流继续萎缩，沿海城市可能依赖海水淡化。

examples.en: The final cost should depend on how much material is reused.
examples.cn: 最终成本应取决于有多少材料被再利用。

examples.en: A referee must depend on the linesman's view of the touchline.
examples.cn: 裁判必须依靠边裁对边线的判断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪彭德 昂」：把「悬挂」记成吊篮挂在梁上——绳在梁上，篮才不落地，这就是依赖

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语，由表示「自下」的前缀加表示「悬挂、称重」的动词构成，本义是「挂在某物上」，引申为「依靠、由……决定、信赖」。介词为本族常用词。整条短语保留「悬挂者离不开支撑」的意象。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses hang from something: water, a condition, a person's reliability, a single export, a habitat, a measured variable, a future wind, a drug, and a volunteer.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项各自挂在一处：水、条件、某人的可靠、单一出口、栖息地、测量变量、未来的风、药物与志愿者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket hung from a beam, its rope tightening as weight is added, the beam bending under the pull.
core.cn: 核心意象：篮子挂在梁上，加重时绳子绷紧，梁也被拉得微弯。

branches.en: THE LIVING SUPPORT: a spring and a single crop keep a community alive.
branches.cn: 活命的支撑：泉水与单一作物，维系着一个社区的生存。

branches.en: THE HABITAT: one kind of rotting log is the only thing that holds a beetle up.
branches.cn: 栖息地：一种腐木，是唯一托住这种甲虫的东西。

branches.en: THE MOVING VALUE: a harvest, a rate or a launch shifts with a factor one cannot fix.
branches.cn: 变动的值：收成、速率或发射，随一个无法固定的因素起落。

branches.en: THE TRUSTED PERSON: a handbook's sources and a volunteer at the door are relied on to hold.
branches.cn: 被信任的人：手册的来源与门口的志愿者，被指望守住。

branches.en: THE HELD HABIT: a pill that must be taken before sleep arrives.
branches.cn: 被抓住的习惯：不吃药就睡不着的夜晚。

intro.en: The family hangs from a Latin weighing verb; the prefix points downward, and the endings name the state, the person and the negation.
intro.cn: 这个词族挂在拉丁语「称重、悬挂」动词上；前缀指向下方，词尾命名状态、人与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere and dependere passed through French into English, which added its own endings and its own negative prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「悬挂」与「依附」动词经法语进入英语，英语加上自己的词尾与否定前缀。

items.example: It marks the weight as hanging down from a support.
items.exampleCN: 它标出重物从支撑处垂下。

items.example: The hanging verb at the base.
items.exampleCN: 底层的「悬挂」动词。

items.example: The direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The stem used in the modern phrase.
items.exampleCN: 现代短语所用的词干。

items.example: It forms the noun of reliance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「依赖」的名词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for one who relies.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「依赖者」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what can be relied on.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可靠的」形容词。

items.example: It reverses the adjective into independence.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词翻成「独立」。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加状态名词尾构成，义为「依赖」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「依赖的」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可靠的」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「独立的」

definition_zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；监测；监控；监听
definition_en: a device that displays or records information, a person who warns or keeps order, or to watch and check something continuously over time
core_image: 一个站在旁边不断提醒“注意”的人，眼睛一直盯着同一处
scene: 控制室里，工程师盯着显示管道压力的监视器。 From the control room the engineer watched the monitor that showed the pressure inside the pipeline.
sceneCN: 这里 monitor 是「显示器」（第 1 个义项：显示画面或数据的屏幕）；句意：工程师在控制室里盯着显示管道内压力的显示器。场景要点：昏暗的控制室、一排亮着的屏幕、屏幕上跳动的压力曲线、管道剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；告诫者
监测；监控；监听；跟踪观察

derivatives.zh: 监测；监控
告诫的；警告的
级长的；监督的
监督职务；级长职位

senses.title: A screen that shows the picture
senses.definition: a screen, especially a computer or television display, that shows information or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 显示信息或画面的屏幕，尤指电脑或电视显示屏
senses.example: The second monitor shows the camera feed from the front door.
senses.exampleCN: 第二块显示器显示前门的摄像头画面。
senses.why: Broadcasting used a monitor for a device that continuously checked a transmission, and the screen showing that check took the name. A computer display repeats the role: it lets someone keep watch on what the machine is doing.
senses.whyCN: 广播业曾把持续检查传输质量的设备称为 monitor，显示这项检查的屏幕便沿用了这个名字。电脑显示器重复着同一角色：让人持续看清机器在做什么。

senses.title: An instrument that keeps watch
senses.definition: a device that continuously measures and displays a physical condition, such as heart rate or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 持续测量并显示某项身体或物理状况的设备，如心率或压力
senses.example: The heart monitor began to beep faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏监测仪开始越响越快地鸣叫。
senses.why: The Latin monitor was a person who warned. An instrument that watches a pulse and sounds an alarm takes over the warning job, so the person's title passes to the machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 是一个发出警告的人。一台盯着脉搏、并发出警报的仪器接过了这份警告的职责，于是人的称呼转移到了机器上。

senses.title: The pupil who keeps order
senses.definition: a senior pupil at a school given the task of keeping order or checking attendance
senses.definitionCN: 学校里被赋予维持秩序或检查出勤任务的高年级学生
senses.example: The hall monitor checked the corridors every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊值日生每小时巡查一次走廊。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, from 1540s: a senior pupil 'charged with keeping order'. The student does exactly what the Latin word says — reminds others of the rules and reports breaches.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，始于 16 世纪 40 年代：受命维持秩序的高年级学生。这个学生做的正是拉丁词所说的——提醒别人守规矩，并报告违规。

senses.title: An official who warns
senses.definition: a person appointed to observe, advise, and warn, especially in an official or technical role
senses.definitionCN: 受指派观察、建议并提出告诫的人，尤指担任正式或技术职务者
senses.example: A monitor was appointed to warn the committee about conflicts of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会任命了一名监督员，就利益冲突提出告诫。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide'. The English noun keeps that advisory, warning figure before it ever names a machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人”。英语名词先保留了这个提出建议与警告的人，之后才用它命名机器。

senses.title: Watch the numbers over time
senses.definition: to measure and check a quantity or condition regularly over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内定期测量并检查某个数量或状况
senses.example: Sensors monitor the temperature of the tank every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每十分钟监测一次储罐的温度。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1924 for checking the quality of radio signals. Its core is repetition: a monitor does not look once but keeps looking, so the verb means sustained checking rather than a single glance.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 1924 年出现，指检查无线电信号的质量。它的核心是重复：monitor 不是看一眼，而是持续地看，所以这个动词表示持续的检查，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: Keep someone under surveillance
senses.definition: to watch a person, group, or activity closely, especially to detect wrongdoing or risk
senses.definitionCN: 密切注视某人、某群体或某项活动，尤为了发现不当行为或风险
senses.example: The company monitors its drivers' speed and braking through an app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通过一个应用监控司机的车速与刹车情况。
senses.why: When the watching is turned from a gauge to people, the warning role becomes surveillance. The same continuous attention is now aimed at behaviour that may need correcting.
senses.whyCN: 当注视的对象从仪表转向人，提醒的职责就变成了监控。同样的持续关注，现在对准了可能需要纠正的行为。

senses.title: Listen to a channel
senses.definition: to listen to a radio, telephone, or other channel continuously in order to catch particular information
senses.definitionCN: 持续收听无线电、电话或其他频道，以捕捉特定信息
senses.example: They monitored the radio channel all night, waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜监听那个无线电频道，等待回复。
senses.why: The earliest verb sense was exactly this: checking radio signals for quality. Listening to a channel is watching with the ears, and the word's continuity remains.
senses.whyCN: 最早的动词义正是这个：检查无线电信号的质量。用耳朵听一个频道就是“用耳朵看”，而这个词的持续性仍然保留。

senses.title: The lizard that warns
senses.definition: a large lizard of the family Varanidae, called a monitor because of an old story that it warned people of crocodiles
senses.definitionCN: 巨蜥科的大型蜥蜴，因古老传说称它会向人预警鳄鱼而得名
senses.example: A monitor lizard crossed the trail and disappeared into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨蜥穿过小径，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The name was given in 1826 because the lizard was fabled to give warning of Nile crocodiles. It is the same 'warner' sense, applied to an animal rather than a person or device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字始于 1826 年，因为传说这种蜥蜴会预警尼罗河鳄鱼。它仍是“警告者”这层意思，只是用在了动物身上，而不是人或设备。

senses.title: The ironclad that admonished
senses.definition: the name of the first ironclad warship of that design, built in 1862 and intended as a warning to the Confederacy
senses.definitionCN: 1862 年建造的第一艘该型铁甲舰的名称，意在向南方邦联发出警告
senses.example: The Monitor fought the Merrimack in 1862 and changed naval warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年，莫尼特号与梅里马克号交战，改变了海战方式。
senses.why: The inventor chose the name because the ship was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders. The Latin warner becomes a floating threat, a warning made of iron.
senses.whyCN: 发明者选择这个名字，是因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。拉丁语的告诫者变成了浮在水上的威胁，一个用铁铸成的警告。

senses.title: A background watcher in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的后台监控程序
senses.definition: in computing, a program or process that runs in the background and checks system activity
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指在后台运行、检查系统活动的程序或进程
senses.example: A background monitor logs every login and flags unusual hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个后台监控程序记录每次登录，并标记异常时段。
senses.why: Software repeats the human watchman: it runs unnoticed, checks continuously, and reports what looks wrong. The old 'one who warns' is now a loop of code.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复着人类更夫的角色：它不声不响地运行，持续检查，并报告看起来不对的地方。古老的“告诫者”如今成了一段循环的代码。

intro.en: Monitor began as a Latin word for a person who warns, entered English in the sixteenth century as a school officer, and only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries became a machine, a lizard, a warship, and finally a screen. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitor 最初是拉丁语中表示“告诫者”的词，16 世纪作为学校职务进入英语，直到 19 与 20 世纪才变成仪器、蜥蜴、军舰，最后成为屏幕。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'senior pupil at a school charged with keeping order'. It came from Latin monitor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“受命维持秩序的学校高年级学生”。它来自拉丁语 monitor。

items.en: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide, teacher'. It was an agent noun from monere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人、教师”。它是 monere 的施动名词。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, bring to one's recollection, tell of; admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach'. It goes back to PIE *moneie-, a causative form of *men- 'to think', the root also behind Latin memini 'I remember' and mens 'mind'.
items.cn: monere 意为“提醒、使想起、告知；告诫、建议、警告、指导、教导”。它可追溯到原始印欧语 *moneie-，即 *men-“思考”的使役形式；同一词根也是拉丁语 memini“我记得”与 mens“心智”的来源。

items.en: The monitor lizard was so called because it was fabled to warn people of Nile crocodiles (1826). The ironclad warship Monitor (1862) was named by its inventor because it was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders.
items.cn: 巨蜥被称为 monitor，是因为传说它会向人预警尼罗河鳄鱼（1826）。铁甲舰莫尼特号（1862）由发明者命名，因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1924 meaning 'to check for quality', originally of radio signals. The general sense 'observe, keep under review' is from 1944. Keats had used it in 1818 to mean 'to guide'.
items.cn: 动词于 1924 年有记录，意为“检查质量”，最初用于无线电信号。泛指“观察、持续审视”的义项始于 1944 年。济慈在 1818 年曾用它表示“引导”。

items.en: A broadcasting sense, 'a device to continuously check on the technical quality of a transmission', is recorded from 1931 and led to the sense 'a TV screen displaying the picture from a particular camera'. The computer display is a later extension of that screen sense.
items.cn: 广播义“持续检查传输技术质量的设备”记录于 1931 年，并由此引出“显示某一摄像机画面的电视屏幕”这一义项。电脑显示器是该屏幕义的后期引申。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adjective forms built on monitor from two related warning words; the second compares the verbs of watching that learners use interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组把由 monitor 构成的名词与形容词形式，同两个相关的“警告”词分开；第二组比较学习者常互换使用的几个“看管”动词。

entries.definition: the continuous act of checking or watching something. It is the process, while monitor is the device or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查或观察的行为。它是过程，而 monitor 是设备或动词。

entries.definition: giving or serving as a warning. It keeps the Latin sense of admonition and is mostly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 给予警告的，或起警告作用的。它保留了拉丁语“告诫”的意思，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly. It shares the Latin monere root but is a separate verb, not a form of monitor.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定但不严厉地警告或责备某人。它与 monitor 共享拉丁语 monere 词根，但它是另一个动词，不是 monitor 的词形。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something bad. It is a warning that comes before the event, built with pre- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种某事即将发生、尤指坏事的感觉。它是事件之前到来的警告，由 pre-“在前”构成。

entries.definition: to be in charge of people or work and make sure it is done properly. It stresses authority over workers, while monitor stresses continuous checking of signals or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 负责管理人或工作，确保事情做好。它强调对工作者的权威，而 monitor 强调对信号或状况的持续检查。

entries.definition: to look at something for a period of time, often without measuring it. Monitor usually adds a purpose: to detect change, risk, or poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内看着某物，通常不进行测量。monitor 通常多一层目的：发现变化、风险或质量问题。

entries.definition: to follow the movement or development of something over time, often by recorded traces. It focuses on where something goes; monitor focuses on whether it stays within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的移动或发展，常依据记录下来的痕迹。它关注东西去了哪里，monitor 关注它是否仍在限度之内。

entries.definition: to examine people, substances, or signals in order to sort or filter them. It is usually a test applied at a point in time, while monitor is a watch kept over time.
entries.definitionCN: 检查人、物质或信号，以便分类或筛选。它通常是在某一时点施行的检验，而 monitor 是长期保持的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin monere 'warn', the agent noun monitor, and the English family monitoring, monitory, admonish, and premonition.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 monere“警告”、施动名词 monitor，以及英语词族 monitoring、monitory、admonish、premonition。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn, remind'. A monitor is literally 'one who warns' — first a pupil, then an instrument, then a screen.
normal.cn: monere 意为“警告、提醒”。monitor 字面上就是“发出警告的人”——先是学生，再是仪器，最后是屏幕。

normal.en: The school sense is the oldest English one (1540s); the machine and screen senses are centuries later.
normal.cn: 学校职务义是英语里最古老的义项（16 世纪 40 年代）；仪器与屏幕义要晚好几个世纪。

normal.en: The verb arrived in 1924 for checking radio signal quality, which is why 'monitor a channel' still sounds natural.
normal.cn: 动词于 1924 年出现，用于检查无线电信号质量，所以 monitor a channel 至今听起来自然。

normal.en: monitoring is the process, monitory is 'warning', admonish is a separate verb from the same root.
normal.cn: monitoring 是过程，monitory 是“警告的”，admonish 则是同根的另一动词。

normal.en: A monitor differs from a supervisor: it keeps checking a signal or condition, while a supervisor holds authority over people.
normal.cn: monitor 与 supervisor 不同：它持续检查信号或状况，而 supervisor 对人拥有管理权。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman at a factory gate. He does not repair anything; he looks, checks, and raises the alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守在工厂大门的更夫。他不修理任何东西；他看、检查、发出警报。

abstract.en: Move that watchman into a box on the wall, and he becomes a heart monitor; put his gaze on a screen, and he becomes a display.
abstract.cn: 把这位更夫装进墙上的盒子，他就成了心脏监测仪；把他的目光放到屏幕上，他就成了显示器。

abstract.en: The word always means attention spread over time: a single look is not monitoring, however careful it is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终表示铺在时间上的注意：只看一眼，无论多仔细，都不算监测。

examples.en: Nurses monitor the patient's pulse and blood pressure every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时监测病人的脉搏与血压。

examples.en: The app monitors how much time you spend on each website.
examples.cn: 这个应用监控你在每个网站上花多少时间。

examples.en: The teacher left a monitor in charge of the class while she fetched the keys.
examples.cn: 老师去取钥匙时，让班长负责管班。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫离他”——莫要离开他，他一直在旁边盯着、随时提醒你 → monitor 监视器；监测（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 monere“警告、提醒”的施动名词 monitor“告诫者”，核心是“持续盯着并随时发出提醒”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of monitor, all held together by one figure: someone standing beside a thing, watching without stopping and speaking up when something is wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: monitor 的十个义项都由同一个形象串起：有人站在某物旁边，不停地看，一有不对就出声提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warner standing beside, eyes fixed on one spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在旁边、目光钉在一处的告诫者。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: the warner becomes a measuring device, and the screen that shows its check takes the same name.
branches.cn: 仪器：告诫者变成测量设备，显示这项检查的屏幕也沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest senses keep a person in the role, either a pupil keeping order or an official who warns.
branches.cn: 人：最古老的义项让一个人留在这个角色里，或是维持秩序的学生，或是提出告诫的官员。

branches.en: WATCHING: the verb checks quantities over time, and when aimed at people it becomes surveillance.
branches.cn: 注视：动词随时间检查数量，而当对象转向人时，它就变成监控。

branches.en: LISTENING: a channel is watched with the ears, the earliest verb use of all.
branches.cn: 监听：频道是用耳朵看的，这是所有动词用法中最早的一个。

branches.en: THE NAME TRAVELS: a lizard fabled to warn, an ironclad built to admonish, and a background program that keeps checking.
branches.cn: 名字远行：传说会预警的蜥蜴、为告诫而造的铁甲舰，以及持续检查的后台程序。

intro.en: Monitor is a Latin agent noun in -itor built on mon- 'warn'. English adds -ing, -y, -ial and -ship, while the same root also reaches English through admonish, monition, and premonition.
intro.cn: monitor 是拉丁语中以 -itor 结尾的施动名词，词干 mon- 意为“警告”。英语加上 -ing、-y、-ial 与 -ship，同一词根还通过 admonish、monition、premonition 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is monere 'warn, remind', its agent noun monitor, and the action noun monitio 'a warning'. Summon also belongs here: Latin summonere meant 'hint, remind, warn'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族包括 monere“警告、提醒”、它的施动名词 monitor，以及行为名词 monitio“警告”。summon 也属于这里：拉丁语 summonere 意为“暗示、提醒、警告”。

items.meaning: one who warns or checks; a checking device
items.meaningCN: 告诫者；检查者；监测设备（mon- 警告 + -itor 施动名词）
items.example: The monitor on the wall showed a steady line.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的监测仪显示出一条平稳的线。

items.meaningCN: 监测；监控（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: The patient was kept under close monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 病人被置于密切监测之下。

items.meaningCN: 告诫的；警告的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave a monitory glance at the noisy table.
items.exampleCN: 他朝吵闹的那桌投去一个警告的目光。

items.meaning: relating to a monitor or prefect
items.meaningCN: 级长的；监督的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The monitorial duties rotated each week.
items.exampleCN: 级长职责每周轮换。

items.meaningCN: 告诫；温和地责备（ad- 向 + mon- 警告）
items.example: The coach admonished the players for arriving late.
items.exampleCN: 教练因球员迟到而告诫了他们。

items.example: She ignored the admonition and drove faster.
items.exampleCN: 她无视那句告诫，反而开得更快。

items.meaning: a warning, especially an official one
items.meaningCN: 警告；正式告诫（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The court issued a monition to the landowner.
items.exampleCN: 法院向那位土地所有者发出正式警告。

items.meaning: a feeling that something is coming
items.meaningCN: 预感；事前警告（pre- 在前 + monition 警告）
items.example: She had a premonition that the flight would be delayed.
items.exampleCN: 她预感到那趟航班会延误。

items.meaningCN: 召唤；传唤（sum- 暗中 + mon- 提醒）
items.example: The manager summoned the clerk to her office.
items.exampleCN: 经理把那名职员叫到办公室。

items.structure: Greek Mentor, perhaps from PIE *men- 'to think'
items.meaningCN: 导师；可信赖的顾问（同出“思考”词根）
items.example: She became a mentor to the younger researchers.
items.exampleCN: 她成了年轻研究者的导师。

latinEntries.meaning: one who warns, reminds, or checks

definition_zh: 脱落；（植物器官的）自然脱落；切除
definition_en: the natural shedding of a plant part such as a leaf or fruit, or the act of cutting something off
core_image: 一片叶子在叶柄基部被一层细胞轻轻断开，随风落下
scene: 秋天一到，树叶基部形成一层特殊细胞，让叶片自然落下。 Leaf abscission begins when the days grow shorter.
sceneCN: 这里 abscission 是「（植物器官的）自然脱落」（第 1 个义项：植物主动断开并舍弃某部分）；句意为白昼变短时，叶片脱落开始。

pos.zh: 脱落；（植物）器官自然脱落
切除；断离

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「脱落；切断」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「脱落酸的；与脱落有关的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「脱落素」，脱落酸的旧称

senses.title: Shedding of plant parts
senses.definition: the natural dropping of leaves, fruits, flowers, or other plant parts
senses.definitionCN: 叶片、果实、花或其他植物部位的自然掉落
senses.example: Leaf abscission is controlled by plant hormones.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片脱落受植物激素控制。
senses.why: Latin abscindere meant 'to cut off'; the plant cuts its own leaf, and the word names that controlled separation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abscindere 意为「切掉」；植物自己把叶子切断，这个词命名了这种受控的分离。

senses.title: The fall of leaves
senses.definition: the seasonal process by which leaves are shed from a tree
senses.definitionCN: 树木按季节把叶子舍弃的过程
senses.example: Autumn abscission removes water‑losing leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季脱落会去掉会失水的叶子。
senses.why: Seasonal leaf fall is the most visible case of the plant cutting away a whole organ before winter.
senses.whyCN: 季节性落叶是植物在入冬前切掉整个器官最显眼的例子。

senses.title: The drop of fruit
senses.definition: the shedding of fruit before or after ripening
senses.definitionCN: 果实在成熟前后掉落
senses.example: Premature fruit abscission reduces the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 果实过早脱落会减少收成。
senses.why: Fruit is cut free at the stalk when the plant no longer supports it, so the same separation image applies.
senses.whyCN: 当植物不再供养果实时，果实就在果柄处被切离，因此同一个分离意象适用。

senses.title: Surgical removal
senses.definition: the removal of a part by cutting, especially in older medical writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过切割去除某部分，尤见于较早医学文献
senses.example: The older term abscission referred to cutting away tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的术语 abscission 指把组织切掉。
senses.why: Medicine used the literal sense first: tissue is cut off, exactly as the Latin verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 医学先使用这个字面义：组织被切掉，正如拉丁动词所描述的那样。

senses.title: The abscission zone
senses.definition: the layer of cells at the base of a plant part where separation occurs
senses.definitionCN: 植物器官基部发生分离的细胞层
senses.example: A visible line marks the abscission zone.
senses.exampleCN: 一条可见的线标出脱落区。
senses.why: The zone is the seam where the cut will happen, so the place of separation takes the name of the process.
senses.whyCN: 脱落区就是即将发生切断的接缝，于是分离的地点借用了过程的名字。

senses.title: Separation of flowers
senses.definition: the shedding of petals or whole flowers after pollination
senses.definitionCN: 授粉后花瓣或整朵花的掉落
senses.example: Flower abscission follows pollination in many species.
senses.exampleCN: 许多物种在授粉后发生花器官脱落。
senses.why: Once pollination is done, the flower's work is finished, and the plant cuts the now-useless parts away.
senses.whyCN: 授粉完成后，花的任务就结束了，植物便把不再有用的部分切掉。

senses.title: Cutting off in general
senses.definition: the act of cutting something away from its base
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从基部切离的行为
senses.example: The word abscission is rare outside botany and surgery.
senses.exampleCN: abscission 一词在植物学与外科之外很少使用。
senses.why: The general sense is simply the Latin verb translated: any cutting away from a base.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是拉丁动词的直译：任何从基部切离的行为。

senses.title: A sharp separation
senses.definition: a sudden or clean separation of one thing from another
senses.definitionCN: 一物从另一物上突然或干净地分离
senses.example: The report describes the abscission of the ice shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了冰架的断裂分离。
senses.why: Large structures can also break along a seam, so the botanical image extends to ice and rock.
senses.whyCN: 大型结构也能沿接缝断开，因此植物学意象延伸到冰体与岩石。

intro.en: Abscission comes from a Latin noun for cutting off, built from a prefix and the verb for cutting.
intro.cn: abscission 来自一个意为「切掉」的拉丁语名词，由前缀与表示「切」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *skheID- is reconstructed with the sense 'to cut, split'; the exact reconstruction varies among sources.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *skheID- 被重构为「切、劈」之义；不同来源的具体重构形式不一致。

items.en: scindere meant 'to cut, split', and it also lies behind scissors and rescind.
items.cn: scindere 意为「切、劈」，scissors 与 rescind 也源自它。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus scindere formed abscindere, 'to cut off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 scindere 构成 abscindere，意为「切掉」。

items.en: The noun abscissio named the act of cutting off, the direct source of English abscission.
items.cn: 名词 abscissio 指切掉的行为，是英语 abscission 的直接来源。

items.en: English abscission first appeared in medical and general writing for cutting away a part.
items.cn: 英语 abscission 最初出现在医学与一般文献中，指切去某部分。

items.en: Botany made the word central for the natural shedding of leaves and fruit, especially through the abscission zone.
items.cn: 植物学使这个词成为叶果自然脱落的核心术语，尤其通过「脱落区」的概念。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the acid adjective, and two other cutting words; the second gathers nouns for natural shedding and removal.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、酸的形容词与另外两个「切」词；第二组收表示自然脱落与去除的名词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to cut off or to be shed naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「切掉」或「自然脱落」。

entries.definition: An adjective used in abscisic acid, the hormone that controls shedding.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，用于 abscisic acid（脱落酸），即控制脱落的激素。

entries.definition: The horizontal coordinate in mathematics, literally 'a cut-off line'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「横坐标」，字面是「被切下的一段线」。

entries.definition: A cutting tool, from the same Latin verb scindere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剪刀」，来自同一个拉丁动词 scindere。

entries.definition: To cancel a law or agreement, literally to cut it away.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废除、取消」，字面是「把它切掉」。

entries.definition: The natural dropping of leaves, skin, or hair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脱落」，指叶、皮或毛发的自然掉落。

entries.definition: The state of becoming separate from something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分离、脱离」，指与某物分开的状态。

entries.definition: The act of taking something away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「去除、移除」，指把某物拿走的动作。

entries.definition: The surgical cutting out of a part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「切除」，指外科切去某部分。

entries.definition: The act of dividing or coming apart.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分离」，指分开或断离的行为。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the botanical collocations and the shared Latin cutting root; the abstract hooks picture the leaf's clean break.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用植物学搭配与共享的拉丁「切」词根；抽象记忆点想象叶片干净的断口。

normal.en: Leaf abscission and abscission zone are the core botanical phrases.
normal.cn: leaf abscission 与 abscission zone 是核心植物学短语。

normal.en: Abscisic acid is the hormone named after abscission.
normal.cn: abscisic acid（脱落酸）是以 abscission 命名的激素。

normal.en: Abscission and scissors share Latin scindere, 'to cut'.
normal.cn: abscission 与 scissors 共享拉丁语 scindere（切）。

normal.en: The verb is abscise, and the adjective abscisic belongs to the acid.
normal.cn: 动词是 abscise，形容词 abscisic 属于那种酸。

normal.en: In older medicine abscission meant cutting away tissue.
normal.cn: 在较早的医学中，abscission 指切去组织。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf stem developing a thin line of cells, then letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象叶柄长出一条薄薄的细胞线，然后松手。

abstract.en: Picture a fruit dropping onto grass while the branch stays intact.
abstract.cn: 想象果实落到草地上，而树枝完好无损。

abstract.en: Picture an ice shelf cracking along a clean seam and sliding away.
abstract.cn: 想象冰架沿一条干净的接缝裂开并滑走。

examples.en: Abscission protects trees from losing too much water.
examples.cn: 脱落能保护树木不过度失水。

examples.en: The abscission zone forms at the base of the leaf.
examples.cn: 脱落区在叶片基部形成。

examples.en: Fruit abscission can be triggered by stress.
examples.cn: 果实脱落可能由胁迫引发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布西申」——叶子基部像被小剪刀轻轻一剪，叶子就脱离枝条落下来。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ scindere（切），构成 abscindere（切掉），名词 abscissio；核心义是「沿一条线干净地切离」

sensesIntro.en: The senses center on the plant's controlled cutting away of leaves, fruit, and flowers, with extensions to surgery and clean separation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项围绕植物受控地切离叶片、果实与花，并延伸到外科切除与干净分离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf cut free along a thin seam of cells
core.cn: 核心意象：叶片沿一条薄细胞缝被切离

branches.en: Plant parts are shed in a controlled seasonal process.
branches.cn: 植物部位在受控的季节过程中脱落。

branches.en: The abscission zone is the anatomical seam where separation happens.
branches.cn: 脱落区是发生分离的解剖接缝。

branches.en: Older medicine used the word for cutting tissue away.
branches.cn: 较早的医学用这个词表示切去组织。

branches.en: The general sense is any cutting away from a base.
branches.cn: 一般义是从基部切离任何东西。

branches.en: Clean separation extends to ice shelves and other structures.
branches.cn: 干净分离延伸到冰架及其他结构。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem absciss-, the prefix ab-, and the endings -ion, -ize, and -ic.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 absciss-、前缀 ab-，以及后缀 -ion、-ize、-ic 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abscindere and abscissio are the direct source of abscission, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abscindere 与 abscissio 是 abscission 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其名词。

definition_zh: 政治的；政党的；政治性的；涉及权力关系的；关心并参与政治的
definition_en: relating to government, parties or public power, and also used of anything shaped by the struggle for influence
core_image: 竞选办公室的墙上一层层贴着海报，志愿者守着电话名单逐个催票
scene: 选举前夜，竞选办公室的墙上贴满海报，志愿者守着电话名单逐个催票。 The rally was a political event from the first speech to the last handshake.
sceneCN: 这里指「与政党及选举有关的」，对应第 2 个义项：属于党派竞争与投票活动范畴的；句意为这场造势集会从第一场演讲到最后一次握手都是政治活动。画面要点：海报墙、电话名单、成排折叠椅；对应第 1 个义项。
