senses.title: Relating to government and public affairs
senses.titleCN: 与政府及公共事务有关
senses.definition: concerned with the state, its institutions and the making of public decisions
senses.definitionCN: 涉及国家、其机构以及公共决定的作出
senses.example: The constitution sets the political institutions of the country.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法确立了这个国家的政治机构。
senses.why: the Greek adjective meant 'of citizens, civic', so political first described what belongs to the organised community.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊形容词意为「公民的、城邦的」，因此 political 最初描述属于有组织共同体的事物。

senses.title: Relating to parties and elections
senses.definition: belonging to the competition of parties, campaigns and votes
senses.definitionCN: 属于政党竞争、竞选活动与投票的范畴
senses.example: The rally was a political event from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这场集会从头到尾都是政治活动。
senses.why: when civic business organised itself into parties, the adjective followed the contest rather than the institution.
senses.whyCN: 当城邦事务组织成党派之后，这个形容词就跟着竞争走，而不只指机构。

senses.title: Moved by power rather than by merit
senses.titleCN: 出于权力考量而非事理本身
senses.definition: describing a choice made to protect influence or advantage rather than because it is right or efficient
senses.definitionCN: 形容某项选择是为保住影响力或优势而作，而非因为它正确或高效
senses.example: The appointment was political, not technical.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任命是政治性的，不是技术性的。
senses.why: once the adjective can mean 'of the contest', it can also mean 'shaped by the contest', and that reading carries the criticism.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个形容词能表示「属于竞争」，也就能表示「被竞争左右」，后一种读法自带批评意味。

senses.title: Sensitive or contested in public terms
senses.titleCN: 在公共层面敏感、容易引发争执
senses.definition: describing a topic that arouses strong public disagreement and is therefore hard to handle openly
senses.definitionCN: 形容会激起强烈公共分歧、因而难以公开处理的话题
senses.example: Water rights are a political subject in every dry province.
senses.exampleCN: 在每个干旱省份，水权都是敏感的政治话题。
senses.why: topics become political when they enter the space where groups must take sides, so the adjective marks that entry.
senses.whyCN: 话题一旦进入群体必须站队的那个空间，就变得政治化，这个形容词标记的正是这一进入。

senses.title: Power relations inside an organization
senses.definition: describing the informal side of an institution where influence, alliance and status are at stake
senses.definitionCN: 形容机构中影响力、结盟与地位暗中较劲的那一面
senses.example: A political reading of the memo explained why the plan died.
senses.exampleCN: 从权力关系的角度读这份备忘录，就能解释这个方案为何夭折。
senses.why: the pattern of alliance and rivalry repeats in firms and faculties, so the adjective travels wherever scarce goods are allocated.
senses.whyCN: 结盟与对立的格局在企业与院系里都会重演，因此只要稀缺之物需要分配，这个形容词就会跟过去。

senses.title: Engaged or aware as a person
senses.titleCN: 形容关心并参与政治的人
senses.definition: describing a person who follows public affairs and acts on them, as in a very political family
senses.definitionCN: 形容关注公共事务并付诸行动的人，如一个政治气氛浓厚的家庭
senses.example: She came from a political family and knew the ward maps by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 她出身于政治家庭，把选区地图记得滚瓜烂熟。
senses.why: the adjective applies to people as well as things, and then it means absorbed in the activity rather than belonging to it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可用于人，此时指沉浸在政治活动中，而不是属于某个机构。

senses.title: Belonging to the state sphere
senses.titleCN: 属于国家领域而非民间或宗教领域
senses.definition: marking the boundary between matters of the state and matters of faith, market or private life
senses.definitionCN: 标出国家事务与信仰、市场或私人生活之间的界线
senses.example: The dispute was religious in form and political in effect.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端形式上属宗教，实际效果上属政治。
senses.why: a society divides its spheres, and the adjective names the one that ends in enforceable collective decisions.
senses.whyCN: 社会把领域划分开来，这个形容词所指的正是最终以可强制执行的集体决定收尾的那一个领域。

senses.title: Abstract: concerning who decides collectively
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：关乎集体由谁决定
senses.definition: in general use, touching on the question of who has the right to make a binding choice for a group
senses.definitionCN: 泛指触及「谁有权为一个群体作出有约束力的选择」这一问题
senses.example: Even the choice of a chairman became political.
senses.exampleCN: 连选谁当主席都变成了政治问题。
senses.why: the abstract sense reduces the word to one question, namely who may decide for the group.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把这个词压缩成一个问题，即为群体作决定的权利归谁。

intro.en: Political is the English form of a Greek adjective meaning 'of citizens', built on the word for a city-state. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: political 是希腊语中意为「公民的」这一形容词在英语里的形式，其词根是表示城邦的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis named a city-state and its citizen body; its deeper origin is not settled, and a pre-Greek source is a hypothesis rather than an established fact.
items.cn: polis 指城邦及其公民总体；它更深的来源未有定论，前希腊语来源只是假说，并非已确认的事实。

items.en: Politikos meant 'of a citizen, civic, fit for governing', and it described affairs that concerned the community rather than the household.
items.cn: politikos 意为「公民的、城邦的、适于治理的」，描述与共同体相关、而非与家户相关的事务。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective as politicus and used it for civil and state affairs, especially in translations of Greek political works.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借作 politicus，用于民政与国家事务，尤其在翻译希腊政治著作时使用。

items.en: Middle French politique took the word into English in the fifteenth century, first as a noun for the study of the state and soon after as an adjective.
items.cn: 中古法语 politique 在十五世纪把这个词带入英语，先作名词指对国家的研究，随后不久用作形容词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective was extended to party competition and then to any sphere where influence is contested, including offices and universities.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词先扩用到党派竞争，再扩用到任何影响力受争夺的领域，包括办公室与大学。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same civic stem that are easily mistaken for this adjective; group two holds adjectives that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「城邦」词干、容易被误当作本词的词；第二组是含义部分重叠的形容词。

entries.definition: A shorter adjective meaning shrewd and tactful; a politic move is a wise one, not necessarily a governmental one.
entries.definitionCN: 更短的同源形容词，意为精明得体的；得体的举动是明智之举，未必与国家有关。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used for the standpoint or the consequences in power terms, as in politically impossible.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，用于表示政治角度或权力层面的后果，如政治上不可行。

entries.definition: Built with a negative prefix, it means indifferent to or outside politics, and is the direct opposite of one sense of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 由否定前缀构成，意为不问政治的或与政治无关的，与本词的某一义项正好相反。

entries.definition: The activity itself; the adjective describes what belongs to it or resembles it.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动本身；本词形容词则描述属于该活动或与之相似的事物。

entries.definition: Relating to government as an institution; it does not extend to party contests or office manoeuvring.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为机构的政府有关；不延伸到党派竞争或办公室权术。

entries.definition: Loyal to a party or cause; political can be neutral, while partisan always implies taking sides.
entries.definitionCN: 忠于某党或某项主张；political 可以是中性的，而 partisan 总意味着站队。

entries.definition: Relating to the duties and rights of citizens in a town; it is about membership rather than about power struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 与市民的义务和权利有关；侧重成员身份，而非权力争夺。

entries.definition: Concerning the community as a whole or open to view; it lacks the connotation of contest for authority.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及整个共同体或对外公开；不含争夺权威的意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The stem is the Greek word for a city-state, so the adjective originally means 'belonging to the citizen body'.
normal.cn: 词干是希腊语中表示城邦的词，所以这个形容词本义是「属于公民总体的」。

normal.en: The family runs political, politically, politics, politician, politicize and apolitical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治的、在政治上、政治、从政者、使政治化与不问政治的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institutional sense: political party, political system, political will, political debate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出制度义：政党、政治制度、政治意愿、政治辩论。

normal.en: Saying a decision was political is a criticism; saying a map is political is a description.
normal.cn: 说某个决定是政治性的，是批评；说某张地图是政治的，是描述。

normal.en: The pair to remember is politic for prudent and political for governmental.
normal.cn: 要记住的对照是：较短的 politic 指精明得体，political 指与国家相关。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every chair is placed to show who outranks whom.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，每把椅子的位置都在显示谁的位次更高。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn across a table, with faith on one side and enforceable rules on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上画一条线，一边是信仰，另一边是可强制执行的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall, asking not what is true but who may decide.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里举起一只手，问的不是何为真，而是谁有权决定。

examples.en: The reforms were blocked for purely political reasons.
examples.cn: 这些改革因纯粹的政治原因被搁置。

examples.en: She kept her political views out of the classroom.
examples.cn: 她不让自己的政治观点进入课堂。

examples.en: A political solution is needed before the water can be shared.
examples.cn: 在分配水源之前，需要一个政治层面的解决方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「城邦公民的」——凡涉及谁掌权、谁站队的事 → 政治的

root: political 出自希腊 politikos「公民的、城邦的」，源头为 polis「城邦」与 politēs「公民」，经拉丁 politicus 与中古法语 politique 进入英语；polis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses branch from one adjective: what belongs to the citizen body, then to parties, to power-driven choices, to sensitive topics, to office rivalries, to engaged persons, to the state sphere, and finally to any question of who decides.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个形容词分出：先属公民总体，再属党派、属出于权力的选择、属敏感话题、属办公室里的对立、属积极参与的人、属国家领域，最后属任何「谁来决定」的问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a campaign office wall layered with posters, a list of names to call.
core.cn: 核心意象：竞选办公室的墙上一层叠一层的海报，以及一列待拨的姓名。

branches.en: CIVIC BASE: the adjective first marks what belongs to the organised citizen body and its institutions.
branches.cn: 公民基础：这个形容词最初标记属于有组织公民总体及其机构的事物。

branches.en: PARTY CONTEST: once civic business is organised in parties, the adjective follows the campaign.
branches.cn: 党派竞争：城邦事务一旦组织成党派，这个形容词就跟着竞选活动走。

branches.en: MOTIVE AND SENSITIVITY: a choice can be driven by advantage, and a topic can be explosive, and one adjective covers both warnings.
branches.cn: 动机与敏感：选择可能被利益驱动，话题可能一触即发，同一个形容词兼具这两种提醒。

branches.en: SMALL SCALE AND PERSONAL: office rivalries repeat the pattern, and a person can be absorbed in it.
branches.cn: 小规模与个人：办公室的对立重演这一格局，而个人也可以沉浸其中。

branches.en: SPHERE AND QUESTION: the state sphere is marked off from faith and market, and behind it lies the bare question of who decides.
branches.cn: 领域与问题：国家领域与信仰、市场被划开，而其后正是「谁来决定」这个赤裸的问题。

intro.en: Political is a Greek adjective stem plus an English adjective ending, and the stem also builds politics, politician and policy.
intro.cn: political 是希腊形容词词干加英语形容词词尾，同一词干还造出政治、从政者与政策。

latinIntro.en: Latin politicus carried the Greek adjective into learned use, and its feminine noun politica stands behind policy and polity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 politicus 把这个希腊形容词带入学术用法，其阴性名词 politica 则是政策与政体两词的来源。

items.example: The root supplies the civic frame of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供这个词的城邦框架。

items.example: The citizen is the reference point of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 公民是这个形容词的参照点。

items.example: The suffix turns the citizen into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「公民」变成表示归属的形容词。

items.example: The adjective was used of matters of the community.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于共同体的事务。

items.example: Latin kept the adjective for civil affairs.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词保留给民政事务。

items.example: The ending makes the borrowed stem into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把借来的词干变成英语形容词。

items.example: The adverb marks the standpoint rather than the thing.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记的是角度，而非事物本身。

items.example: A budget cut politicized the whole faculty.
items.exampleCN: 一次预算削减把整个院系政治化了。

items.example: The survey was designed to look apolitical.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查被设计得看似不问政治。

latinEntries.structure: politicus, politica, politicum (adjective, borrowed from Greek)
politica, politicae (f., first declension; from Greek ta politika)

definition_zh: 减少；缩小；降低；使陷入（某种状态）；把复杂之物归结为；约分；收汁；还原；复位
definition_en: to make something smaller or lower, to bring it into a simpler form or a worse state, and in chemistry to add electrons to it
core_image: 一口宽锅里汤汁翻滚，水汽不断散走，最后只剩薄薄一层浓汁挂在锅底
scene: 厨师把一大锅汤留在小火上慢慢收，水分一点点走掉，最后只剩能挂勺的浓汁。 Long simmering will reduce the sauce to a thick glaze.
sceneCN: 这里 reduce 指通过加热让液体变少变浓（第 6 个义项：烹调收汁，把汤汁熬到更少的量）；句意：长时间小火慢熬会把酱汁收成浓稠的亮汁。图中可辨识物件：宽口锅、上升的水汽、木勺、挂勺的浓汁。

pos.zh: 减少；缩小；降低；把……归结为；使陷入
减少；缩小；变浓；（化学）被还原

derivatives.zh: 由 reduce 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「减少；还原」
由 reduce 加已然词尾构成，义为「已减少的；已还原的」
由 reduce 加进行词尾构成，义为「有还原能力的」
由 reduce 加「能够被……的」后缀构成，义为「可减少的；可约分的」
由 reduce 加施动词尾构成，义为「还原剂；缩小装置」

senses.title: Make smaller in size or amount
senses.titleCN: 在大小或数量上使之变小
senses.definition: to make something smaller, fewer or less in amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在体积、数量或总量上变小变少
senses.example: Insulation reduces heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿墙而走的热量。
senses.why: The core gesture is bringing something down; the modern everyday sense simply applies that downward motion to quantity and size.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是「把某物带下来」；现代日常义只是把这个向下的动作用在数量与大小上。

senses.title: Lower a price, rate or level
senses.definition: to bring a price, rate, speed or level down to a lower figure
senses.definitionCN: 把价格、比率、速度或水平降到一个更低的数值
senses.example: The store reduced prices by a fifth before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 节前商店把价格降了五分之一。
senses.why: Prices and rates are quantities on a scale, so the same downward gesture is read as a movement along that scale.
senses.whyCN: 价格与比率是尺度上的量，因此同一个向下动作被读作沿尺度向下移动。

senses.title: Bring a problem to a simpler form
senses.titleCN: 把问题归结为更简单的形式
senses.definition: to restate a complicated thing as a simpler one that explains it
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂之事重新表述为能解释它的更简单之事
senses.example: The authors reduce the argument to a single question.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把这个论证归结为一个问题。
senses.why: A simpler form carries the same content in fewer parts, so reduction here means stripping away what can be dropped.
senses.whyCN: 更简单的形式用更少的部件承载同样的内容，因此这里的「减」指剥掉可以舍去的部分。

senses.title: Force into a worse condition
senses.definition: to bring someone or something into a lower or worse state, often with 'to'
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物带到更低、更糟的状态，常与表示「到」的介词连用
senses.example: The flood reduced the village to a few broken walls.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水使村庄只剩几堵断墙。
senses.why: The downward movement can be read as loss of standing, so the verb also describes being brought low rather than made smaller.
senses.whyCN: 向下的移动也可以读作地位的丧失，于是这个动词也描述「被压低」，而不是「被缩小」。

senses.title: Simplify a fraction in arithmetic
senses.definition: to divide the top and bottom of a fraction by a common number so that the value stays the same but the figures get smaller
senses.definitionCN: 用公因数同时除分子与分母，使数值不变而数字变小
senses.example: Students reduce the fraction before adding it to another.
senses.exampleCN: 学生先把分数约分，再与另一个分数相加。
senses.why: Arithmetic keeps the value while shrinking the written figures, which is the clearest small-scale model of the whole word.
senses.whyCN: 算术让数值保持不变而让写出的数字变小，这是整个词最小尺度、也最清晰的模型。

senses.title: Boil a liquid down
senses.definition: to cook a liquid until it thickens and its volume falls
senses.definitionCN: 加热液体使其变稠、体积减少
senses.example: Long simmering will reduce the sauce to a thick glaze.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间小火慢熬会把酱汁收成浓稠的亮汁。
senses.why: Cooking turns the abstract downward movement into something visible: steam leaves and what remains is denser.
senses.whyCN: 烹调把这个抽象的向下运动变成可见之事：水汽走掉，剩下的更浓。

senses.title: Add electrons in chemistry
senses.definition: to add electrons to an atom, ion or molecule, or to remove oxygen from it
senses.definitionCN: 给原子、离子或分子加上电子，或从中去掉氧
senses.example: Carbon can reduce the metal oxide to the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 碳能把金属氧化物还原成金属。
senses.why: The chemical sense came from the older notion of bringing a substance back to a simpler state: the ore returns to bare metal.
senses.whyCN: 化学义来自更早的「把物质带回更简单的状态」：矿石退回为纯金属。

senses.title: Put a bone or joint back in place
senses.definition: to restore a displaced bone or joint to its proper position
senses.definitionCN: 把错位的骨头或关节恢复到正确位置
senses.example: The doctor reduced the shoulder and strapped the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 医生使肩关节复位，并把手臂固定好。
senses.why: Medicine uses the original 'bring back' reading literally: the part is led back to where it belongs.
senses.whyCN: 医学把最初「带回」的读法用在字面上：那个部位被领回原位。

senses.title: Sum up raw data
senses.titleCN: 把原始数据归纳成摘要
senses.definition: to turn a set of measurements into a few summary figures
senses.definitionCN: 把一组测量值变成少数几个汇总数字
senses.example: The software reduces thousands of readings to a mean and a range.
senses.exampleCN: 软件把上千个读数归纳成一个均值与一个范围。
senses.why: Statistics repeats the simplifying gesture: many pieces become one figure that is easier to hold.
senses.whyCN: 统计学重复了那个简化动作：许多碎片变成一个更易把握的数字。

intro.en: Reduce comes from Latin reducere, 'to lead back', built on re- 'back' and ducere 'to lead'. English shortened the sense to 'bring down' and later added technical uses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reduce 来自拉丁 reducere「领回」，由 re-「向后」与 ducere「引领」构成；英语把词义收窄到「使降低」，之后又长出各种专门用法。年代为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead or draw along', the root behind duke, duct and conduct; the idea is direction rather than shrinking.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引领、牵引」，是 duke、duct、conduct 等词背后的词根；其核心是方向，而不是缩小。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus ducere produced reducere, 'to lead back, bring back, restore', as one brings a traveller or a troop home.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 ducere 构成 reducere「领回、带回、恢复」，如同把旅人或队伍带回家。

items.en: English took the word through Old French, first in the senses of bringing back, restoring and leading a person to a place.
items.cn: 英语经古法语引入该词，最初指带回、恢复、把人领到某处。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the verb increasingly meant bringing something to a lower figure or condition, and that reading now dominates ordinary use.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪起，这个动词越来越多地指把某物带到更低的数值或状态，这一读法如今在日常用法中占主导。

items.en: Cooking added the simmering sense, arithmetic the simplifying of fractions, and medicine the restoring of a joint; chemistry adopted 'reduce' for the removal of oxygen, later generalised to the gain of electrons.
items.cn: 烹调加上收汁义，算术加上约分义，医学加上关节复位义；化学用这个词指去掉氧，后来又一般化为「获得电子」。

items.en: First date uncertain for the sense shift: the date at which the 'lessen' sense overtook the older 'bring back' sense is inferred from citation records, not a fixed event.
items.cn: 义项转变的首见年代不确定：表示「减少」的义项何时压过更早的「带回」义，是根据文献记录作出的推断，并非某一个确定事件。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root and is constantly confused; the second group holds other words for making something less.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根，极易混淆；第二组是其他表示「使变少」的词。

entries.tag: the noun of the same verb
entries.definition: The act or result of reducing, including the chemical gain of electrons; it names the event, not the action of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 减少的动作或结果，也包括化学上的获得电子；它命名事件，而非执行动作。

entries.definition: Built on de- 'down from' plus ducere: to draw a conclusion out of given premises, which is reasoning, not shrinking.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-「从……向下」加 ducere 构成：从给定前提出结论，属推理，不属缩小。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus ducere: to lead someone into a state or to bring about an effect, with no sense of lessening.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 ducere：把某人引入某种状态或促成某结果，与「变少」无关。

entries.definition: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere: to bring something out into existence; the root is shared but the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「向前」加 ducere：把某物带出来使其存在；词根相同但方向相反。

entries.definition: To become or make less in number or size; it states the change of amount without the idea of simplifying or restoring.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或大小上变少或使之变少；它只说量的变化，不含简化或恢复之意。

entries.definition: To move something down in height, level or rank; it suits a position on a scale better than a bulk of material.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物在高度、水平或等级上往下移；它更适合尺度上的位置，而非成堆的物质。

entries.definition: To remove a portion, especially of cost, text or supply; it stresses the removal rather than the resulting smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉一部分，尤指费用、文字或供应；它强调移除，而非变小后的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus ducere 'lead': the oldest picture is leading something back home.
normal.cn: re-「向后」加 ducere「引领」：最早的画面是把某物领回家。

normal.en: The family runs reduce, reduction, reduced, reducing, reducible, reducer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reduce、reduction、reduced、reducing、reducible、reducer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern sense: reduce costs, reduce the risk, reduce emissions.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代义：降低成本、降低风险、减少排放。

normal.en: The same root leads in deduce, induce and produce, each with a different direction.
normal.cn: 同一词根也出现在 deduce、induce 与 produce 中，各自的方向不同。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps an old picture: ore is led back to bare metal.
normal.cn: 化学保留了一个旧画面：矿石被领回成纯金属。

abstract.en: Picture a wide pot of soup losing its steam until only a spoonful of glaze is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一大锅汤不断散走水汽，最后只剩一勺浓汁。

abstract.en: Picture a long report folded again and again until one small square remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一份长报告被反复对折，最后只剩一个小方块。

abstract.en: Picture a scattered crowd walking back through one gate until the field is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象散开的人群从一道门走回，最后场地空了。

examples.en: Better lamps reduce the electricity bill in winter.
examples.cn: 更好的灯具能降低冬季电费。

examples.en: The committee reduced the proposal to three short points.
examples.cn: 委员会把提案归结为三条短要点。

examples.en: Hydrogen can reduce the oxide at high temperature.
examples.cn: 氢在高温下能还原这种氧化物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ duce（引导）」——把数量往回领，就是减少

root: 拉丁 reducere「领回、带回」= re-（向后）+ ducere「引领」；英语先取「带回、恢复」义，后转为「使降低、减少」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one downward or backward gesture: quantity falls, price falls, a problem is simplified, a person is brought low, a fraction shrinks, a sauce thickens, an ore returns to metal, a joint returns to place, and data is folded into a summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个向下或向回的动作：数量下降、价格下降、问题被简化、人被压低、分数变小、酱汁变浓、矿石退回金属、关节回到原位、数据被折成摘要。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide pot of sauce simmering down to a spoonful of thick glaze.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口宽锅里的酱汁慢慢收成一勺浓汁。

branches.en: DOWN THE SCALE: whatever is counted or priced moves to a smaller figure, from heat loss to holiday prices.
branches.cn: 沿尺度向下：凡可计数或标价之物都移向更小的数字，从热损失到节日价格。

branches.en: FEWER PARTS: an argument or a pile of readings is restated in a form that can be held at once.
branches.cn: 更少的部件：论证或一堆读数被重新表述成可以一次握住的形式。

branches.en: LED TO A PLACE: a village is led down to rubble, and a shoulder is led back into its socket.
branches.cn: 被领到某处：村庄被带到只剩瓦砾，肩关节被领回关节窝。

branches.en: SHRINKING THE WRITTEN OR THE LIQUID: a fraction loses common factors, a sauce loses water.
branches.cn: 缩小写下的或流动的：分数失去公因数，酱汁失去水分。

branches.en: THE ORE RETURNS: chemistry keeps the oldest picture and calls the gain of electrons a leading back.
branches.cn: 矿石退回：化学保留最古老的画面，把获得电子称为「领回」。

intro.en: Reduce is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb root, and both parts are unusually productive in English.
intro.cn: reduce 由一个拉丁前缀加一个拉丁动词词根构成，这两部分在英语里都异常能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives duct, conduct, induce, produce and deduce, while re- recur in return, remain and reflect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 duct、conduct、induce、produce 与 deduce，而 re- 也反复出现在 return、remain 与 reflect 中。

items.example: The prefix supplies the backward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供向后的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供牵引的动作。

items.meaning: to lead back; to bring down
items.example: The verb still carries a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词至今带着方向感。

items.structure: reduce plus the action noun ending
items.meaning: the act or result of reducing
items.example: The reduction in cost was welcome.
items.exampleCN: 成本的降低很受欢迎。

items.example: The reduced price applies at weekends.
items.exampleCN: 优惠价在周末适用。

items.meaning: causing a decrease; chemically able to add electrons
items.meaningCN: 起减少作用的；化学上能提供电子的
items.example: A reducing agent gives electrons away.
items.exampleCN: 还原剂把电子让出去。

items.structure: reduce plus the 'able to be' ending
items.example: The fraction is reducible by three.
items.exampleCN: 这个分数可以用三约分。

items.meaning: a substance or device that reduces
items.example: A reducer joins pipes of different widths.
items.exampleCN: 异径接头把不同粗细的管子接起来。

latinEntries.structure: ducere, duco, duxi, ductum (v., third conjugation)

derivatives.zh: 由 reduce 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「减少；还原」
由 reduce 加已然词尾构成，义为「已减少的；已还原的」
由 reduce 加进行词尾构成，义为「有还原能力的」
由 reduce 加「能够被……的」后缀构成，义为「可减少的；可约分的」
由 reduce 加施动词尾构成，义为「还原剂；缩小装置」

definition_zh: 互利共生；互利主义；互惠互助
definition_en: a lasting association between two species in which each partner gains a net benefit, and by extension any doctrine or practice of reciprocal benefit between parties
core_image: 两株植物的根系在地下相互缠绕，一侧输出糖分、另一侧输出磷盐，两端都抽出新叶
scene: 这里指「互利共生」。 The fig and its pollinating wasp form a textbook mutualism in which neither species can reproduce without the other.
sceneCN: 这里 mutualism 指「互利共生」（第 1 个义项：双方都获得净收益的共生关系）；无花果与传粉榕小蜂构成教科书式的互利共生，彼此离开对方都无法繁殖。图中可辨识物件：榕果、小蜂、交织的根系、磷盐结晶。

pos.zh: 互利共生；互利主义；互惠互助（指关系或学说时不可数，指一例具体共生时可用复数 mutualisms）

collocations.zh: 专性互利共生；双方离开对方都无法生存的共生
兼性互利共生；有互利好处但并非必需
植物与传粉者之间的互利共生
肠道互利共生；肠道菌与宿主之间的互惠关系
互利主义理论；主张以互惠而非竞争解释社会协作
经济互惠主义；以相互授信、互助合作为基础的经济主张
使一段互利共生关系瓦解

derivatives.zh: 相互的；共同的；彼此之间的
相互地；彼此地
相互性；互惠性；共同性
互利共生的一方；互惠主义者
互利共生的；体现互惠的
偏利共生；一方受益、另一方不受影响

senses.title: Both partners gain
senses.titleCN: 互利共生：双方都获得净收益
senses.definition: in ecology, a lasting association between two species in which each partner receives a net benefit from the other
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指两个物种长期共处，且每一方都从对方获得净收益的关系
senses.example: Coral polyps and their photosynthetic algae live in an obligate mutualism.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚虫与共生光合藻类处于一种专性互利共生关系。
senses.why: The word names the plus-plus corner of symbiosis, where a relationship can be scored by what each partner gains rather than by who dominates.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出共生关系里的「双赢」一角：衡量一段关系，看双方各自得到什么，而不是看谁占上风。

senses.title: The pollination contract
senses.titleCN: 传粉契约：花给报酬，虫送花粉
senses.definition: a mutualism in which a plant supplies nectar or a place to lay eggs and an animal moves its pollen between flowers
senses.definitionCN: 指植物提供花蜜或产卵场所、动物替它把花粉在花间搬运的互利共生
senses.example: Fig-wasp mutualism depends on the wasp entering the fruit to pollinate it while laying its eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 榕树与榕小蜂的互利共生依赖小蜂钻进果实产卵，同时完成授粉。
senses.why: Here the benefit is a service rather than a substance: pollen is delivered, and the insect is paid in food and nursery space.
senses.whyCN: 这里的收益不是物质而是服务：花粉被送达，昆虫得到食物与育幼空间作为报酬。

senses.title: Cleaning stations
senses.titleCN: 清洁站：小鱼取食寄生虫，大鱼得到清洁
senses.definition: a mutualism in which one animal removes parasites or debris from another and gains food in return
senses.definitionCN: 指一种动物替另一种清除寄生虫或残渣，并以此换取食物的互利共生
senses.example: Cleaner fish at the reef station remove ticks from larger fish, a well-studied mutualism.
senses.exampleCN: 礁石清洁站上的清洁鱼替大鱼清除寄螨、吸血虫，这是一种被充分研究过的互利共生。
senses.why: The pairing is a service trade, so ecologists call it mutualism rather than parasitism: both sides leave better off.
senses.whyCN: 这组关系是服务交换，因此生态学家称其为互利共生而非寄生：双方离开时都更好。

senses.title: Gut microbiome
senses.titleCN: 肠道共生：菌群发酵，宿主获得养分
senses.definition: a mutualism between a host animal and its resident microbes, in which the microbes receive habitat and the host receives nutrients or protection
senses.definitionCN: 指宿主动物与常驻微生物之间的互利共生：微生物获得栖息地，宿主获得养分或保护
senses.example: Gut mutualism lets bacteria ferment fibre into acids the human body can absorb.
senses.exampleCN: 肠道互利共生让细菌把膳食纤维发酵成人体可吸收的酸。
senses.why: The relationship is scored inside one body: habitat is paid for with metabolic work, so the label fits the ecological definition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这段关系发生在一个身体内部：栖息地由代谢劳动来支付，正好符合互利共生的生态学定义。

senses.title: Mutualist doctrine
senses.titleCN: 互利主义：以相互授信取代中央权力
senses.definition: in political economy, a doctrine that organises credit, exchange and federation through reciprocal agreements among equals
senses.definitionCN: 政治经济学中主张以平等者之间的相互授信、交换与联合来组织经济与社会的主张
senses.example: Proudhon's mutualism proposed interest-free credit banks run by the workers themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 蒲鲁东的互利主义主张由劳动者自己经营无息信贷银行。
senses.why: The biological word has an older political life: mutualisme named a society built on reciprocity rather than hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 这个生物学词汇有更早的政治生命：mutualisme 指以互惠而非等级构建的社会。

senses.title: Mutual aid in practice
senses.titleCN: 互助实践：团体之间的自愿互惠
senses.definition: the everyday practice of voluntary reciprocal help among people or groups, as in mutual aid funds and cooperatives
senses.definitionCN: 指个人或团体之间自愿互惠的日常互助实践，如互助基金与合作社
senses.example: The mutualism of the village cooperative kept grain prices stable through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 村合作社的互惠机制让粮价在整个冬天保持稳定。
senses.why: Once reciprocity is organised into a habit, the abstract suffix -ism turns it into a named way of doing things.
senses.whyCN: 当互惠被组织成习惯，抽象后缀 -ism 就把它变成一种有名有姓的做法。

senses.title: Coevolved partnership
senses.titleCN: 共同演化：相互选择塑造出的伙伴
senses.definition: a partnership so tight that each partner's traits have been shaped by selection acting through the other
senses.definitionCN: 指紧密到每一方的性状都被对方所施加的选择塑造过的伙伴关系
senses.example: The long mutualism left both the flower and the bee with matching tube lengths.
senses.exampleCN: 长期的互利共生让花与蜂都演化出彼此匹配的管长。
senses.why: Mutualism is not only a present exchange but a history: reciprocal selection leaves anatomical evidence on both sides.
senses.whyCN: 互利共生不只是当下的交换，也是一段历史：相互选择会在双方身上留下解剖学证据。

senses.title: Institutional reciprocity
senses.titleCN: 机构互惠：借生物学词汇描述合作
senses.definition: a figurative use for two institutions or sectors that each supply what the other lacks, such as shared data and shared funding
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指两个机构或部门各自提供对方所缺之物，如共享数据与共享经费
senses.example: The university and the hospital describe their joint research as a mutualism.
senses.exampleCN: 大学与医院把他们联合开展的科研称作一种互利共生。
senses.why: The metaphor works because the test is the same: if either side stops gaining, the arrangement no longer deserves the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，因为检验标准相同：只要有一方不再获益，这种安排就不配叫这个名字。

intro.en: Mutualism joins Latin mutuus 'reciprocal, borrowed' with the noun suffix -ism; ecology gave an old word for reciprocity a biological body.
intro.cn: mutualism 把拉丁语 mutuus「相互的、借来的」与名词后缀 -ism 结合；生态学让这个表示互惠的旧词有了生物学躯体。

items.en: Latin mutuus meant 'reciprocal, exchanged, borrowed'. It described things that pass back and forth between parties, not things that merely look alike.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus 意为「相互的、交换的、借来的」，描述在双方之间来回传递之物，而不是仅仅长得相似之物。

items.en: Mutual is often connected with Latin mutare 'to change, exchange', the source of mutate and commute. The link is plausible but not proved, so the deeper root connection is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 mutual 与拉丁语 mutare「改变、交换」有关，该词根也是 mutate 与 commute 的来源；但这一联系只是合理推测、未获确证，更深的词根关联属来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix came into Latin as -ismus from Greek -ismos, which formed nouns for doctrines, practices and conditions.
items.cn: 该后缀以 -ismus 形式进入拉丁语，源自希腊语 -ismos，用来构成表示学说、实践与状态的抽象名词。

items.en: Mutual reached English in the fifteenth century through Old French mutuel, first describing shared feelings and shared obligations.
items.cn: mutual 于 15 世纪经古法语 mutuel 进入英语，最初描述共同的情感与共同的义务。

items.en: In the 1870s the Belgian zoologist Pierre-Joseph van Beneden applied mutualism to symbioses that benefit both partners. The exact first printing and date are uncertain, and older uses in political economy complicate the record.
items.cn: 19 世纪 70 年代，比利时动物学家皮埃尔-约瑟夫·范贝内登把 mutualism 用于双方都受益的共生关系；确切的首见文本与年代存疑，政治经济学中更早的用法也让文献记录变得复杂。

items.en: French mutualisme named a scheme of reciprocal credit and voluntary federation in the nineteenth century. It is generally dated to the 1840s and predates the biological sense, but the first citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 法语 mutualisme 在 19 世纪指相互授信与自愿联合的方案；一般认为其年代在 1840 年代、早于生物学义项，但确切首见书证仍不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the mut- stem and must be kept apart by part of speech; the second group is the three-way symbiosis vocabulary that beginners most often mix up.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mut- 词干，需按词性区分；第二组是初学者最容易混淆的共生三分法词汇。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning shared by two or more parties. It describes the quality of an exchange, while mutualism names the relationship or doctrine built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为两方或多方共同拥有的。它描述交换的性质，而 mutualism 指建立在这种性质之上的关系或学说。

entries.definition: A noun for the state of being reciprocal. It is a quality, not a biological relationship, so it cannot replace mutualism in ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指相互性这一状态。它表示性质而非生物关系，因此在生态学语境中不能替换 mutualism。

entries.definition: A count noun for one partner in a mutualism, or for a person who advocates mutualist economics. The system itself is mutualism.
entries.definitionCN: 可数名词，指互利共生中的一方，或主张互利主义经济的人。制度或关系本身叫 mutualism。

entries.definition: Any close, lasting association between two species. It covers mutualism, commensalism and parasitism, so it is broader and neutral about who gains.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个物种之间任何紧密而持久的共处。它涵盖互利共生、偏利共生与寄生，范围更广且不判断谁获益。

entries.definition: A symbiosis in which one partner benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed. The plus-zero counterpart of mutualism.
entries.definitionCN: 指一方受益、另一方既不受益也不受害的共生。它是互利共生的「加零」对应项。

entries.definition: A symbiosis in which one partner benefits at the expense of the other. The plus-minus counterpart of mutualism.
entries.definitionCN: 指一方获益、另一方受损的共生。它是互利共生的「加减」对应项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mutuus means reciprocal, and -ism turns a quality into a system: reciprocal benefit as a system.
normal.cn: mutuus 意为相互的，-ism 把性质变成制度：把互惠互利做成一套关系。

normal.en: The family runs mutual, mutually, mutuality, mutualist and mutualistic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mutual、mutually、mutuality、mutualist、mutualistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: obligate mutualism, facultative mutualism, plant-pollinator mutualism, gut mutualism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：专性互利共生、兼性互利共生、植物与传粉者互利共生、肠道互利共生。

normal.en: Place it in the triad: mutualism is plus-plus, commensalism is plus-zero, parasitism is plus-minus.
normal.cn: 放进三分法：互利共生是加加，偏利共生是加零，寄生是加减。

normal.en: Van Beneden applied the term to beneficial symbiosis in the 1870s, and political mutualisme came earlier.
normal.cn: 范贝内登在 1870 年代把这个词用于有益共生，而政治上的互惠主义用法更早出现。

abstract.en: Picture two root systems trading sugar for phosphate underground, both pushing up new shoots.
abstract.cn: 想象两套根系在地下用糖分换磷盐，两侧都抽出新芽。

abstract.en: Picture a cleaner fish entering a large fish's mouth and leaving fed, while the host leaves clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一条清洁鱼游进大鱼口中，离开时吃饱了，而宿主也变干净了。

abstract.en: Picture two workshops keeping a shared ledger of favours, each entry owed by one and paid by the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个作坊共用一本恩惠账簿，每一笔都由一方欠下、另一方偿还。

examples.en: The coral-algae mutualism collapses when water temperatures rise too far.
examples.cn: 水温升得过高时，珊瑚与藻类的互利共生就会崩溃。

examples.en: Ecologists distinguish obligate mutualism from relationships that are merely convenient.
examples.cn: 生态学家把专性互利共生与仅仅图方便的关系区分开来。

examples.en: The cooperative's mutualism is written into its rules on shared credit.
examples.cn: 这家合作社的互惠机制写进了它关于共享信贷的章程。

dict_mnemonic.text: mutual（相互的）+ ism（主义）→ 相互受益的一套关系 → mutualism 互利共生

root: 拉丁 mutuus「相互的、借来的」+ -ism；19 世纪生态学用它命名双方都受益的共生关系，政治经济学中的互惠主义用法更早。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one test: does each side leave better off? Ecology applies the test to species, economics to credit, and the metaphor to institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕同一条检验：双方离开时是否都更好？生态学用它检验物种，经济学用它检验信贷，比喻用法用它检验机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two root systems trading sugar for phosphate, both growing new shoots.
core.cn: 核心意象：两套根系用糖分换磷盐，两侧都长出新芽。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: the basic definition is a plus-plus score for two species living together.
branches.cn: 生态学：基本定义是两个物种共处时得到加加评分。

branches.en: SERVICE TRADE: pollination, cleaning and gut fermentation are the same bargain in different currencies.
branches.cn: 服务交换：传粉、清洁与肠道发酵是同一笔交易换了不同货币。

branches.en: SOCIAL PRACTICE: reciprocity becomes a doctrine when credit and aid are organised on purpose.
branches.cn: 社会实践：当授信与互助被有意组织起来，互惠就成了一种主张。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: reciprocal selection writes the partnership into both bodies.
branches.cn: 深层时间：相互选择把这段伙伴关系写进双方的身体。

branches.en: METAPHOR: institutions borrow the word, and the same test still applies.
branches.cn: 比喻：机构借用这个词，检验标准依然不变。

intro.en: Mutualism is built from a Latin adjective plus a Greek-derived noun suffix, so the word means 'the system of the reciprocal'.
intro.cn: mutualism 由拉丁形容词加希腊来源的名词后缀构成，字面意思是「相互性所成的制度」。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutuus supplies the stem, Greek -ismos reaches English through Latin -ismus, and the family also grows through -ity, -ist and -istic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus 提供词干，希腊语 -ismos 经拉丁语 -ismus 进入英语，这一族还通过 -ity、-ist 与 -istic 扩展。

items.meaning: a system of reciprocal benefit, especially between species
items.meaningCN: 互惠受益的体系，尤指物种之间的互利共生
items.example: Reef mutualism keeps both coral and algae alive.
items.exampleCN: 礁体互利共生让珊瑚与藻类都得以生存。

items.meaning: shared or felt by both sides
items.meaningCN: 双方共享或共同感受到的
items.example: The two labs signed a mutual data agreement.
items.exampleCN: 两个实验室签署了共享数据的互惠协议。

items.example: The two species depend mutually on each other.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种相互依赖。

items.example: The contract stresses mutuality of obligations.
items.exampleCN: 合同强调义务的相互性。

items.meaning: one partner in a mutualism; an advocate of mutualist economics
items.meaningCN: 互利共生的一方；互利主义的支持者
items.example: Each mutualist gains something the other cannot make.
items.exampleCN: 每个互利共生方都得到对方无法自造的东西。

items.meaning: of or marked by mutual benefit
items.meaningCN: 互利共生的；带有互惠特征的
items.example: The ants and the acacia have a mutualistic bond.
items.exampleCN: 蚂蚁与金合欢之间存在互利共生纽带。

items.example: The two fungi grow mutualistically on the same log.
items.exampleCN: 这两种真菌在同一根木头上互利共生地生长。

items.meaningCN: 一方受益而另一方无损的偏利共生
items.example: Barnacles on a whale are a case of commensalism.
items.exampleCN: 鲸身上的藤壶是偏利共生的一例。

items.meaningCN: 任何紧密而持久的共处关系
items.example: Symbiosis covers all three plus-minus scores.
items.exampleCN: 共生涵盖加加、加零、加减三种评分。

latinEntries.structure: mutare, muto, mutavi, mutatum (v., first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to change, to exchange; its link to mutuus is plausible but unproved
latinEntries.meaningCN: 改变、交换；它与 mutuus 的关联只是合理推测，未获确证

definition_zh: 归因于；归功于；认为出自；把……归属于；归咎于
definition_en: to say that something is caused by, produced by, or belongs to a particular person, thing or circumstance
core_image: 修谱的桌上摊开一卷世系，一支朱笔把新添的名字画回祖辈的方格，旁边注明这一支的来处
scene: 修谱人把新抄的名字放回旧格，再用一支朱笔把名字画回祖辈的方框，并在旁边注明这一支的来处。 Historians can attribute to the workshop a set of unsigned panels.
sceneCN: 这里指把一组作品认定出自某个作坊（第 3 个义项：认定作品出自某人）；句意为史学家可以把一组没有署名的画板认定出自那个作坊。图中可辨识物件：世系卷、朱笔、方格、批注。

pos.zh: 归因于；归功于；认为出自；归咎于

collocations.phrase: attribute to a lack of funds

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加名词尾构成，义为「归因；归属；出处」
由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「可归因的；可归功的」
由同一词干加形容词尾构成，义为「定语性的」
短语核心词的名词形式，义为「属性；特征」
由表示「错误」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「错归；误认为出自」

senses.title: To name a cause
senses.definition: to say that an event or condition was caused by a particular factor
senses.definitionCN: 指出某一事件或状况由某个特定因素造成
senses.example: Scientists can attribute to volcanic ash the sudden cooling.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家可以把突然降温归因于火山灰。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to assign a share, and a cause is the share of responsibility assigned to one factor.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为分派一份，而原因就是分派给某个因素的那一份责任。

senses.title: To credit a person for something good
senses.definition: to say that a good result was produced by a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个好结果是由某个特定的人或群体带来的
senses.example: The coach will attribute to the captain the team's revival.
senses.exampleCN: 教练会把球队的复苏归功于队长。
senses.why: Credit is a share of honour, and the same verb that assigns a cause also assigns praise.
senses.whyCN: 功劳是一份荣誉，分派原因的那个动词也分派赞扬。

senses.title: To name the author of a work
senses.definition: to say that a painting, book or other work was made by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认定一幅画、一部书或其他作品由某个特定的人创作
senses.example: Scholars may attribute to Titian the unsigned portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 学者可能认为那幅未署名的肖像出自提香。
senses.why: A work has an origin, and the verb that assigns a cause to a factor also assigns a work to a hand.
senses.whyCN: 作品有其来处，把原因分派给因素的那个动词也把作品分派给某一双手。

senses.title: To assign a quality to someone
senses.titleCN: 把某种特征归属于某人
senses.definition: to say that a person or thing has a particular quality or characteristic
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人或某物具有某种特定的品质或特征
senses.example: People can attribute to the breed a calm temperament.
senses.exampleCN: 人们可以把温和的性情归属于这一品种。
senses.why: A quality is treated as a share laid on a subject, the same arithmetic of assignment as a cause.
senses.whyCN: 品质被当作放在某个主体身上的一份，与原因的分派是同一套算法。

senses.title: To trace a symptom to its cause
senses.definition: to say that a symptom or illness was produced by a particular pathogen or condition
senses.definitionCN: 认为某种症状或疾病由某个特定病原体或状况引起
senses.example: Doctors may attribute to the tick the sudden fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生可能把突然发热归到蜱虫身上。
senses.why: Medical tracing repeats the general pattern: an effect is handed back to the thing that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 医学溯源重复着同一模式：结果被交还给产生它的东西。

senses.title: To link a climate effect to warming
senses.titleCN: 把气候现象归因于变暖
senses.definition: in climate science, to state that a particular weather or ice change was made more likely by global warming
senses.definitionCN: 在气候科学中，指认定某一特定天气或冰情变化因全球变暖而更可能发生
senses.example: The panel will attribute to warming the shrinking glacier.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组会把冰川退缩归因于变暖。
senses.why: Climate research made attribution a technical term: the share of risk assigned to a named driver.
senses.whyCN: 气候研究把「归因」变成了术语：把风险的一份分派给某个被指名的驱动因素。

senses.title: To trace something to an origin
senses.definition: to show that a word, custom or lineage belongs to a particular source or family
senses.definitionCN: 表明一个词、一种习俗或一支血脉属于某个特定源头或族系
senses.example: Linguists can attribute to the same root two distant dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家可以把两种相距很远的方言都追溯到同一个词根。
senses.why: Origin is a place on a family tree, and the verb places a thing on that tree by assigning it a branch.
senses.whyCN: 源头是谱系树上的一个位置，这个动词通过分派一个枝系把事物放到那棵树上。

senses.title: To blame a fault on someone
senses.definition: to say that a fault, failure or bad outcome was caused by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个过失、失败或坏结果由某个特定的人造成
senses.example: The inquiry may attribute to the pilot the final error.
senses.exampleCN: 调查可能把最后的失误归咎于飞行员。
senses.why: When the assigned share is blame, the same neutral verb takes on a hostile edge without changing its structure.
senses.whyCN: 当被分派的那一份是责难时，同一个中性的动词就带上敌意，而结构并未改变。

intro.en: Attribute comes from Latin attribuere, to assign or allot, formed from ad-, to, and tribuere, to divide or give, which goes back to tributum, a tax. The same root produced tribute, contribute and distribute. English took the verb in the sixteenth century, and attribute to became the usual frame for naming a cause, an author or a fault.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「attribuere」「分派、给予」，由「ad-」「朝向」和「tribuere」「分配、给予」构成，而「tribuere」出自「tributum」「税」。同一词根还产生「tribute」、「contribute」与「distribute」。英语在十六世纪引入这个动词，短语「attribute to」成为指出原因、作者或过错的常用框架。

items.en: The noun meant a tax or a payment divided among people, the concrete image of parting out a sum.
items.cn: 这个名词意为税或按人分摊的款项，是「把钱分出去」的具体意象。

items.en: The verb meant to divide, allot or grant, and it named the act of giving each party its share.
items.cn: 这个动词意为分配、分给、授予，指给每一方一份的动作。

items.en: The prefix meant to or towards, and it directed the share towards a particular recipient.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为朝向，把那一份指向某个特定的接受者。

items.en: The compound meant to assign or impute something to a person or thing, the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为把某物分派或归到某人某物身上，是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century and used it for assigning causes, qualities, authors and blame.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，用于分派原因、品质、作者与过错。

items.en: The phrase attribute to fixed the target of the assignment, and it now appears in science, law, art history and ordinary argument.
items.cn: 短语「attribute to」固定了分派的目标，如今出现在科学、法律、艺术史与日常论辩中。

note.en: The first group gathers words built with the same root or a neighbouring prefix; the second group gathers verbs of assigning a cause, an author or a fault.
note.cn: 第一组收录由同一词根或相近前缀构成的形式；第二组收录表示分派原因、作者或过错的动词。

entries.definition: The act of saying who or what something comes from, and the name given to that origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指认定某物来自谁或什么的动作，也指由此给出的出处。

entries.definition: Able to be explained by or credited to a particular cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够由某一特定原因解释或归于其名下的。

entries.definition: To give money, effort or ideas towards a common purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同目的拿出钱财、努力或想法。

entries.definition: To divide something and give it out among several people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物分开并分发给若干人或地方。

entries.definition: A payment made by one ruler or group to another as a sign of submission.
entries.definitionCN: 指一方统治者或群体向另一方缴纳以示臣服的贡品。

entries.definition: To say that something belongs to or is caused by a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某物属于或由某个特定的人或物引起。

entries.definition: To say that someone is responsible for a good result.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某人应对某个好结果负责。

entries.definition: To say that someone or something is at fault for a bad result.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某人或某物应对坏结果负责。

entries.definition: To give a particular role, cause or value to someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某个角色、原因或数值分派给某人或某物。

entries.definition: To say that a fault or quality belongs to someone, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 指把过失或品质归到某人身上，常含不公之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin act of handing out a share, the real prefix family, and the real phrases of cause, credit and fault.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语中「分出一份」的动作、真实的前缀词族，以及原因、功劳与过错的真实搭配。

normal.en: Tribuere is to divide and give out, so attribute to is to hand a share back to its source.
normal.cn: 「tribuere」是分开并发放，因此「attribute to」就是把一份交还给它该去的地方。

normal.en: Contribute, distribute and tribute all carry the same offering of a share.
normal.cn: 「contribute」「distribute」与「tribute」都带着同一个「献出一份」的意思。

normal.en: People attribute a painting to a painter, a fever to a tick, and a failure to a pilot; the frame never changes.
normal.cn: 人们把画归给画家，把发热归给蜱虫，把失败归给飞行员；框架始终不变。

normal.en: The word often takes the cause as its target: attribute to the storm the delay.
normal.cn: 这个词常把原因放在短语之后：把延误归因于暴风雨。

normal.en: In climate reports, attribution means the share of risk that a named factor can claim.
normal.cn: 在气候报告里，归因指某个被指名的因素可以认领的那一份风险。

abstract.en: Attribution is a family tree drawn on the fly: every effect gets a branch, every work gets a hand.
abstract.cn: 归因是随手画出的谱系树：每个结果都得到一根枝，每件作品都得到一双手。

abstract.en: The verb is neutral until the share is shame; then assigning a cause becomes assigning blame.
abstract.cn: 这个动词本中性，直到那一份是羞耻；此时分派原因就变成分派责难。

abstract.en: To attribute well is to resist the nearest hand: distance makes the difference between evidence and blame.
abstract.cn: 善加归因就是抵抗最近的那双手：距离划出证据与责难之间的界线。

examples.en: The report will attribute to bad wiring the loss of power.
examples.cn: 报告会把断电归因于线路不良。

examples.en: Many readers attribute to Homer the whole epic.
examples.cn: 许多读者认为整部史诗出自荷马。

examples.en: Officials may attribute to heavy rain the closed road.
examples.cn: 官员可能把道路封闭归因于大雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿特崔比优特·图」——按份派回去，功劳或错处落到该去的人头上：归因、归功

root: 拉丁语「attribuere」「分派、给予」=「ad-」「朝向」+「tribuere」「分配、给予」←「tributum」「税」；同根有「contribute」「distribute」「tribute」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one frame of assignment: naming a cause, crediting a person, naming an author, assigning a quality, tracing a symptom, attributing a climate effect, tracing an origin, and placing blame.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「分派」框架：指出原因、把功劳归于某人、认定作者、归属品质、追溯症状、归因气候现象、溯源系属、分派过错。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush draws a new name back to an older branch on a family scroll and marks where that branch comes from.
core.cn: 核心意象：朱笔把新添的名字画回家谱上较老的枝，并标明这一枝的来处。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: a factor receives its share of responsibility, whether a local event or a warming climate.
branches.cn: 原因：某个因素得到它的一份责任，无论是局部事件还是气候变暖。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same share becomes honour for a captain or shame for a pilot.
branches.cn: 人：同一份既可成为队长的荣誉，也可成为飞行员的羞耻。

branches.en: THE WORK AND THE QUALITY: a creation is given a hand, and a trait is given a subject.
branches.cn: 作品与品质：创作被配上一双手，特征被配上一个主体。

branches.en: THE SYMPTOM: a fever is sent back to the creature that caused it.
branches.cn: 症状：发热被送回到引起它的生物。

branches.en: THE LINEAGE: a word or custom is set on a branch of a larger family tree.
branches.cn: 谱系：一个词或习俗被放到更大谱系树的某一枝上。

intro.en: Attribute is built from a Latin verb of dividing and giving, and its family spreads across money, praise and blame.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示分配与给予的拉丁动词构成，其词族散布在钱财、赞誉与责难之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies tribuere and attribuere, with tributum behind them; the same root reaches English through tribute, contribute and distribute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「tribuere」与「attribuere」，它们背后是「tributum」；同一词根经「tribute」、「contribute」与「distribute」进入英语。

items.example: The prefix sends the share to a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把那一份送往一个目标。

items.meaning: tax, a payment divided among people
items.example: The concrete image is a sum parted out.
items.exampleCN: 这一具体意象是把一笔钱分出去。

items.example: The verb names the act of giving each its share.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指给每一方一份的动作。

items.structure: Latin verb from ad- and tribuere
items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a payment to a stronger power
items.example: English kept the concrete payment.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了具体的缴纳物。

items.structure: English verb from com- and tribuere
items.meaning: to give towards a common purpose
items.example: The prefix com- gathers the shares together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀「com-」把各份聚到一起。

items.structure: English verb from dis- and tribuere
items.meaning: to give out in separate shares
items.example: The prefix dis- scatters the shares apart.
items.exampleCN: 前缀「dis-」把各份散开。

items.meaning: the act of naming a source
items.example: The noun names the whole act of assignment.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指整个分派行为。

items.example: It forms the word for what can be attributed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「可被归因」的词。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- and tribuere

由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「可归因的；可归功的」
由同一词干加形容词尾构成，义为「定语性的」
短语核心词的名词形式，义为「属性；特征」
由表示「错误」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「错归；误认为出自」

definition_zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的；双语并用的（也可作名词：双语者）
definition_en: using or written in two languages, or able to speak two languages
core_image: 一张对开的告示纸，左半边与右半边写着同样内容却用两种文字，中间用一条细线分开
scene: 社区公告栏上贴着一张对开的告示，左右两半内容相同，文字却不同。 Every bilingual form in the office carried the same sentence twice.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用两种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及两种语言并用）；句意为办公室里的每份双语表格都把同一句话写了两遍。可辨识物件：告示、对开纸、两种文字、公告栏。

pos.zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的
双语者（可数）

derivatives.zh: 双语现象；双语能力
以双语方式
多语的

senses.title: Using two languages
senses.definition: describing a thing, service or activity that works in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以两种语言运作的事物、服务或活动
senses.example: The bilingual help desk answers in Mandarin and English.
senses.exampleCN: 双语服务台用普通话与英语应答。
senses.why: the word pairs a prefix for 'two' with the Latin word for tongue, so it counts two languages exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「二」的前缀与拉丁语表「舌头」的词相连，精确地数两种语言。

senses.title: A person who speaks two languages
senses.definition: describing someone who can use two languages in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 描述能在日常生活中使用两种语言的人
senses.example: She grew up bilingual and still dreams in both.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小双语成长，至今仍用两种语言做梦。
senses.why: a person who carries the pair through a whole life is the human face of the count.
senses.whyCN: 把这一对语言带过一生的人，是这个数目的「人面」。

senses.title: A text or sign in two languages
senses.titleCN: 用两种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: printed or displayed in two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种语言印刷或展示
senses.example: The bilingual label lists every ingredient twice.
senses.exampleCN: 双语标签把每种成分列出两遍。
senses.why: two languages printed side by side make the pair visible.
senses.whyCN: 两种语言并排印出，就让这一对变得可见。

senses.title: Bilingual education
senses.definition: schooling in which two languages serve as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以两种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Bilingual education delayed the shift to the majority language.
senses.exampleCN: 双语教育推迟了向多数语言的转换。
senses.why: a school that teaches in two languages turns the count into a curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 用两种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成课程。

senses.title: A bilingual community or region
senses.definition: describing a place where two languages are in everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 描述两种语言在日常中并用的地方
senses.example: The valley has been bilingual since the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路开通以来，这条山谷一直双语并存。
senses.why: a whole place can hold the pair for generations, so the adjective describes geography as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 整个地方能把这一对保留几代，因此这个形容词既描述人也描述地理。

senses.title: Bilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how one mind stores and switches between two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对同一心智如何储存并切换两种语言的研究
senses.example: Bilingual speakers separate their languages by context, not by effort.
senses.exampleCN: 双语说话者按场合区分语言，而不是靠费力控制。
senses.why: a mind that holds two systems is the pair studied from inside.
senses.whyCN: 容纳两套系统的心智，是从内部研究的「这一对」。

senses.title: A bilingual dictionary or resource
senses.definition: a reference that gives equivalents in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 给出两种语言对应说法的工具书
senses.example: The bilingual dictionary marks which word fits which register.
senses.exampleCN: 这本双语词典标出哪个词属哪种语域。
senses.why: a dictionary exists to place one language beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 词典的存在，就是把一种语言放在另一种旁边。

senses.title: Bilingual policy or rights
senses.definition: describing official arrangements that guarantee services in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述保障以两种语言提供服务的官方安排
senses.example: Bilingual policy made every statute readable in both tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 双语政策使每项法规都能以两种语言阅读。
senses.why: a promise made in law must appear in both tongues, which turns the count into an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律作出的承诺必须以两种语言出现，这就把数目变成义务。

intro.en: Bilingual comes from Latin bilinguis 'two-tongued', built on bis 'twice' and lingua 'tongue, language'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」，由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and, by extension, 'language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 指「舌头」，引申为「语言」。其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: Bilinguis meant 'two-tongued'. In Roman usage it could also mean 'double-tongued', that is, deceitful, a sense that English did not keep.
items.cn: bilinguis 意为「双舌的」。在罗马用法中它也可指「两面三刀的」，即欺骗性的，这一含义英语没有保留。

items.en: English formed the modern adjective in the nineteenth century, when schooling and censuses made two-language populations visible.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪形成这个现代形容词，当时学校教育与人口普查使双语人群变得可见。

items.en: The twentieth century gave the word a policy life, naming programs that teach in two languages.
items.cn: 二十世纪赋予这个词政策生命，用来指以两种语言教学的项目。

items.en: Psychology and neuroscience later used it for the mental organisation of two language systems.
items.cn: 心理学与神经科学后来用它指两套语言系统在心智中的组织方式。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root is unknown, and the first English use of the modern sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语之前的词根不明，这个现代义在英语中最早使用的年代只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds the counting words that are constantly confused; group two holds terms about two-language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的计数词；第二组是关于两种语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using several languages, often without a fixed count; bilingual is the exact two.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用多种语言，常不限定数目；双语则精确指两种。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole of the same counting series.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是同一计数序列的另一端。

entries.definition: The state or practice of having two languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有两种语言的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A rare word for a person who speaks two languages; bilingual is far commoner as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说两种语言者的罕用名词；双语一词作名词更常见。

entries.definition: A common label for two-language school programs; it is a compound rather than a Latin borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 指双语学校项目的常见标签，属复合词而非拉丁借词。

entries.definition: A literal English rendering of the Latin word; in older use it could also mean deceitful.
entries.definitionCN: 是那个拉丁词的直译英语说法；旧用法中也可指欺骗性的。

entries.definition: Using two dialects of one language, a narrower case than two separate languages.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用同一种语言的两种方言，范围比两种独立语言更窄。

entries.definition: The act of moving between languages in conversation; bilingual describes the capacity behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指会话中在语言间切换的行为；双语描述其背后的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means two and the root means tongue, so the word literally has two tongues.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「二」，词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词字面上就是「有两条舌头」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to services: bilingual signs, forms, help desk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到服务上：双语标识、双语表格、双语服务台。

normal.en: It sits exactly in the middle of the counting ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它正好在计数阶梯的中间：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs bilingualism, bilingually, bilinguals, multilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「双语现象」「以双语方式」「双语者」「多语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A split notice with the same sentence twice is the picture to hold.
normal.cn: 一张左右分栏、同一句话写两遍的告示，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture two doors side by side, both opening into the same room.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两道门，都通向同一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a mind with two indexes to the same world.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑，为同一个世界备有两套索引。

abstract.en: Picture a single sentence walking across a thin line and changing its clothes.
abstract.cn: 想象同一句话跨过一条细线，换了一身衣服。

examples.en: Bilingual ballots were introduced after the court ruling.
examples.cn: 法院裁决之后，双语选票开始启用。

examples.en: Children in bilingual programs read in both languages by nine.
examples.cn: 参加双语项目的孩子到九岁已能用两种语言阅读。

examples.en: The bilingual dictionary distinguishes formal from everyday words.
examples.cn: 这本双语词典区分正式词与日常词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拜林圭尔」——拜两条舌头所赐，两种话都能说，这就是双语的。

root: 拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成；罗马用法中亦可指「两面三刀的」，该贬义未被英语保留。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses pair two languages across a person, a sign, a school, a valley, a mind, a dictionary and a law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两种语言配到人、标牌、学校、山谷、心智、词典与法律之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet folded down the middle, the same sentence on both halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从中间对折的纸，两半写着同一句话。

branches.en: THE COUNT: exactly two languages is the word's whole definition.
branches.cn: 数目：正好两种语言，就是这个词的全部定义。

branches.en: THE SPEAKER: a person can carry both languages through a whole life.
branches.cn: 说话者：一个人可以把两种语言带过一生。

branches.en: WORDS ON PAPER: labels and dictionaries put the two side by side.
branches.cn: 纸上的词：标签与词典把两者并排放置。

branches.en: PLACES THAT TEACH: schools and whole valleys keep two languages alive together.
branches.cn: 教学之地：学校与整条山谷让两种语言一同存活。

branches.en: MIND AND LAW: one brain holds both, and one statute can promise both.
branches.cn: 心智与法律：一个头脑容纳两者，一项法规也能承诺两者。

intro.en: The word is two Latin pieces and an English adjective ending, and each piece also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分与一个英语形容词词尾构成，每个成分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis 'twice' supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the root, and the adjective ending makes the description; the same pieces build multilingual and monolingual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bis「两次」提供计数前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供词根，形容词词尾完成描述；同样的成分也构成「多语的」与「单语的」。

items.example: The prefix fixes the count at exactly two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数目固定为二。

items.example: The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。

items.example: The bilingual form served both communities.
items.exampleCN: 这份双语表格服务两个社群。

items.example: Bilingualism began at home, not at school.
items.exampleCN: 双语现象始于家庭，而非学校。

items.example: The ceremony was conducted bilingually.
items.exampleCN: 仪式以双语进行。

items.example: A multilingual city outgrows the pair.
items.exampleCN: 一座多语城市超出了「两种」的范围。

items.example: Monolingual readers needed a translation.
items.exampleCN: 单语读者需要译本。
