definition_zh: 压迫；不义的统治或制度性压制；沉重压抑的感受
definition_en: the unjust or cruel exercise of power over a group, or the heavy sense of being weighed down
core_image: 一盘沉重的石磨压在一排肩上，磨盘下的地面被压出深深的凹痕
scene: 工厂门口，工人排成长队等候检查，守卫把证件扔回他们脸上，午后的热气压在低矮的屋顶下。 The novel describes the oppression, the unjust weight of rule that kept the whole district silent.
sceneCN: 这里 oppression 指「制度性的不义压制」（第 1 个义项：长期施于群体的沉重统治）；句意为小说描写了让整个街区噤声的那种压迫。可辨识物件：工厂门、长队、证件、守卫、低矮屋顶下的热气。

pos.zh: 压迫；压制；压抑感（可数，复数 oppressions）

derivatives.zh: 压迫；压制
压迫者
压迫性的；沉闷的
受压迫的
镇压；抑制
压制；压抑
按；压；新闻界

senses.title: Systematic unjust rule over a group
senses.titleCN: 对群体的系统性不义统治
senses.definition: the prolonged, unjust exercise of power that keeps a group down
senses.definitionCN: 长期不义地行使权力，使一个群体处于低下地位
senses.example: The novel describes the oppression that kept the whole district silent.
senses.exampleCN: 小说描写了让整个街区噤声的那种压迫。
senses.why: opprimere is ob- 'against' plus premere 'press': power is pressed down on someone until they cannot rise.
senses.whyCN: opprimere 是 ob-「对着」加 premere「压」：权力压在某人身上，直到他起不来。

senses.title: A heavy feeling of being weighed down
senses.definition: a bodily or mental sense of heaviness, tightness or suffocation
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心理上沉重、紧绷或窒息的感受
senses.example: A sudden oppression in the chest made him sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口突然一阵压抑，使他坐了下来。
senses.why: the physical image of pressing explains the feeling: something invisible sits on the breath.
senses.whyCN: 「压」的身体意象解释了这种感受：有某种无形之物压住了呼吸。

senses.title: A specific oppressive act or measure
senses.titleCN: 具体的压迫行为或措施
senses.definition: one law, order or action that imposes unjust burden on people
senses.definitionCN: 给人们施加不义负担的一项法律、命令或行动
senses.example: Each oppression was recorded in the parish ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次压迫都被记在教区账簿里。
senses.why: a system is made of measures, and the countable plural names them one by one.
senses.whyCN: 制度由措施构成，可数复数把它们逐条命名。

senses.title: Economic oppression
senses.definition: exploitative wages, debt, rents or exclusion that keep people poor by design
senses.definitionCN: 有意使人贫穷的剥削性工资、债务、租金或排斥
senses.example: Debt peonage was an economic oppression dressed as contract.
senses.exampleCN: 债务劳役是披着契约外衣的经济压迫。
senses.why: pressure can be applied through prices and contracts, not only through police.
senses.whyCN: 压力可以通过价格与契约施加，而不只是通过警察。

senses.title: Gender or ethnic oppression
senses.definition: structural disadvantage imposed on people because of gender, caste, ethnicity or similar identity
senses.definitionCN: 因性别、种姓、族群等身份而强加的结构性劣势
senses.example: The report documented the oppression of migrant women.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了对移民女性的压迫。
senses.why: the same heavy hand can target a category rather than an individual, which is why the word pairs with identity terms.
senses.whyCN: 同一只重手可以针对一个类别而非个人，因此这个词常与身份词搭配。

senses.title: A historical oppressive regime
senses.definition: a named colonial, caste or authoritarian order studied as a system
senses.definitionCN: 被作为制度研究的殖民、种姓或专制秩序
senses.example: Scholars compare the oppression of two colonial administrations.
senses.exampleCN: 学者比较两套殖民行政的压迫方式。
senses.why: historians treat oppression as an institutional design, not only as individual cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 历史学家把压迫当作制度设计，而不只是个人残忍。

senses.title: Metaphor: psychological or environmental weight
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心理或环境的重压
senses.definition: by extension, any atmosphere or mood that makes people feel small and tired
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何使人感到渺小而疲惫的气氛或情绪
senses.example: A grey sky added its own oppression to the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 灰暗的天空给这个下午添了一层自己的压抑。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the stone's weight to air, light and mood.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把石头的重量转移到空气、光线与情绪上。

senses.title: Abstraction: any force that contracts freedom
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：收缩自由的力量
senses.definition: any structure or pressure that narrows a person's or group's room to act
senses.definitionCN: 任何缩小个人或群体行动空间的结构或压力
senses.example: Oppression is freedom compressed until it cannot breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 压迫是被压缩到无法呼吸的自由。
senses.why: the deepest sense is spatial: the hand does not only hurt, it reduces the space in which one can move.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是空间性的：那只手不仅造成疼痛，还缩小了可行动的空间。

intro.en: Oppression comes from Latin opprimere, ob- 'against' plus premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oppression 来自拉丁 opprimere，由 ob-「对着」与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opprimere meant 'to press against, crush, overwhelm', built from ob- 'against, toward' and premere 'to press'.
items.cn: opprimere 意为「压向、压碎、压倒」，由 ob-「对着、朝向」与 premere「压」构成。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze'; its deeper origin is usually reconstructed with a root for striking, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」；其更深来源通常以一个表示「击打」的词根重构，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Oppressio named a pressing down or crushing; the noun carried the physical weight of the verb into abstract use.
items.cn: oppressio 指压下或压碎；这个名词把动词的身体重量带入抽象用法。

items.en: Oppression entered English through Old French in the fourteenth century, first as a general word for crushing or burden.
items.cn: oppression 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，最初泛指压碎或重负。

items.en: The political sense of unjust rule took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and dominates modern usage.
items.cn: 不义统治的政治义在十七、十八世纪成形，并主导现代用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (political sense date and root shape): the exact point at which the word became primarily political is not fixed, and the pre-Latin root of premere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（政治义年代与词根形态）：这个词何时主要转为政治义并无定论，premere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds press-root words that are easily swapped with oppression; group two holds neighbouring ideas of unjust power.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」词根、易与 oppression 互换的词；第二组是不义权力的邻近概念。

entries.definition: From sub- 'down' plus premere: the act of putting something down by force, such as a revolt or a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 sub-「向下」加 premere：以武力压下某物，如叛乱或事实。

entries.definition: From re- 'back' plus premere: keeping something from emerging, often used for impulses or dissent.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 re-「向后」加 premere：阻止某物浮现，常用于冲动或异议。

entries.definition: From de- 'down' plus premere: a lowered state, whether of ground, economy or mood. It is not a political term.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 de-「向下」加 premere：被压低的状态，可为地面、经济或情绪，并非政治术语。

entries.definition: From com- 'together' plus premere: squeezing into less space, a physical rather than social process.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 com-「一起」加 premere：压进更小空间，是物理过程而非社会过程。

entries.definition: Cruel and arbitrary rule by one person or a small clique; oppression can be impersonal and institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 指一人或小集团的残暴专断统治；oppression 可以是非个人的、制度性的。

entries.definition: Taking advantage of people's labour or weakness for profit; it is one engine of economic oppression.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用他人劳动或弱点获利；它是经济压迫的一种引擎。

entries.definition: Treating people differently because of identity; it can occur without a heavy system of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指因身份而区别对待；可以没有沉重的统治体系。

entries.definition: The act of conquering and subjecting a people; it stresses the moment of defeat more than daily pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指征服并使一个民族臣服；更强调被击败的时刻，而非日常压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the press-root family and the bodily image of weight.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、press 词根家族，以及「重量」的身体意象。

normal.en: ob- 'against' + premere 'press': a hand pressing against someone until they cannot stand.
normal.cn: ob-「对着」+ premere「压」：一只手压在人身上，直到他站不起来。

normal.en: The family runs press, pressure, compress, suppress, repress, depress, oppress.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 press、pressure、compress、suppress、repress、depress、oppress。

normal.en: The prefixes show direction: sub- down, re- back, de- down, com- together, ob- against.
normal.cn: 前缀显示方向：sub- 向下、re- 向后、de- 向下、com- 一起、ob- 对着。

normal.en: Oppression has both a political sense and a bodily sense of heavy breathing.
normal.cn: oppression 既有政治义，也有呼吸沉重的身体义。

normal.en: Typical partners are live under, escape, systematic and economic.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「生活在……之下」「逃离」「系统性的」与「经济的」。

abstract.en: Picture a stone lid placed over a pot so that nothing can rise out.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板盖住锅口，使任何东西都升不出来。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose walls move inward a little each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，墙壁每年向内挪一点。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that weighs a person every morning and never lets the needle fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一台每天早上称人的秤，指针从不肯下落。

examples.en: The characters speak quietly because oppression has taught them caution.
examples.cn: 人物说话很轻，因为压迫教会了他们谨慎。

examples.en: Economic oppression can outlast the laws that created it.
examples.cn: 经济压迫可能比造成它的法律活得更久。

examples.en: The painting conveys the oppression of a low ceiling and a grey light.
examples.cn: 这幅画传达了低矮天花板与灰光的压抑感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「op（对着）+ press（压）」——一直对着人往下压 → 压迫

root: 拉丁 opprimere「压向、压倒」= ob-（对着）+ premere（压）；名词 oppressio。premere 的更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one gesture: a weight is pressed down. The weight becomes a political system, then a bodily feeling, then single measures, then economic and identity-based forms, then a historical regime, then a mood and finally any narrowing of freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个动作展开：把重量压下去。这个重量先成为政治制度，再成为身体感受，再成为单项措施，再成为经济与身份形式，再成为历史政权，再成为气氛，最后成为对自由的任何收窄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a millstone resting on a row of shoulders, the ground dented beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘石磨压在一排肩上，地面被压出凹痕。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND ITS MEASURES: rule is applied one order at a time.
branches.cn: 制度与措施：统治是按一条条命令施加的。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT FELT: the stone becomes breath, sky and mood.
branches.cn: 感到的重量：石头变成呼吸、天空与情绪。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND THE CATEGORY: money and identity are two faces of the same hand.
branches.cn: 物质与类别：金钱与身份是同一只手的两个面。

branches.en: THE REGIME: historians study oppression as an institutional design.
branches.cn: 政权：历史学家把压迫当作制度设计来研究。

branches.en: THE SHRUNKEN ROOM: the deepest sense is reduced space for action.
branches.cn: 收缩的房间：最深的一层是行动空间的缩小。

intro.en: Oppression is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb root, and the same root builds a whole family of pressing words in English.
intro.cn: oppression 是拉丁前缀加拉丁动词词根，同一词根在英语中构成整个「压」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere gives press, pressure, compress, suppress, repress and depress; ob- adds the sense of pressing against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 premere 衍生 press、pressure、compress、suppress、repress 与 depress；ob- 增添「对着压」的意思。

items.example: The prefix gives the pressure a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给压力一个方向。

items.example: The root is the physical act of pressing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是「压」这个身体动作。

items.example: The Latin verb joined direction and weight.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词把方向与重量结合起来。

items.example: Oppression can be a policy, not only a temper.
items.exampleCN: 压迫可以是一项政策，而不只是脾气。

items.example: The rules oppressed the poorest tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则压制了最贫穷的佃户。

items.example: The oppressor feared the square at noon.
items.exampleCN: 压迫者害怕正午的广场。

items.example: The heat was oppressive by ten o'clock.
items.exampleCN: 到十点，热气已经令人窒息。

items.example: Press the seal into the wax.
items.exampleCN: 把印章压进蜡里。

items.example: The officers suppressed the protest.
items.exampleCN: 官员镇压了抗议。

items.example: She repressed the urge to answer.
items.exampleCN: 她压下了回嘴的冲动。

definition_zh: 熔岩；熔岩流；熔岩冷却形成的岩石；熔岩穹丘；熔岩管；枕状熔岩；比喻大量涌出之物；熔岩灯
definition_en: molten rock that has reached a planet's surface and flows from a volcano, or the solid rock it forms when it cools
core_image: 火山口边缘，暗红的黏稠流体沿斜坡推进，表面结出黑色硬壳，壳缝里透出橙色光
scene: 夜里的山坡上，暗红色流体一边移动一边结壳，缓慢逼近远处的房屋。 A river of lava cut across the road and reached the sea by dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 lava 指流出地表的熔岩（第 1 个义项：到达地表并正在流动的高温熔融岩石）；句意为一条熔岩流横穿公路，天亮时抵达海边。

pos.zh: 熔岩（到达地表的熔融岩石）
熔岩流；熔岩冷却形成的岩石
熔岩灯；（比喻）大量涌出之物

derivatives.zh: 熔岩的；似熔岩的（较少见，地质学用）
熔岩般的；像熔岩那样炽热流动的
熔岩流（复合术语，指流动的熔岩体及其堆积）
熔岩穹丘（复合术语，黏稠熔岩堆成的圆丘）
熔岩管（复合术语，熔岩流内部排空后留下的隧道）

senses.title: Molten rock at the surface
senses.definition: molten rock that has reached the surface through a vent
senses.definitionCN: 通过火山口到达地表的熔融岩石
senses.example: Lava poured from a fissure on the flank of the cone.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩从锥体侧面的裂缝中涌出。
senses.why: lava names the melt only after it is exposed; while it is underground the same material is still magma.
senses.whyCN: lava 只在这团熔体露出地表之后才这么叫；它在地下时仍是 magma。

senses.title: A stream of lava
senses.definition: a flowing body of lava moving down a slope, or the deposit it leaves
senses.definitionCN: 沿坡面流动的熔岩体，或它留下的堆积物
senses.example: The lava flow stopped two hundred metres from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩流在离村庄两百米处停住。
senses.why: the moving stream became a countable thing, so the word can name one flow as well as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 流动的熔岩被当作可数的个体，于是该词既能指物质，也能指一条熔岩流。

senses.title: The rock that lava becomes
senses.definition: the solid igneous rock formed when a lava flow cools, commonly basalt
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩流冷却后形成的坚硬火成岩，常见为玄武岩
senses.example: The cliff is made of lava that hardened under water.
senses.exampleCN: 这道崖壁由在水下硬结的熔岩构成。
senses.why: once cooled, the material keeps the name of its molten stage, so the product inherits the word.
senses.whyCN: 冷却之后，这种材料仍沿用熔融阶段的名称，于是产物继承了该词。

senses.title: A dome of thick lava
senses.definition: a rounded mound built by viscous lava piling up around a vent
senses.definitionCN: 黏稠熔岩在火山口周围堆叠而成的圆丘
senses.example: The lava dome grew by several metres each week.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩穹丘每周增高数米。
senses.why: stiff lava cannot run far, so it stacks into a dome, and the compound records that behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 黏稠的熔岩流不远，只能堆成穹丘，这个复合词记录了这种行为。

senses.title: A tube left by a lava flow
senses.definition: a hollow tunnel formed when the surface of a lava flow crusts over while the molten interior drains away
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩流表面结壳、内部熔体排空后留下的空心隧道
senses.example: The lava tube ran for six kilometres beneath the field.
senses.exampleCN: 这条熔岩管从田野下方延伸六公里。
senses.why: the crust freezes first, the interior keeps moving, and the empty channel survives as a tube.
senses.whyCN: 表层先凝固，内部继续流动，排空后的通道便作为管道留存。

senses.title: Pillow lava
senses.definition: bulbous, pillow-shaped masses of lava formed where lava is erupted under water
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩在水下喷出时形成的球状、枕状团块
senses.example: Pillow lava on the sea floor showed the eruption had been submarine.
senses.exampleCN: 海底的枕状熔岩表明这次喷发发生在水下。
senses.why: water chills the outside instantly, so each pulse of lava freezes as a rounded pillow.
senses.whyCN: 水使外层瞬间冷却，于是每一股熔岩都冻成圆枕状。

senses.title: A flood of something
senses.definition: a figurative use for something that pours out in great quantity, often hot or unstoppable
senses.definitionCN: 比喻大量涌出之物，常带灼热或不可阻挡的意味
senses.example: Lava of complaints poured into the office after the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 产品上线后，投诉如熔岩般涌进办公室。
senses.why: the image keeps heat and unstoppable flow, so the word suggests something that cannot be held back.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象保留了高温与不可阻挡的流动，因此暗示无法被拦住的东西。

senses.title: The lava lamp
senses.definition: a decorative lamp in which blobs of coloured wax rise and fall in heated liquid, named for their look
senses.definitionCN: 一种装饰灯，加热液体中彩色蜡块升降起伏，因其外观而得名
senses.example: A lava lamp glowed on the shelf beside the old record player.
senses.exampleCN: 旧唱机旁的架子上亮着一盏熔岩灯。
senses.why: the wax blobs mimic rising and sinking lava, so a cultural object borrowed the geological word.
senses.whyCN: 蜡块升降的样子模仿熔岩，于是一件文化物件借用了这个地质词。

intro.en: Lava entered English from Italian, specifically the Neapolitan dialect, where lava meant a torrent or stream. Its deeper origin is disputed: one common hypothesis links it to Latin labes, a fall or slide, from labi, to slip; others suggest Latin lavare, to wash, or a local pre-Roman word. It is not a direct Latin inheritance, and no single origin is settled.
intro.cn: lava 经意大利语、具体是那不勒斯方言进入英语，方言中 lava 指急流或水流。其更深来源有争议：一种常见假说把它联系到拉丁 labes「坠落、滑落」，出自 labi「滑落」；也有人提出拉丁 lavare「洗」，或当地前罗马时期的词。它不是拉丁语的直接继承词，也没有定论。

items.en: In the Naples dialect lava meant a torrent, especially a stream of rain water rushing down a slope.
items.cn: 在那不勒斯方言中，lava 指急流，尤指雨水沿坡冲下的水流。

items.en: One hypothesis derives the dialect word from Latin labes, a fall or sliding, from labi, to slip; the image of sliding material fits a lava flow, but the chain is unproven.
items.cn: 一种假说把方言词追溯到拉丁 labes「坠落、滑落」，出自 labi「滑落」；「滑落之物」的意象与熔岩流相合，但这条例证链未被证实。

items.en: Other suggestions connect lava to Latin lavare, to wash, or to a pre-Roman local word; scholars have not agreed, so no single origin is asserted here.
items.cn: 其他说法把 lava 联系到拉丁 lavare「洗」，或联系到前罗马时期的当地词；学界未达成一致，因此此处不指定单一来源。

items.en: English travellers and naturalists brought the word home in the eighteenth century, describing Vesuvius and Etna.
items.cn: 英语世界的旅行者与博物学家在十八世纪把这个词带回，用于描述维苏威火山与埃特纳火山。

items.en: Geology built a family of compounds: lava flow, lava dome, lava tube, pillow lava, each naming a shape the melt takes.
items.cn: 地质学构造了一族复合词：熔岩流、熔岩穹丘、熔岩管、枕状熔岩，各自指熔体的一种形态。

items.en: Source uncertain (root in doubt): the Italian route is well documented, but the deeper origin is unsettled; it is generally thought to be related to Latin labes, a fall, while lavare, to wash, and a pre-Roman local word are competing hypotheses, so no single source is chosen; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：意大利语这条路径有充分记录；但更深的来源未定，一般认为是与拉丁 labes「坠落」有关的假说，另有 lavare「洗」及前罗马时期当地词等说法并列，不选定论；英语首见的确切年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms; group two holds the terms that overlap with lava in geology.
note.cn: 第一组是形近形式；第二组是在地质学中与熔岩重叠的术语。

entries.definition: The immature form of an insect or other animal; the spelling differs by a single letter and the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 昆虫或其他动物的幼体；拼写只差一个字母，意义毫无关联。

entries.definition: A rare adjective meaning of or like lava, used mainly in geological writing.
entries.definitionCN: 少见形容词，意为熔岩的或似熔岩的，主要用于地质写作。

entries.definition: The regular plural, used when counting separate flows or types of melt.
entries.definitionCN: 规则复数，用于计数不同的熔岩流或熔岩类型。

entries.definition: The decorative lamp whose wax blobs suggested the name, now the best-known non-geological use.
entries.definitionCN: 那种蜡块让人联想到熔岩的装饰灯，如今是该词最知名的非地质用法。

entries.definition: The same molten rock before it reaches the surface; the two words mark stages, not different substances.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种熔融岩石在到达地表之前的名称；两词标记的是阶段，而非不同物质。

entries.definition: A neutral description of rock heated to liquid, avoiding the technical stage terms.
entries.definitionCN: 对加热成液态的岩石的中性描述，避开阶段术语。

entries.definition: The dark, fine-grained rock most lava flows become; it names the product after cooling.
entries.definitionCN: 多数熔岩流冷却后形成的深色细粒岩石；指冷却后的产物。

entries.definition: Any moving mass of material; lava flow narrows it to molten rock and its deposit.
entries.definitionCN: 任何流动的物质团；熔岩流把它收窄到熔融岩石及其堆积物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Italian dialect source, the real magma boundary and the real compound series.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的意大利方言来源、真实的岩浆分界，以及真实的复合词系列。

normal.en: The dialect word first meant a torrent running down a slope, then settled on the molten stream from a volcano.
normal.cn: 这个方言词本指沿坡冲下的急流，后来固定指火山流出的熔融流体。

normal.en: Underground it is magma, at the surface it is lava: one substance, two stages.
normal.cn: 地下叫岩浆，地表叫熔岩：同一种物质，两个阶段。

normal.en: The compounds line up by shape: lava flow, lava dome, lava tube, pillow lava.
normal.cn: 复合词按形态排开：熔岩流、熔岩穹丘、熔岩管、枕状熔岩。

normal.en: After cooling the material is still called lava, though it has become dark basalt.
normal.cn: 冷却之后，这种材料仍叫熔岩，只是已成了深色玄武岩。

normal.en: The lava lamp is the one everyday use: wax blobs rise and fall as if lava flowed inside the glass.
normal.cn: 熔岩灯是唯一日常可见的用法：蜡块升降，仿佛玻璃里有熔岩在流。

abstract.en: Picture honey falling from a spoon, thickening as it goes, a skin forming first.
abstract.cn: 想象蜂蜜从勺上缓慢垂落，越流越厚，表面先结一层皮。

abstract.en: Picture thick porridge tipped onto a table, still bubbling at the centre while the edge hardens.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅浓粥倒在桌上，中心还在冒泡，边缘已经硬了。

abstract.en: Picture a dark moving line at night whose colour can only be guessed.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一条移动的暗线，颜色只能靠猜。

examples.en: Lava from the fissure flowed into the valley for three days.
examples.cn: 裂缝中的熔岩流入山谷，持续了三天。

examples.en: The lava had cooled into a dark, glassy crust.
examples.cn: 熔岩冷却成一层深色、带玻璃光泽的硬壳。

examples.en: Tourists queued to watch the wax blobs rise in the lava lamp.
examples.cn: 游客排队观看熔岩灯里蜡块升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 意大利方言「急流」——从火山口冲出的流动物 → 熔岩

root: 意大利语（那不勒斯方言）lava「急流」进入英语作 lava；更深来源未定，或与拉丁 labes「坠落、滑落」有关（仅属假说），亦有人提出拉丁 lavare「洗」；并非拉丁语直接继承词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the melt after it escapes: first the substance at the surface, then the stream it forms, the rock it becomes, three shapes cooling gives it, a figurative flood, and finally a cultural object named after the look.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟踪熔体逃出地表之后的经历：先是在地表的物质，然后是它形成的流体、它变成的岩石、冷却赋予它的三种形态、比喻性的涌流，最后是以其外观命名的文化物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glowing paste that has escaped its rock lid and now crawls over the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团逃出岩石盖子的灼热糊状物，正在地面上爬行。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND FLOW: the exposed melt and the moving body it makes.
branches.cn: 物质与流动：露出地表的熔体，以及它形成的流动体。

branches.en: COOLED PRODUCT: the melt keeps its name after it hardens into dark rock.
branches.cn: 冷却产物：熔体硬结成深色岩石后仍沿用原名。

branches.en: SHAPES OF FLOW: a dome, a tube and a pillow are three ways the same melt freezes in place.
branches.cn: 流动的形态：穹丘、管道与枕状体，是同一熔体在原地冻住的三种方式。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE FLOOD: heat and unstoppable motion carry over to anything pouring out.
branches.cn: 比喻涌流：高温与不可阻挡的运动被移用到一切大量涌出之物。

branches.en: CULTURAL OBJECT: a lamp borrows the look of rising and sinking melt.
branches.cn: 文化物件：一盏灯借用了熔体升降的外观。

intro.en: Lava has no Latin prefixes or suffixes of its own; it arrived as a whole dialect word, so the items below are compounds and borrowed combining forms rather than true affixes.
intro.cn: lava 没有自己的拉丁前缀或后缀；它作为一个完整的方言词传入，因此下列条目是复合形式与借入的组合成分，而非真正的词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries are listed: lava is not inherited from Latin, and its possible Latin links are hypotheses rather than a derivational family.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不列拉丁词条：lava 并非由拉丁语继承而来，其可能的拉丁联系只是假说，而非一个派生词族。

items.meaning: torrent; molten rock at the surface
items.example: The word arrived whole, without a Latin prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个词整体传入，没有拉丁前缀。

items.meaning: noun ending, not a suffix of meaning
items.example: The final -a is an Italian noun ending, not an English suffix.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -a 是意大利语的名词结尾，不是英语后缀。

items.example: The flow reached the road by noon.
items.exampleCN: 熔岩流在正午前抵达公路。

items.example: The dome cracked as it grew.
items.exampleCN: 穹丘在增长时开裂。

items.example: The tube held a cold river of air.
items.exampleCN: 管道里流着一股冷空气。

items.example: Pillow lava records a submarine eruption.
items.exampleCN: 枕状熔岩记录了水下喷发。

items.example: The lamp was a gift from a friend.
items.exampleCN: 这盏灯是朋友的礼物。

items.example: Lavic deposits line the valley.
items.exampleCN: 谷底两侧分布着熔岩沉积。

items.structure: Old English molten, past participle of melt
items.example: Molten rock glows dull red.
items.exampleCN: 熔化的岩石发出暗红的光。

items.example: Basalt forms most of the ocean floor.
items.exampleCN: 玄武岩构成大部分海底。

definition_zh: 港口；港市；端口；左舷；（把舵）转向左舷；波尔图葡萄酒
definition_en: a harbor where ships load and unload, an opening on a device for a cable, the left side of a ship, a fortified wine from Porto, or to turn a ship to the left
core_image: 码头边一排起重机，一艘货轮把船头缓缓靠向岸壁
scene: 黎明前的海湾里，灯塔还亮着，一艘货轮正慢慢靠上码头。 By dawn the cargo ship had entered the port and begun to unload.
sceneCN: 这里 port 是「港口」（第 1 个义项：船只装卸货物的港湾）；句意为天亮时货轮已经进港开始卸货。图中可辨识物件：海湾、灯塔、货轮、码头。

pos.zh: 港口；港市；端口；左舷；波尔图葡萄酒
把舵转向左舷；使船靠左

derivatives.zh: 由 air 与 port（港口、停靠地）复合，义为「机场」
由 sea 与 port 复合，义为「海港；港市」
由拉丁 porta（门）加 -al 构成，义为「门户；入口」
由 port 加 -age 构成，义为「水陆之间的搬运；搬运费」

senses.title: A harbor where ships load and unload
senses.definition: a place on a coast or river where ships can tie up and where goods and passengers are loaded or unloaded
senses.definitionCN: 海岸或河边供船只停靠、装卸货物和上下旅客的地方
senses.example: The fishing boats return to port before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在暴风雨来临前回到港口。
senses.why: Latin portus named a sheltered place where a ship could lie safely; English borrowed it early, so the first sense is simply that stopping place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portus 指船只能安全停靠的有遮蔽之处；英语借入得很早，所以第一个义项就是这个停靠点本身。

senses.title: A socket for a cable or device
senses.definition: an opening or socket on a computer or machine where a cable, plug or storage device is connected
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或机器上用来连接线缆、插头或存储设备的开口或插槽
senses.example: Plug the monitor into the port at the back of the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 把显示器插到机器背面的接口上。
senses.why: A port is also a gateway, a sense that came through Latin porta, a door; the socket is the narrow doorway through which signals enter and leave a machine.
senses.whyCN: port 也曾指「门户」，这一支经拉丁语 porta（门）而来；插槽就是信号进出机器的那道窄门。

senses.title: The left side of a ship
senses.definition: the left-hand side of a ship or aircraft when you are facing the front
senses.definitionCN: 面朝船头或机头时，船或飞机的左侧
senses.example: The lighthouse passed along the port side as the ship turned.
senses.exampleCN: 船转向时，灯塔从船的左舷掠过。
senses.why: One common explanation is that ships tied up with their loading side to the quay, so the harbor side became the name for the left; the derivation is still debated.
senses.whyCN: 一种常见解释是，船进港时把装卸的一侧靠向码头，于是「靠港的那一边」成了左舷的名字；这一来源仍有争论。

senses.title: A fortified wine from Porto
senses.definition: a sweet, strong red wine made in the Douro valley and shipped through the city of Porto
senses.definitionCN: 在杜罗河谷酿造、经波尔图城运出的甜型高度红葡萄酒
senses.example: They finished dinner with a glass of port and some cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以一杯波尔图葡萄酒配奶酪结束了晚餐。
senses.why: The drink took its English name from Porto, the Portuguese city at the river mouth, so a place name shrank into a short everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这种酒的英语名取自河口城市波尔图，于是一个地名缩成了日常使用的短词。

senses.title: To turn a ship to the left
senses.definition: to turn a ship or its helm towards the left side
senses.definitionCN: 把船或船舵转向左侧
senses.example: The captain ported the helm to avoid the drifting buoy.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把舵转向左舷，避开漂来的浮标。
senses.why: Once port names the left side, the verb applies that direction to steering: to port the helm is to send the bow that way.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 port 成为左舷的名称，动词就把这个方向用到操舵上：把舵转向左舷，就是让船头朝那边摆。

intro.en: The short word port joins three Latin threads: portus, a harbor, porta, a gate, and the wine named after the city of Porto.
intro.cn: 这个短词 port 汇合了三条拉丁线索：portus（港口）、porta（门），以及得名于波尔图城的葡萄酒。

items.en: Portus meant a harbor or haven, a sheltered place where a ship could lie safely; it is generally connected with an old root for passing through or crossing.
items.cn: portus 意为港口、避风处，是船只能安全停泊的有遮蔽之处；一般认为它与表示「穿过、越过」的古老词根有关。

items.en: Porta meant a gate or door, and it is the source of port in the sense of an opening, including the socket on a computer.
items.cn: porta 意为大门、出入口；表示「开口」的 port 就来自这里，电脑上的插口也属于这一支。

items.en: English borrowed port for a harbor from Latin, partly through Old French; by the Middle Ages it named both seaports and gateways.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借来表示港口的 port，其中一部分经古法语传入；到中世纪，它既指海港，也指出入口。

items.en: Port came to name the left side of a ship, usually explained by the side laid against the quay for loading; the explanation is not certain.
items.cn: port 开始指船的左舷，通常解释为进港装卸时靠向码头的那一侧；这一解释并不确定。

items.en: Porto in Portugal gave port wine its name, while computing made port a socket for cables and signals.
items.cn: 葡萄牙的波尔图给了波尔图葡萄酒这个名字，计算机则让 port 成为线缆与信号用的插口。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and relatives of the short form; the near-meaning group gathers words for sheltered water and places where ships tie up.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个短词构成的复合词与同族词；近义组收表示避风水域与船只停靠处的词。

entries.definition: A place where aircraft take off and land, built on port in the old sense of a stopping place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 air 与 port 复合，指飞机起降的机场；这里的 port 保留了「停靠地」的旧义。

entries.definition: A town or city with a harbor used by seagoing ships.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sea 与 port 复合，指拥有海港的城市。

entries.definition: A doorway or entrance, especially a large one; from Latin porta.
entries.definitionCN: 与表示「门」的 port 同出拉丁 porta，义为门户、入口。

entries.definition: Able to be carried; built on Latin portare, a different source from the harbor word.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但来自拉丁 portare（搬运），与「港口」的 port 不是同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: A sheltered body of water where ships can stay safely.
entries.definitionCN: 港湾；强调有遮蔽、可避风，与港口近义。

entries.definition: A structure at the water's edge where a ship is loaded, repaired or kept.
entries.definitionCN: 码头；船坞；强调靠岸装卸或修船的具体设施。

entries.definition: A flat platform at a harbor where ships are loaded and unloaded.
entries.definitionCN: 码头；强调沿岸用于装卸的平台。

entries.definition: A small harbor designed for pleasure boats.
entries.definitionCN: 游艇码头；专供休闲船只停泊的小港。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on Latin portus for a harbor, and the same spelling has picked up a gate, a ship's side and a wine along the way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于表示港口的拉丁语 portus，同一个拼写沿途又接上了门、船舷与一种酒。

normal.en: Port comes from Latin portus, a harbor, and English had the word early enough to use it for any place a ship stops.
normal.cn: port 来自拉丁语 portus（港口），英语借入很早，凡船停靠之处都能用它。

normal.en: A computer port is a gate for signals, which is why this sense goes back to Latin porta, a door, rather than to portus.
normal.cn: 电脑端口是信号进出的门，所以这一义项上溯的是拉丁语 porta（门），而不是 portus。

normal.en: Port side is the left side of a ship; the usual explanation is that the loading side lay against the quay in harbor.
normal.cn: port side 是船的左舷；常见解释是装卸的一侧在港里靠着码头。

normal.en: Port wine is named after Porto, the Portuguese city at the mouth of the Douro.
normal.cn: port wine 得名于杜罗河口的葡萄牙城市波尔图。

normal.en: Airport and seaport stretch port from a harbor to any place where vehicles stop and load.
normal.cn: airport 与 seaport 把 port 从港湾扩展到任何车辆停靠、装卸的地方。

abstract.en: A harbor is where a journey pauses, so one short word can name a ship's rest, a signal's doorway and a glass at the end of dinner.
abstract.cn: 港口是旅程暂停的地方，所以一个短词既能指船的歇脚处，也能指信号的门口和晚餐末尾的一杯酒。

abstract.en: A port is a controlled opening: water, people and data all pass through a narrow gate that can be watched.
abstract.cn: 端口是一道受控的开口：水、人和数据都得从一道可以被看守的窄门通过。

abstract.en: The left side of a ship is named from the shore it once faced, a reminder that directions are often borrowed from land.
abstract.cn: 船的左舷用它曾经面对的岸来命名，这提醒人：方向常常是从陆地借来的。

examples.en: By dawn the cargo ship had entered the port and begun to unload.
examples.cn: 天亮时货轮已经进港开始卸货。

examples.en: Plug the monitor into the port at the back of the machine.
examples.cn: 把显示器插到机器背面的接口上。

examples.en: They finished dinner with a glass of port and some cheese.
examples.cn: 他们以一杯波尔图葡萄酒配奶酪结束了晚餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波特」——船停在港湾里卸货，杯里也盛着波尔图来的甜酒；port 就是港口，也是端口、左舷与波尔图酒。

root: port 背后有三条拉丁线：portus（港口、避风处）、porta（门，电脑端口由此而来）与 portare（搬运，portable、porter 由此而来）；三者深层同源，但在拉丁语里是彼此不同的词。port wine 则得名于葡萄牙城市波尔图。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheltered place where movement stops; the senses branch into the harbor, the gate for signals, the ship's left side, the wine of Porto and the act of turning that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是运动暂停的有遮蔽之处；义项由此分出港口、信号的门、船左舷、波尔图酒，以及朝那边转舵的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes along a quay, a freighter easing its bow towards the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：码头边一排起重机，一艘货轮把船头缓缓靠向岸壁。

branches.en: a cable clicking into a socket at the back of a machine
branches.cn: 线缆咔哒一声插进机器背面的插槽

branches.en: a lighthouse sliding past the left rail of a ship
branches.cn: 灯塔从船左侧的栏杆旁滑过

branches.cn: 船舵转向，让船头朝码头一侧摆去

intro.en: The form is short, but it carries three Latin nouns: a harbor, a gate and a carrying verb that also built portable and porter.
intro.cn: 这个词形很短，却背着三个拉丁名词：港口、门，以及一个也造出了 portable 与 porter 的「搬运」动词。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words stand behind this short form: portus for a harbor, porta for a gate, and portare for carrying; they are related at a deeper level but were separate words in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短词背后有三个拉丁词：portus（港口）、porta（门）与 portare（搬运）；它们在更早的层次上相关，但在拉丁语里是彼此独立的词。

definition_zh: 证伪；证明为假；伪造；篡改（记录、数据、账目）；（哲学）可证伪性方法中的反证环节
definition_en: the act of showing that a statement or theory is false, or of making a document or record false
core_image: 一支笔把文件上原本的数字划掉，改写成另一个数字，墨迹还压在纸面上
scene: 档案馆里有人把原始记录的年份悄悄改早，后来的研究者用同位素检测发现了这处改动。 The historian exposed a falsification of the archive record that had stood for sixty years.
sceneCN: 这里指对记录、数据的篡改（第 3 个义项：伪造、篡改）；句意为这位历史学家揭穿了一处冒充了六十年的档案篡改。场景图取象：文件上的数字被划掉改写。

pos.zh: 证伪；证明为假（不可数）
伪造；篡改（文件、数据、账目）
（哲学）证伪；反证的一次具体操作

derivatives.zh: 证伪；伪造（由「假」与「做」两个拉丁词根合成，字面即「使之为假」）
可证伪的（加表示「能够被……」的形容词后缀，指一种说法能被事实推翻）
证伪者；伪造者（加表示「施动者」的名词后缀，兼指做实验推翻理论与造假两种人）
虚假；不实（由「假」的形容词加表示「性质」的名词后缀构成）
谎言；虚假陈述（英语本族语复合词，指不实之事）
证伪主义（在证伪后加表示「学说」的后缀，指以能否被推翻来判断科学性的主张）

senses.title: Showing a claim is false
senses.definition: the act of proving that a statement, belief or theory is false
senses.definitionCN: 证明一个说法、信念或理论为假的行为
senses.example: The falsification of the rumour took only one document.
senses.exampleCN: 推翻那个传闻只用了一份文件。
senses.why: The word is built as 'making false', and the oldest sense is exactly that: bringing a claim down.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「使之为假」构成，最古老的义项正就是这个：把一种说法打翻。

senses.title: The test that could fail
senses.definition: in the philosophy of science, a test so framed that a negative result would count against the theory
senses.definitionCN: 在科学哲学中，设计得使否定结果足以打击该理论的一次检验
senses.example: Popper made falsification the mark of a scientific claim.
senses.exampleCN: 波普尔把证伪立为科学主张的标志。
senses.why: A theory that cannot lose is not being tested; the power to be shown false is what makes a test real.
senses.whyCN: 不会输的理论并没有受检；能被证明为假的力量，才让检验成其为检验。

senses.title: Doctoring a record
senses.definition: the deliberate alteration of a document, data set or account so that it misrepresents the facts
senses.definitionCN: 故意改动文件、数据集或账目，使其歪曲事实
senses.example: The audit found falsification of three quarterly reports.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现三份季度报告被篡改。
senses.why: The same verb that means proving false also means making false, and paperwork is where the second sense lives.
senses.whyCN: 既表示「证明为假」又表示「使之为假」的同一个动词，第二层意思就落在纸面上。

senses.title: A refuting instance
senses.definition: a single observation or case that contradicts a general statement and thereby disproves it
senses.definitionCN: 与一般性陈述相抵触、从而推翻它的一条观察或事例
senses.example: One falsification is enough to sink a universal claim.
senses.exampleCN: 一条反证就足以推翻一个全称主张。
senses.why: Universal claims promise everything without exception, so one exception makes the promise false.
senses.whyCN: 全称主张承诺无一例外，因此一个例外就让这承诺为假。

senses.title: Forgery of a signature
senses.definition: the forging of a signature, document or certificate so that it appears genuine
senses.definitionCN: 伪造签名、文件或证书，使其看起来像真品
senses.example: Falsification of a passport is a criminal offence.
senses.exampleCN: 伪造护照是刑事犯罪。
senses.why: Forgery makes a false thing pass as true, which is the 'making false' branch in its legal form.
senses.whyCN: 伪造让假东西冒充真东西，这是「使之为假」一脉在法律上的形态。

senses.title: Research misconduct
senses.definition: the fabrication or manipulation of research data, images or results
senses.definitionCN: 编造或操纵研究数据、图像或结果
senses.example: The journal retracted the paper after evidence of falsification.
senses.exampleCN: 有造假证据后，期刊撤下了那篇论文。
senses.why: Modern universities separate honest error from falsification, because only the second is misconduct.
senses.whyCN: 现代大学把诚实的错误与造假分开，因为只有后者才算不端。

senses.title: False accounting
senses.definition: the falsification of financial accounts, invoices or tax records
senses.definitionCN: 对财务账目、发票或税务记录的作假
senses.example: He was charged with falsification of company accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控对公司账目作假。
senses.why: Law names the offence after the act, and accounts are the documents most often made false.
senses.whyCN: 法律以动作命名罪名，而账目是最常被做假的文件。

senses.title: The state of being disproved
senses.definition: the condition of a statement that has been shown to be false
senses.definitionCN: 某一说法已被证明为假的状态
senses.example: The falsification of that model came from its own predictions.
senses.exampleCN: 那个模型是被它自己的预测推翻的。
senses.why: The noun can name the outcome as well as the act, so a theory can be said to suffer falsification.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指结果而非动作，所以说一个理论遭到证伪。

senses.title: A counterfeit copy
senses.definition: a copy or imitation made to be taken for the genuine article
senses.definitionCN: 被做出来冒充真品的复制件或仿制品
senses.example: The museum rejected the painting as a falsification.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆认定这幅画是赝品而拒收。
senses.why: A false copy is a thing made false in the literal sense, and the word carries that older weight.
senses.whyCN: 假画就是字面意义上被做假的东西，这个词还带着那层旧有的分量。

intro.en: Falsification joins Latin falsus 'false' with facere 'to make'. Both elements are well attested; the only uncertain point is how early the 'forgery' sense appears in English.
intro.cn: falsification 把拉丁语 falsus「假」与 facere「做」合在一起。两个构件都有充分记录，唯一不确定的是「伪造」这一义项在英语中出现得有多早。

items.en: Falsus meant false or deceptive and came from fallere, to deceive, which also stands behind fail, fault and fallacy.
items.cn: falsus 意为虚假的、骗人的，出自 fallere「欺骗」，fail、fault 与 fallacy 也源于此。

items.en: Fallere first described a trick or a slip, and its family spreads across failure, default and fallible.
items.cn: fallere 最初描述欺骗或失足，其词族延伸到 failure、default 与 fallible。

items.en: The second element, to make, turns the adjective into a verb of producing a state: to make false.
items.cn: 第二个构件意为做、造，把形容词变成制造某种状态的动词：使之为假。

items.en: Late Latin falsificare meant to make false or to counterfeit, a word used of coins and documents as well as arguments.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 falsificare 意为使假或伪造，既用于钱币与文件，也用于论证。

items.en: English took the noun in the sixteenth century; the exact date of its first use in the forgery sense is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个名词；它首次用于「伪造」义的确切年代不确定。

items.en: In the 1930s Karl Popper made falsification the test of scientific status, and the word became a term of method.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代，波普尔把证伪立为科学资格的检验，这个词于是成了方法论术语。

note.en: The first group shares the false-making root or only looks close; the second group holds the neighbouring acts that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「使假」词根，或只是字形相近；第二组是常与之混淆的邻近行为。

entries.definition: The verb: to prove false or to make a record false.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：证明为假，或把记录做假。

entries.definition: Able to be shown false, the quality Popper demanded of a theory.
entries.definitionCN: 能被证明为假的，正是波普尔对理论的要求。

entries.definition: The plain adjective of untruth, from the same Latin source.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的「假」的形容词，来自同一拉丁语来源。

entries.definition: A mistaken argument that looks convincing; it shares fallere but not facere.
entries.definitionCN: 看似有理实则错误的论证；共享「欺骗」词根，不含「做」。

entries.definition: Making a process easier; the ending matches but the root means easy.
entries.definitionCN: 使过程更容易；词尾相同，词根却意为容易。

entries.definition: The act of proving an argument or claim wrong by evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证明某一论证或主张有误。

entries.definition: Evidence that a claim is false, the plain noun for a negative result.
entries.definitionCN: 证明主张为假的证据，最朴素的否定结果之名。

entries.definition: A false document, signature or object made to pass as genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 为冒充真品而造的假文件、假签名或假器物。

entries.definition: Inventing data or a story; falsification alters what exists, fabrication creates what does not.
entries.definitionCN: 编造数据或故事；造假改动已有之物，编造则凭空造出。

entries.definition: Publicly exposing a false claim, usually in journalism rather than in method.
entries.definitionCN: 公开揭穿虚假说法，多见于新闻而非方法论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real false-making root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「使假」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Falsus is false and facere is make, so falsification is literally the making false of something.
normal.cn: 前者为假，后者为做，字面就是把某物做成假的。

normal.en: Fallere, to deceive, also gives fail, fault and fallacy, so the whole family smells of a slip.
normal.cn: 表示欺骗的 fallere 还给出 fail、fault 与 fallacy，整个词族都带着失足的气味。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: falsification of data, falsification of records, falsification test.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：数据篡改、伪造记录、证伪检验。

normal.en: In science the word is honourable: a theory earns trust by surviving attempts at falsification.
normal.cn: 在科学里这个词是体面的：理论靠挺过证伪的尝试而赢得信任。

normal.en: In paperwork the same word is a crime: falsification of accounts and of passports.
normal.cn: 在文书里同一个词是罪名：账目作假与伪造护照。

abstract.en: Falsification is the only honest way a theory can be wrong in public.
abstract.cn: 证伪是一个理论能在公开场合出错的唯一体面方式。

abstract.en: A claim that nothing could ever contradict is not strong; it is simply out of reach.
abstract.cn: 任何东西都无法反驳的说法并不强大，只是够不着。

abstract.en: Making a record false is a small war on memory, since the paper was supposed to remember for us.
abstract.cn: 把记录做假，是对记忆发动的一场小战争，因为纸本来该替我们记住。

examples.en: The falsification of the original minutes changed the whole case.
examples.cn: 原始会议记录被篡改，整个案子都变了。

examples.en: Popper treated falsification as the dividing line of science.
examples.cn: 波普尔把证伪当作科学的分界线。

examples.en: A single falsification ended the belief in that remedy.
examples.cn: 一条反证终结了人们对那种疗法的相信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛西菲克申」——把「假」做出来，划掉原字改写：证伪、伪造

root: 晚期拉丁语 falsificare「使假、伪造」← 拉丁语 falsus「假」＋ facere「做」，falsus 出自 fallere「欺骗」，同族有 fail、fault、fallacy、false。十六世纪进入英语；证伪作为科学方法术语由波普尔在二十世纪三十年代确立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from proving a claim false, through a test that could fail, to doctored records, a single counterexample, a forged signature, research misconduct, false accounts, the state of being disproved, and a counterfeit copy.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「证明说法为假」出发，经过可能失败的一次检验，到篡改记录、一条反证、伪造签名、科研造假、账目作假、被推翻的状态，最后是冒充真品的仿件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number on a page crossed out and rewritten, with the old ink still under the new.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上的数字被划掉改写，旧的墨迹还压在新字下面。

branches.en: THE CLAIM BROUGHT DOWN: the act of proving a statement false, and the state it is left in.
branches.cn: 被打翻的主张：证明说法为假的动作，以及它被留下时的状态。

branches.en: THE TEST AND THE INSTANCE: a planned attempt that could fail, and the single case that does the failing.
branches.cn: 检验与实例：一次可能失败的设计，以及真正造成失败的那一个事例。

branches.en: THE DOCTORED PAPER: records and accounts altered so that they misstate the facts.
branches.cn: 被改动的纸面：记录与账目被改动，从而歪曲事实。

branches.en: THE FALSE THING: a forged signature or a copy passed off as the genuine article.
branches.cn: 假东西：伪造的签名，或被当作真品递出的仿件。

branches.en: THE MISCONDUCT: research data invented or manipulated, which the word separates from honest error.
branches.cn: 不端行为：研究数据被编造或操纵，这个词把它与诚实的错误分开。

intro.en: Falsification is built from the Latin words for false and make, and the same endings recur across English.
intro.cn: falsification 由拉丁语「假」与「做」两个词构成，同样的词尾在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin falsus and facere are the sources, with the noun ending through Late Latin -ficatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falsus 与 facere 是来源，名词词尾经由晚期拉丁语的 -ficatio 而来。

items.example: The noun names both the act and the false result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指动作，也指假的结果。

items.example: It is the past participle of the verb to deceive.
items.exampleCN: 它是表示欺骗的动词的过去分词。

items.example: It supplies the -fication ending.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 -fication 词尾。

items.example: It builds amplification, classification and falsification.
items.exampleCN: 它构成放大、分类与证伪等词。

items.example: It builds falsify, verify and simplify.
items.exampleCN: 它构成证伪、核实与简化。

items.example: The adjective keeps the oldest layer of meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留最古老的一层意思。

items.example: The adjective is the key term of Popper's method.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是波普尔方法的关键词。

items.example: The ending marks the person, honest or not.
items.exampleCN: 词尾标出人，无论诚实与否。

items.example: The noun names the property rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指性质而非动作。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin falsificare means to make false or to counterfeit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 falsificare 意为使假、伪造。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective falsus (false), participle of fallere
latinEntries.example: Latin falsus means false, from fallere, to deceive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 falsus 意为假的，出自 fallere（欺骗）。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb facere (fac-, factum; to make)
latinEntries.example: Latin facere supplies the making of the compound.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 facere 提供该复合词中「造」的部分。
